Low compiles to static native binaries with no libc dependency, has a tracing garbage collector and green threads with channels, and adds sum-type enums and typed error returns on top of a Go-sized core. Command Does low run Compiles and runs a file or a module directory. low build Writes a native binary. -o names it and -target picks linux/amd64 or windows/amd64 and defaults to the host. low dev Runs the program and patches changed functions into it on save. Changing main, a type's layout or a function's signature restarts it. Needs a Linux host. low ir Prints the optimised SSA form. low asm Prints the generated assembly. low lint Type-checks the program and prints its warnings. low doc Prints the public API of every module under a directory as JSON. low lsp Starts the language server that the editor extensions use. low version Prints the release, or dev+ and the commit for a build from source. A directory is a module. A low.mod file marks the project root, and import ui/text loads ui/text/ under it. The standard library is imported as std/..., and the editor extensions need low on PATH. Build from source with Go 1.27.3: $ git clone https://github.com/simon-curtis/lowlang $ cd lowlang $ go install ./cmd/low Goals Syntax Builtins Standard library Compiler Hot reload UI Tests Editors Roadmap

Compile speed and binary size comparable to Go. Runtime speed comparable to Go. Exhaustive enums with payloads. Errors as values, propagated with one character, impossible to ignore. A small language: one way to loop, one way to declare, data and functions with no methods or inheritance.
Newlines terminate statements. Blocks are expressions; the last expression is the value.

import std/<name> loads a standard library module. The library is compiled into low , and the project root is not searched for it.

import std/file import std/http import std/http/websocket import std/io import std/net fn handle(req: http.Request) -> http.Response { if req.path == "/chat" { using ws = websocket.accept(req) or return http.response(400, "") let m = websocket.receive(ws) or return http.upgraded() websocket.send_text(ws, str(m.data)) or {} return http.upgraded() } http.response(200, file.read_text("index.html") or "missing") } fn main() ! io.Error { let client = http.client().with_bearer_token("token").with_timeout(5000).build() let page = client.get("https://example.com/") or return using l = net.listen("", 8080)? http.serve(l, handle)? } import std/<name> loads a standard library module. The library is compiled into low, and the project root is not searched for it. Every module except std/math and std/sql/sqlite talks to the kernel through raw syscalls. std/math calls libm and std/sql/sqlite calls libsqlite3 through extern blocks. A library is linked only when reachable code calls it, so a program stays static unless it calls one of their C functions. Every public struct, enum, function, struct field and enum variant carries a doc comment, and TestStdDocumented in internal/compiler fails on any that does not. A doc is written for a caller reading it on hover: The first sentence is the summary: a verb phrase for a function (Returns the ..., Parses ...), a noun phrase for a type, field or variant. Later paragraphs carry the contract the signature cannot: which error variant is returned and when, whether the call blocks, what dropping or closing releases, limits, defaults and edge cases such as empty input or end of input. Identifiers and literals are in backticks. A low example block appears only where usage is not obvious from the signature, and it type-checks. It stays a few lines long; a program that shows how to use the module goes in the module's examples directory, where it runs. A doc states the current behaviour as read from the code. Module Contents std/sys The operating system layer: Linux system calls, and kernel32, ws2_32 and the other Win32 libraries on Windows. It is the only standard library module besides the prelude that calls __syscall, and its Windows files call none. It owns every syscall number, flag, errno and structure layout and exposes typed wrappers that repeat an interrupted call and fail with an io.Error, so callers match io.Error variants. Descriptors: FdHandle, a copyable view whose closing is coordinated by an io.Guard, and the droppable Fd that owns one; read, write, write_all, stream and the _on forms on a view park the green thread while a non-blocking descriptor is not ready; pipe, set_nonblocking, try_read, try_write and wait_input. Files: open with an Open mode, stat, fstat, access, chmod, chown, set_times, unlink, rmdir, mkdir, rename, symlink, link, readlink, statfs, lock, seek, fsync, ftruncate, list_dir and random_bytes. Processes: fork_exec, reap, kill, signal dispositions and handlers, identity, working directory, arguments, environment, executable_path, memory mapping and exit_process. Sockets: socket, socketpair, bind, listen, accept, connect, finish_connect, recv, send, write_view, wait_socket, set_option, get_option, interface_index and multicast membership. Terminals: termios, raw_mode, window size and open_pty. inotify_init, inotify_add and inotify_remove. std/io Error, the error type shared by the I/O, codec and protocol modules. Stream, a copyable struct of read, write and close closures that views a resource. Guard and Lease (guard, enter, retire), the shared state that makes a closed descriptor fail with NotConnected instead of reaching a reused descriptor. A buffered Reader over a stream or, with bytes_reader, over a buffer, with read_line, read_exact, read_up_to, read_some, read_byte, buffered and fill. write_all, read_all, buffer(n), copy, and the fixed-width integer codec in both byte orders: reads (be16, be24, be32, be64 and the le forms as i64, u16_be, u32_be, u64_be and the _le forms as unsigned types, uint_be and uint_le for any width from 1 to 8 bytes as u64, and u16_le_str, u32_le_str and u64_le_str over a str), appends (put_be16 through put_be64, put_le16 through put_le64, and put_be and put_le for any width up to 8 bytes) and in-place stores (set_be16 through set_be64, set_le16 through set_le64). std/file Opening: open, create, append and update return a droppable File whose handle is a copyable FileHandle. On a File: read, write, write_all, seek, sync, truncate, close, info and stat. On a FileHandle: read_on, write_on, write_all_on, close_on and stream_on. Whole files and directories: exists, read_file, read_text, write_file, write_text, remove, remove_dir, rename, mkdir, mkdir_all, list and stream. read_file sizes its buffer from the file's size; a file that reports no size, such as one under /proc, is read into a 64 KB buffer that doubles when full. Permission bits: create_mode, write_file_mode, write_text_mode, mkdir_mode and mkdir_all_mode take them, the other creators use 0o644 for files and 0o755 for directories, all are filtered by the process umask, and chmod is not. Locks: try_lock and unlock are advisory flock locks that report a held lock as false instead of waiting. remove_all removes a tree without following symbolic links. temp_dir creates a private directory under os.temp_dir_path(), which is TMPDIR when set and /tmp otherwise; temp_file and temp_dir_pattern use it when dir is empty and all three draw the random name suffix from getrandom. child_path joins a directory and an entry name. Info also carries regular, link, accessed, uid, gid, device and inode. Further functions: lstat, is_dir, is_file, is_symlink, symlink, link, readlink, realpath, chown, lchown, set_times, disk_usage and read_dir_info. walk is a sorted depth-first walk that uses lstat, never descends into symbolic links and lets its callback return Continue, Skip or Stop. glob matches each segment with path.matches and supports **. copy and copy_dir keep file modes and recreate symbolic links. temp_file(dir, pattern) creates a uniquely named file with O_EXCL and mode 0600 and returns a droppable TempFile that closes and removes it unless keep is called. temp_dir_pattern makes a 0700 directory the same way. std/file/watch inotify. watch and watch_with take paths and Options (recursive, access) and return a droppable Watcher with a copyable WatcherHandle. On a watcher: add, remove, next, events and stop. next parks the green thread until an Event (watched, name, path, kind, dir, cookie) arrives. events is a chan[Event] fed by a forwarding green thread. Kind is Created, Modified, Deleted, MovedFrom, MovedTo, Attrib, Closed, ClosedUnmodified, Opened, Accessed, SelfDeleted, SelfMoved or Overflow. std/net Addresses: IPv4 and IPv6 Addr, parse_ip, format_ip, parse_addr, format, in_network (tests an address against a CIDR prefix) and is_global (false for addresses the IANA special-purpose registries mark as not globally reachable, and for multicast). Types: the droppable Listener, Conn and Socket, each with a copyable ListenerHandle, ConnHandle or SocketHandle in its handle field; adopt and detach convert between a ConnHandle and a Conn, and adopt_socket and detach_socket between a SocketHandle and a Socket. TCP: listen, accept, accept_handle (returns the connection's view for a green thread to adopt), connect, dial and their _within forms with a connect timeout, connect_through (binds the socket to a network interface first), connect_first (tries a list of addresses in order through an optional interface) and interface_index. Connection I/O: read, write, write_all, close, shutdown_write, set_nodelay, read and write timeouts and stream, with read_on, write_on, write_all_on, close_on and stream_on on the view. UDP: bind_udp, send_to, receive_from and close_socket, with send_to_on, receive_from_on and close_socket_on on the view; a SocketHandle has separate fd and out descriptors, so one green thread can wait to receive while another waits to send. lookup tries an IP literal, then /etc/hosts, then A and AAAA queries to each /etc/resolv.conf nameserver. An Addr with an empty ip is a Unix address: listen_unix, connect_unix, connect_unix_within and socketpair return the same Listener and Conn, abstract names start with @ or NUL, and a listener unlinks its pathname when closed. peer_credentials returns the peer's credentials. listen_with and bind_udp_with take ListenOptions (reuse_addr, reuse_port, backlog). Socket options: set_keepalive and set_buffer_sizes. UDP multicast: join_group, leave_group, set_multicast_ttl, set_multicast_loop and set_multicast_interface. Dialer is a function value that makes a connection; direct_dialer is the plain one. std/quic QUIC version 1 (RFC 9000, 9001 and 9002) over UDP. Config holds the tls.Config (ALPN required), idle and handshake timeouts, keep-alive, the flow control and stream limits advertised to the peer, and retry. Server: listen returns a droppable Listener with a copyable ListenerHandle, and accept and accept_handle wait for an established connection; close_listener and close_listener_on. Client: dial, dial_handle, connect and connect_handle complete the handshake before returning. The droppable Connection closes with code 0 when released; its *ConnectionHandle holds the negotiated protocol, the addresses, group, suite, peer_certificates and, once ended, close_code, close_reason, closed_by_peer and application_close. adopt, detach, close_connection, close_on, stats and stats_on (a Stats snapshot), and update_keys and update_keys_on. Streams: open_stream, open_uni_stream, accept_stream and accept_uni_stream with _on forms return a copyable Stream; read, write, finish, reset, stop and stream, which adapts it to an io.Stream. std/quic/wire QUIC encoding with no I/O: a bounds-checked Cursor with varints and packet numbers, parse_header for long and short headers, version_negotiation, packet protection (keys, initial_keys, next_keys, seal, open, peek_key_phase) with header protection, Retry packets and their integrity tag (retry_packet, retry_tag, retry_valid), the frames as one Frame enum (parse_frames, put_frame, frame_size, put_stream_frame, ack_eliciting, ack_delay_ns), transport parameters (encode_parameters, decode_parameters) and the transport error codes. Every parser fails Malformed on hostile input and never panics. std/quic/recovery RFC 9002 loss detection and congestion control with no I/O: recovery makes a Recovery that on_sent, on_ack, on_timeout and discard_space drive per packet number Space. It keeps the RTT estimate, declares packets lost by packet and time thresholds, runs the probe timeout and NewReno with persistent congestion, and answers can_send, deadline and pto_duration. skip records a packet number left unsent, and an ACK covering one fails Malformed. std/socks SOCKS5 (RFC 1928, with RFC 1929 username and password) and SOCKS4a clients: dial, dial4a, tunnel and tunnel4a over an existing connection, and dialer and dialer4a, which return a net.Dialer. The proxy resolves the target name. std/pipe Pipelines. A Pipe owns a Reader and a Writer, each droppable so that releasing it completes it, with copyable ReaderHandle and WriterHandle views for green threads (adopt_reader, adopt_writer and the _on operations). Also segmented buffers, backpressure, Sequence and SequenceReader, and adapters between pipes and streams. std/cancel Token with token, child, cancel, cancelled, check and done (a channel that closes on cancellation, for select). on_cancel returns a droppable Registration that releases its callback; release, on_cancel_handle and release_on work on the copyable RegistrationHandle. pause is a sleep that ends early on cancellation. std/header The header primitives below std/http, std/multipart and std/mail: Header, get, values, has, add, set, remove, token, token_byte, valid_value, valid, quote, and parse_value with param, which resolve RFC 2231 and 5987 parameters. std/http Server types: Request, Response, header helpers over header.Header and parse_url. Request.token is cancelled when the client goes away and when the handler returns. Request.remote is the client's IP address for connections served by serve, serve_tls and serve_conn. Serving: serve, serve_tls, serve_conn and serve_stream, and serve_quic for HTTP/3 over a std/quic listener; the _on forms (serve_on, serve_tls_on, serve_conn_on, serve_quic_on) take the listener's or connection's view. Client: a pooled client configured through client() and with_* builders, per-request builders, send, stream_to and download. with_version(Http3) sends https requests over QUIC. with_interface binds every connection to a network interface. with_resolver substitutes for net.lookup on host names; TLS keeps the host name for SNI and certificate checks. with_cancel makes a request fail with Io(Aborted) once its token is cancelled. URLs: parse_url, resolve and with_query_pair build on std/uri. connect returns a droppable Connection that closes its stream when released; detach hands the stream on. Proxies: with_proxy, with_http_proxy, with_https_proxy, with_no_proxy, with_proxy_from_environment and with_dialer send requests through an http:// proxy (absolute-form for http targets, CONNECT for https targets) or a socks5://, socks5h://, socks4:// or socks4a:// proxy. no_proxy follows Go's matching rules. The one content-coding table gives each coding its encoder and decoder; accepts_coding, negotiate_coding and encode_body read it, and the client's decompression and std/web compression and static files share it. Cookie is the one cookie model: the jar stores it, request_cookies reads the cookie headers into it and set_cookie and format_set_cookie write it, and std/web sessions use it. CookieJar is a shared RFC 6265 jar (cookie_jar, cookie_jar_on for a jar that reads a clock.Clock, with_cookie_jar, jar_set, jar_header, jar_cookies, jar_clear) that enforces the Secure rules and the __Secure- and __Host- prefixes and has no public-suffix check. A Response whose stream is a chan[[]u8] is written as it is produced, chunked on HTTP/1.1 and as DATA frames on HTTP/2, until the handler closes the channel. std/http/websocket accept (the 101 goes through http.upgrade) and dial over ws and wss return a droppable Socket that sends a normal close when released. Operations: receive, send_text, send_binary, ping and close, with _on forms, and adopt and detach on the *SocketHandle. std/http/sse Server-sent events. Shared: Event (id, event, data, retry), format, comment and keepalive. Server: stream, stream_with, serve_events, serve_events_with, Emitter and last_event_id. Client: parser, feed, parse and listen, which reads a text/event-stream response with any chunking and CR, LF or CRLF line ends. std/http/files serve_file and serve_file_with answer a request from a file. Content type comes from the extension, then sniffing. Weak ETag and Last-Modified work with If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since. A single Range is answered as 206 or 416, with If-Range. HEAD is supported and the body is streamed. std/http/huffman The static Huffman code of RFC 7541 appendix B that HPACK and QPACK share: decode, encode and encoded_size. decode fails Malformed on the EOS symbol and on padding that is longer than 7 bits or not all ones, and never panics on any input. std/http/qpack QPACK (RFC 9204) with no I/O. Decoder (decoder takes the maximum table capacity, the blocked stream limit and the field section size limit) keeps the dynamic table: on_encoder_stream consumes encoder stream bytes split anywhere, buffers at most 64 KiB of an incomplete instruction and returns the blocked streams that can now decode; decode returns Decoded, either Fields or Blocked, and queues a Section Acknowledgment; cancel_stream queues a Stream Cancellation; take_decoder_stream returns the queued decoder stream bytes plus one Insert Count Increment. Encoder writes field sections with the static table only, so they never block and nothing goes on the encoder stream; on_decoder_stream accepts Stream Cancellations and fails Malformed on any other instruction. decompression_failed, encoder_stream_error and decoder_stream_error return the HTTP/3 codes 0x200, 0x201 and 0x202 for failures of decode, on_encoder_stream and on_decoder_stream. Every entry point fails Malformed on hostile input: integers are capped at 2^62-1, and strings, indexes, Required Insert Counts, Bases, entry sizes and capacities are checked before use. static_table, insert_count, table_size and table_entries expose the tables. std/web A router with groups, middleware and typed JSON endpoints, problem details (RFC 9457), an OpenAPI 3.1 document built from the types, cookie sessions, CSRF protection, API key, Basic and bearer authentication, CORS and response compression. static and static_with serve a directory. events and event_stream serve server-sent events. std/tls TLS 1.2 and 1.3 clients and servers. client, server and dial return a droppable Session that sends close_notify and closes the stream beneath it when released. Its handle is the shared *SessionHandle holding protocol, version, group, suite, cipher_suite and peer_certificates. client_handle and server_handle return the view alone, and read_on, write_on, close_on and stream_on operate on it. quic_client and quic_server run the TLS 1.3 handshake of RFC 9001 through a QuicTransport of callbacks that send and receive handshake bytes per Level and install each QuicSecret, and return a QuicResult. suite_hash, key_size, cipher and expand_label derive keys for a Suite. std/serde The Writer and Reader protocols, write[T], read[T] and schema[T] (which the compiler derives for every type), and Field[T, F]. Readers share parse_integer, parse_unsigned and syntax_at, which builds the Syntax error for a line and column; the helpers the derived code calls are private. Tree, Node and Member are the value shape that CBOR, MessagePack, TOML, YAML and template data share: to_tree builds one from any value, tree_reader reads a T from one, and key_text and unsigned_tree hold the key text and the u64 range rule. A format maps its own value type V to a tree with node_of and a Shape[V] function, and back with value_of and a Rebuild[V]. std/json A reader and writer over UTF-8 bytes, the Value document model with member builders (text_member, int_member, bool_member, base64url_member, object_member, array_member) and typed getters (field, field_text, field_int, text_of, int_of), equal (compares numbers numerically and objects without regard to member order), and serialize[T] and deserialize[T] with naming policies. std/json/pointer RFC 6901 pointers: escape, unescape, parse, format, get, has, set, add, replace, remove and relative pointers. Edits return a new document. std/json/patch RFC 6902 apply (atomic, failing with the operation's index) and diff; RFC 7396 merge_patch and merge_diff. std/json/path RFC 9535 JSONPath: compile, query, find, values and paths, with slices, filters, match, search, length, count and value, normalised paths, and syntax errors at a byte offset. std/json/schema JSON Schema 2020-12. compile and compile_with check the schema, resolve $ref, $anchor, $dynamicRef and registered resources, and precompile patterns. validate returns Violations with the instance pointer, the keyword pointer and a message. unevaluatedProperties and unevaluatedItems use annotations from the branches that passed. format annotates or asserts. std/cbor CBOR (RFC 8949): the Value model, a decoder with depth and length limits, a deterministic encoder, diagnostic notation, and serialize[T] and deserialize[T]. std/webauthn A WebAuthn relying party: registration and authentication options as JSON, registration and authentication verification for ES256, EdDSA and RS256 credentials, and COSE key parsing. std/sql The driver contract: Connection, the droppable owner that closes the driver connection when released; ConnectionHandle, the copyable view of closures that std/orm and std/sql/pool use, held in the owner's public handle field (adopt makes an owner from one); Value, Rows, Error, Options and Dialect. A Dialect is a record that owns everything that differs between databases: the OpenTelemetry system name, default port, placeholder prefix, identifier quotes, generated-key and paging syntax, column types, the conditional CREATE TABLE, the session lock statements and the write-transaction statement. postgres(), sqlserver() and sqlite() build the three; std/orm and std/sql/migrate read the one a connection carries. rolled_back rolls a transaction back after an error and reports the rollback's own error when it fails. std/sql/driver What the drivers share. A Session holds the busy and closed state. Every operation of a connection runs as a call on the session, which fails with Busy or Closed and abandons the connection on an error the driver calls fatal. establish runs the login under it, collect, ignore_columns and ignore_row are the row callbacks, dial opens the socket at the dialect's default port, and traced wraps a handle with otel.instrument_sql. connection guards, traces and adopts a driver's handle, so std/sql/postgres, std/sql/sqlserver and std/sql/sqlite do not import std/otel. std/sql/postgres A PostgreSQL driver over protocol 3.0, plain or over TLS. std/sql/sqlserver A Microsoft SQL Server driver over TDS 7.4, plain or over TLS. std/sql/sqlite SQLite through libsqlite3, linked only when a program calls it. open and open_with (read-only, create, busy timeout). exec runs scripts. query, each and execute take ? or ?N parameters over cached prepared statements. Also last_insert_id, begin, begin_immediate, commit and rollback, and backup to a file through the online backup API. close and close_on are idempotent; a closed Database fails with sql.Error.Closed. connection and connect present a database as an sql.Connection: the one connection returns leaves closing to the Database, the one connect returns closes it. Calls block their OS thread. std/sql/pool A pool of connections made by an opener. open takes a Config (max, max_idle, idle_timeout, max_lifetime, wait_timeout, ping_after, ping, clock). acquire and acquire_until (with a cancel token) park in first-in first-out order while every connection is in use. A droppable Lease returns its connection on release. Also with, discard, prune, stats and shutdown. std/sql/migrate Ordered migrations recorded in a schema_migrations table with a SHA-256 checksum: plan, with_table, status, up, up_to and down, each migration in its own transaction under a lock. from_text and load_dir read -- +up and -- +down files named NNN_name.sql. std/toml TOML 1.0.0: a table tree, an encoder, and serde binding. std/yaml YAML 1.2.2: events, a node tree, an encoder, and serde binding. std/otel OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs with W3C propagation, OTLP/HTTP protobuf and JSON, OTLP/gRPC and console exporters, and the instrumentation used by std/http, std/web, std/sql/driver and std/orm. std/protobuf The protobuf wire format: an encoder with nested messages and packed fields, and a field decoder. std/xml XML 1.0 with namespaces: a pull reader, a tree, a writer, and serde binding. std/orm Typed queries over field references, row mapping, inserts, updates and deletes, tables created from types, and raw queries mapped onto structs, over an sql.ConnectionHandle. std/compress/deflate DEFLATE, zlib and gzip. std/compress/xz xz with LZMA2, and .lzma. std/compress/zstd Zstandard (RFC 8878). std/compress/lz4 LZ4 frames. std/compress/brotli Brotli (RFC 7932). std/compress/bzip2 compress(data, level), decompress(data, limit), a streaming decode and an Encoder. The decoder reads multiple streams and blocks and checks both CRCs. Randomised blocks fail with Unsupported. std/compress/snappy Raw blocks (compress_block, decompress_block, decoded_length) and the framing format with masked CRC-32C (compress, decompress, decode, Encoder). std/compress/codec The parts the compressors share: a growable Buffer that packs bits, a BitReader, two-level Huffman decode Tables, a length-limited Huffman Builder, hash-chain Chain and walk, a shared LZ77 History window (history, append, index_to, extend_back), the one-shot decompress scaffold with output_for, deliver and each_chunk, the streaming Encoder shell (encoder, encode, flush, finish), copy_match, and LEB128 varints. std/hash One-shot and incremental forms of CRC-32, CRC-32C, Adler-32, CRC-64 and xxHash32/64. Also FNV-1 and FNV-1a in 32 and 64 bits; SipHash-2-4 and SipHash-1-3 with a 16-byte key in 64- and 128-bit forms; MurmurHash3 (murmur3_32, murmur3_128); wyhash final 4.2; jump consistent hashing; and rendezvous hashing. std/bits Word operations (popcount, trailing_zeros on the processor bit scan, leading_zeros, bit_length, select_in_word and the 32 and 64-bit rotations rotl32, rotr32, rotl64 and rotr64) and dense bitsets. std/hash, std/rand, std/text, the JSON, XML and YAML readers and the compressors use these for rotations, bit counts and bit lengths. std/bits/roaring Roaring bitmaps with the portable serialization format. std/image Bitmaps, pixel operations and resizing, with PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, QOI and lossless WebP codecs. std/crypto random, which reads getrandom and panics when the generator fails. std/crypto/limb Fixed-width limb arithmetic the big-integer code shares: carry and borrow out of a 64-bit step, add, sub and add_masked over limb slices, from_bytes and to_bytes between big-endian bytes and limbs, and the constant-time same, mask_of, blend, choose, gather, equal and is_zero. std/crypto/ecdsa, std/crypto/rsa and std/crypto/ed25519 build on it. std/crypto/hash Algorithm and cloneable Digest, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512, HMAC (hmac, and hmac_keyed for the keyed inner and outer digests that PBKDF2 clones), HKDF and constant-time equal. std/crypto/sha3 SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, SHAKE128 and SHAKE256. std/crypto/aead Aead values for AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and XChaCha20-Poly1305 (xchacha20_poly1305, 24-byte nonce). The AES block functions for 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys (aes_key, encrypt_block_into, decrypt_block, decrypt_block_into). The ChaCha20 functions chacha20_xor (takes the RFC 8439 block counter) and hchacha20. std/crypto/md5 MD5 as a hash.Algorithm, so HMAC, HKDF and PBKDF2 work over it, and sum. For interop and checksums, not security. std/crypto/cipher AES in CBC, raw (cbc_encrypt, cbc_decrypt) or with PKCS#7 padding (cbc_seal, cbc_open, pkcs7_pad, pkcs7_unpad); in CTR with a 128-bit big-endian counter (ctr); and in XTS with ciphertext stealing (xts, xts_encrypt, xts_decrypt). There is no ECB, and CBC provides no integrity: use an Aead. std/crypto/x25519, std/crypto/ed25519 X25519 key agreement (RFC 7748) and Ed25519 signatures (RFC 8032), over std/crypto/curve25519, which also owns the scalar clamp. std/crypto/ecdsa ECDH and ECDSA on P-256 and P-384, with RFC 6979 nonces and SEC1 private keys. The compiler is written in Go. Pipeline:

The compiler is written in Go. Pipeline: Stage Package Output Lex internal/lexer tokens Parse internal/parser internal/ast tree Check internal/check types attached to the tree Build IR internal/ir SSA form, one value per machine word Codegen internal/amd64 x86-64 GNU assembly Assemble internal/asm object: sections, symbols and fixups Link internal/link ELF or PE executable Building a program and running low dev need no external tool. low builds and runs on Linux and on Windows. The default target is the host; -target linux/amd64 or -target windows/amd64 selects one. Every target is assembled and linked in process. On the Windows target, std/sys is built from its _windows.low files, which call kernel32, ws2_32, iphlpapi, shell32 and crypt32, so files, processes, sockets, DNS, terminals, the environment and the system root certificates work there. __syscall itself compiles to a call that panics with system calls are not available on windows. A descriptor is a handle. Descriptors 0 to 2 name the standard handles. A socket's descriptor packs the socket in its low 32 bits and a manual-reset event in its high 32 bits. Sockets are overlapped and non-blocking. wait_socket issues an overlapped IOCTL_AFD_POLL request for the socket's read or write conditions with the descriptor's event, and parks on the event until the request completes, which is at once when the socket is already ready. write_view duplicates the socket with WSADuplicateSocketW and gives the copy its own event, so a reader and a writer of one connection wait on separate requests and events. shutdown cancels the socket's pending requests with CancelIoEx, which wakes the waiters on every descriptor of the socket. Closing the descriptor reads and discards unread input first, because Windows answers a close with unread input by a reset that discards data the peer has not yet read, then closes both. Only sockets are non-blocking. A read from a pipe or file holds an OS thread until it returns; wait_input parks on a console handle until it is signalled and otherwise sleeps a millisecond between tries. process.start calls CreateProcessW with the command line quoted for the Microsoft C runtime, a UTF-16 environment block, and inheritable copies of the child's three streams passed through PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST, so the child inherits nothing else. The process handle stands in for the pidfd, wait waits on it and reads GetExitCodeProcess, and kill calls TerminateProcess. process.find splits PATH on ; and tries each PATHEXT extension. Environment names compare without ASCII case. os.home_dir, cache_dir, config_dir, data_dir, state_dir and temp_dir read USERPROFILE, LOCALAPPDATA, APPDATA, TMP and TEMP. net.lookup reads the hosts file under the system directory and asks the adapters' IPv4 DNS servers from GetNetworkParams. x509.system_roots reads the ROOT certificate store. A refused connection to a loopback address fails at once rather than after the SYN retransmissions Windows would otherwise make. Signals, inotify watches, pseudo-terminals, setting a terminal's size, chown, peer credentials, binding to a device and SO_REUSEPORT fail with Unsupported. User and group IDs are -1 and the umask is 0. Returning from a C call can wait out a collection; the wait keeps the thread's last-error value, so GetLastError after an extern call reads that call's error. The low command lives in cmd/low. compiler.Analyse takes a profile and compiler.Build is the one build entry: it generates the assembly for the unit, assembles it with the unit's embedded files, links it with the linker its target uses and writes the executable. low build, low run, hot reload, the fuzz oracle and the Vulkan and Wayland generator tests all call it. Only the Dev profile produces a hot-reloadable build. low ir prints the SSA form and low asm the generated assembly. Compilation is deterministic: the same source and target always produce the same SSA form, assembly and binary. No pass depends on map iteration order; where order matters the compiler walks slices or stacks. parser.ParseSource is the one entry from source text to tree, for user files, the prelude, the standard library and generated code. The lexer lexes each interpolated {} expression into tokens when it lexes the string, and keeps the ,width:format suffix as text that ast.ParseSpec parses. A lexer, parser or checker error is a *diag.Error holding the position of the fault; low lsp reads it with errors.As. types.Universe interns the pointer, slice, optional, raw pointer, channel, map, result and function types, and owns the built-in type names and the constraint names. check.Check creates it with the checker's callback for new types and returns it. The checker lays out and instantiates types in three phases: declaring, laid out, and functions ready. Modules: internal/compiler finds the root, loads the entry module, then loads each imported directory once, breadth first, and rejects import cycles. One loader reads the program, its imports, embed files and the embedded standard library through fs.FS. compiler.Overlay puts unsaved editor text over the disk for the language server, which shares the loader's Root lookup and ParseFile. internal/check does no file IO. Every file records its module path and every source position its file, so errors name the file they come from. The checker keeps a scope of types and functions per module. The prelude belongs to the entry module, and its __ names cannot clash with anything else. Every module sees the prelude's generic __ functions and types, so std/container/deque is a wrapper over the prelude's __Queue, the ring buffer behind channel wait queues. A function in module ui/text becomes the symbol fn_ui.text.shout. Types display with their module path, such as geometry.Circle. The runtime is runtime.asm, sched.asm and gc.asm, which are shared by every target, plus linux.asm or windows.asm for the target OS. It is emitted with every program. A Linux program talks to the kernel through raw syscalls and ends the process with exit_group, so every thread stops; a dynamically linked Linux program ends with exit. A Windows program calls kernel32 through the WIN macro and ends with ExitProcess. The runtime's data layout, thread-local access and Windows stack-bounds switching are defined once, in layout.asm and the target's linux_header.asm or windows_header.asm, as constants and macros such as G_SCANLO, TLS_GET, TEB_ENTER_OS and MSG_BEGIN. Generated code and patches use those names and macros, and Generate and GeneratePatch both prepend the headers. Go passes RT_DYNAMIC and the hot-reload constants (HOT_BASE, HOT_SIZE, PATCH_BYTES, PATCH_ENTRY, PATCH_SIGNAL) to the assembly as .set lines, and defines HOT_INIT as the call to rt_hot_init in a hot build and as nothing otherwise. The Windows import table lists every function the Windows runtime calls through WIN, taken from windows.asm, plus the program's extern imports. The contracts between the stages have one owner each: internal/builtin numbers every builtin. The checker records the number on each call and internal/ir lowers it through a table indexed by that number. internal/ir/runtime.go lists every runtime routine generated code calls through a runtime instruction: its symbol, its register convention (plain, growth or string equality) and whether it returns a scalar or nothing. A system call is its own syscall instruction. internal/prelude names every prelude function the compiler calls or the checker's generated source calls, the fields internal/ir reads from the struct a function returns (__waiter and __chan_new), and which functions a map or channel type instantiates. The prelude is validated when it loads, so a missing or reshaped entry is an error that names it. internal/ir reads field offsets from the checked types. internal/amd64 owns the target. A Platform value, sysv for Linux and win64 for Windows, supplies the runtime and header text, the C argument classification, the registers a C callback saves, the entry symbol, how a system call is made, stack probing and the dynamic-library shims. PROGRAM_ENTRY and PROGRAM_EXIT in each header are the program's entry and exit. amd64 exports the entry symbols, the hot-patch list and count symbols and the .idata section names that internal/link and internal/hot read. One convention value in internal/amd64 holds the Low register convention: argument, result, caller-saved, callee-saved, system call and growth registers, and the frame offsets derived from them.

low dev app.low or low dev app/ needs a Linux host. It builds a dev binary, runs it, and watches every source file of every loaded module, every embedded file, and the file lists of their directories.

low dev app.low or low dev app/ needs a Linux host. It builds a dev binary, runs it, and watches every source file of every loaded module, every embedded file, and the file lists of their directories. On save: A file that fails to compile is reported and the running program is left alone. The program restarts when any of these changes: the set of linked libraries; the set of called C functions; a struct or enum layout; an existing function's signature; a closure's captured variables; main. A running frame of old code may still call any function, so it must keep the old calling convention and data layout. main never returns to pick up new code. Otherwise every function whose generated assembly differs from the running version is recompiled, including callers whose code changed only because a callee did, every instance of an edited generic function, and new functions. Heap, stack and all live values are kept. Mechanism: Dev builds call every function through fn_table, a writable table of 4096 code addresses, with call [rip+fn_table+8*i]. Release builds call directly. In dev builds a function value's code word is the address of its fn_table entry and calls through it use call [r10], so a stored function value or closure runs the newest code. Callback thunks call through the table too. internal/amd64 owns this protocol: Generate with a FuncTable and GeneratePatch, the fn_table size, the patch signal and entry size, the mailbox symbol names and the region's base and size. At start the dev runtime installs a SIGUSR1 handler and maps a 64 MB read-execute region at 0x40000000, close enough to the binary for 32-bit relative references. A patch is assembled and linked in process, by Built.Patch, at the next free address in that region, resolving its references against the symbols of the running binary that the linker returned with its image. It holds only the changed functions and their strings. Patched functions get a fresh symbol suffix so they never collide with the originals. low dev writes the machine code into the region through /proc/<pid>/mem, writes (index, address) pairs and a count into a mailbox in the program, and sends SIGUSR1. The handler stores each address into fn_table with an aligned 8-byte write and clears the count, which low dev waits for. Frames already running keep executing their old code; the next call through the table enters the new code. Old code is never unmapped.

Zed and Neovim highlight with the tree-sitter-low grammar; VS Code uses the TextMate grammar in vscode/syntaxes. All three start low lsp: diagnostics, hover, go-to-definition, references, rename, document and workspace symbols, completion, signature help, inlay hints for inferred types, and code actions on ?. Rename and inlay hints answer only when the program compiles. At a ?, the code actions offer Catch the error, which rewrites it as catch { e => ... }, and Ignore the error with or, which rewrites it as or ...; in an editor that accepts snippet edits (Zed, VS Code), each leaves the cursor where the handler goes. When the check fails because the enclosing function declares no error type, they also offer Add ! E to f, which declares the operand's error type on that function and imports its module if needed. go test ./editors/ compares each list with the lexer and the checker and fails when one lacks or adds a name. The tree-sitter grammar and highlight query list keywords, contextual keywords, builtin functions, types and constants. The library lays the tree out with std/ui/layout, paints it into a scene.Scene and draws the scene with gpu.present. Hitboxes, mouse dispatch, focus and tab stops from #35 are built here; #35 keeps actions and keymaps. low import std/ui fn counter(count: ui.Signal[i64]) -> ui.Element { ui.div().column().padding(16.0).gap(8.0).background(ui.rgb(0x202124)).children() { ui.text("Clicked {count.get()} times").text_color(ui.rgb(0xe8eaed)), ui.div().padding(8.0).rounded(6.0).background(ui.rgb(0x1a73e8)) .hover(fn(v: ui.Visual) -> ui.Visual { v.with_background(ui.rgb(0x4285f4)) }) .on_click(fn() { count.set(count.get() + 1) }) .child(ui.text("Increment")) } } fn main() ! ui.Error { using app = ui.open(ui.Options { title: "Counter", width: 320, height: 200 })? let count = app.signal(0) app.run(fn() -> ui.Element { counter(count) })? } Module: std/ui holds App, the frame loop, Element and its builders, Signal[T], hit testing, focus and event dispatch, plus ui.rgb and the other colour helpers and ui.Error. ## Elements - An Element is a struct with a layout.Style, a Visual (background, border colour, corner radii, shadow, text colour and text size), its text when it is a text leaf, its children, an optional id, and optional handlers: on_click: fn(), on_key: fn(platform.KeyEvent) -> bool and hover: fn(Visual) -> Visual. - div() and text(s) make elements, and builder functions return a changed copy: row, column, gap, padding, size, width, height, grow, items_center, justify_center, justify_between, background, border, rounded, shadow, text_color, text_size, clip, id, focusable, on_click, on_key, hover, child and children. children() takes a trailing block. - A text element is a layout leaf whose measure function wraps its text with text.wrap to the width it is given. - The layout.Tree is built for every frame and laid out in full. ## App and state - ui.open(Options) -> App ! Error opens the window with platform.open and the GPU with gpu.open_for. App is droppable and releases the Gpu before the Window. app.run(view) loops until the window is closed: wait for events with platform.next, dispatch them, and when a frame is due call view, lay out, paint and present. - Signal[T] is a shared cell owned by the App. get reads it, and set and update change it and request a frame. Signals belong to the green thread that runs the app; another green thread changes state by sending a closure through app.handle().post(f), which runs it on the app's green thread before the next frame and wakes the loop through the window's Waker. - App separates the loop from the window: frame(app, size, scale) -> Scene and dispatch(app, event) run the same code without a window or a GPU. ## Painting, hit testing and focus - Painting walks the tree in order: an element's shadow, its background and border as one quad, its text as sprites, then its children inside its clip when it clips. Each element with a handler or focusable records a hitbox of its rectangle within the clip, and its parent's hitbox index for bubbling. - After layout, the topmost hitbox under the pointer is hovered, and every element whose hitbox contains the pointer applies its hover to its Visual before painting. A change in the hovered hitbox requests a frame. - A press and release on the same element run the nearest on_click from it outward. Keys go to the focused element and bubble outward until an on_key returns true. Clicking a focusable element focuses it; Tab and Shift+Tab move focus through focusable elements in tree order. Focus is kept by id across frames. ## Tests - testdata/run/ui_* programs check hover, click, key and focus dispatch through frame and dispatch, with no library, so they also run on Windows through TestRunWindows. - internal/uitest renders a laid-out element tree offscreen and compares pixels; it skips without libvulkan or a Vulkan 1.3 device. - The example above moves into docs/design.md ## UI once it compiles, so the site build checks it. std/ui example program for Linux and Windows - A runnable example under testdata (not bench/) that opens a window with ui.open and runs a small interactive UI: text, a hoverable and clickable button, a focusable element that takes keys, and state kept in signals. - It builds for Linux and Windows. The filesystem layer shared by std/archive/tar, std/archive/cpio and std/archive/zip, built on std/file and std/sys. Names are cleaned and rejected when absolute, containing .. or NUL, or passing through a symbolic link below the destination. Files are created exclusively without following links. The extractors share its Stamp and apply_stamps for directory times, write_from for file bodies and walk for the sorted tree walk of create, and the tar and cpio readers share its Input, which counts every byte against the total limit.

newc, CRC and odc archives, detected per entry on read: a Reader, a Writer (add_file, add_dir, add_symlink, add_links, finish), and extract and create over the filesystem with the safe extraction of std/archive. Hard links store their data with the last link in newc and CRC. The binary format fails with Unsupported.

ustar, GNU and pax archives. A streaming Reader (next, read_body, read_entry, list) with limits on header, entry and total size. A Writer (add_file, add_dir, add_symlink, add_hardlink, finish) that uses pax records for long or non-ASCII names. gzip through read_gzip and write_gzip. extract, extract_gzip, create and create_gzip over the filesystem strip setuid, setgid and sticky bits.

Zip archives read through the central directory, with zip64, stored and deflate entries, CRC-32 checks and limits on entries, sizes and compression ratio. Written with add_file, add_dir, add_symlink and finish, which emits zip64 records when a count or size needs them. extract works over the filesystem. Encrypted entries and other methods fail with Unsupported.
encode, encode_adobe (with <~ ~>), decode, and Z85 (encode_z85, decode_z85).

Int, Bool and Flag built on compare-and-swap, with load_int, store_int, add_int, swap_int, compare_and_swap_int and update_int, and the same forms for Bool. Every load is a locked operation, so a loop cannot hoist it. Value[T] swaps a heap pointer under a lock: load_value, store_value, swap_value, update_value, snapshot_value and compare_and_swap_value (compares pointer identity).

RFC 4648 base32 with the standard and extended-hex alphabets: encode, encode_unpadded, decode (case-insensitive, padding optional, failing at the first bad character or on an impossible length), encode_hex and decode_hex.
The Bitcoin alphabet (encode, decode), the Flickr alphabet (encode_flickr, decode_flickr) and Base58Check (encode_check, decode_check), failing at the first bad character.

One encoder, encode_with(data, alphabet, padded), and one decoder, decode_with(s, alphabet, padding), over an alphabet (standard, url_safe) and a Padding rule (Required, Forbidden, Optional). encode, encode_unpadded and encode_url, and decode, decode_unpadded and decode_url, fix the alphabet and padding. Every decoder rejects non-zero trailing bits and a byte outside the alphabet.

Int over 32-bit limbs. Parsing and printing in bases 2 to 36 (printing divides the limbs, packed into 64-bit words, by the largest power of the base below 2^64 with a precomputed reciprocal). add, sub, mul (Karatsuba), divmod, divmod_floor, divmod_euclid, pow, modpow (Montgomery for odd moduli), mod_inverse, gcd, lcm, isqrt. Shifts and bitwise operators with two's complement semantics. is_probable_prime, next_prime, random_below, to_f64, from_bytes and to_bytes. Division by zero is an error. Not constant time.
A coefficient and an i32 exponent: exact add, sub and mul, and div and rescale with HalfEven, HalfUp, Down, Up, Floor or Ceiling rounding to a target exponent.
Normalised rationals over big.Int: ratio, parse (a/b, decimals, exponents), the four operations, inv, cmp, to_fixed, to_f64.

Word operations (popcount, trailing_zeros on the processor bit scan, leading_zeros, bit_length, select_in_word and the 32 and 64-bit rotations rotl32, rotr32, rotl64 and rotr64) and dense bitsets. std/hash, std/rand, std/text, the JSON, XML and YAML readers and the compressors use these for rotations, bit counts and bit lengths.
Roaring bitmaps with the portable serialization format.
BSON documents as []Field with ObjectId, datetime, binary, regex, int32, int64, double and Decimal128 (as bytes): decode, encode, get, diagnostic, new_object_id and parse_object_id.

A Builder over a growing byte buffer, appended in place through mut: write, write_bytes, write_byte, write_char, write_i64, write_f64, write_line, write_repeat, write_join, len, capacity, reserve, truncate, reset, to_str and to_bytes.

Token with token, child, cancel, cancelled, check and done (a channel that closes on cancellation, for select). on_cancel returns a droppable Registration that releases its callback; release, on_cancel_handle and release_on work on the copyable RegistrationHandle. pause is a sleep that ends early on cancellation.
CBOR (RFC 8949): the Value model, a decoder with depth and length limits, a deterministic encoder, diagnostic notation, and serialize[T] and deserialize[T].

The Chrome DevTools Protocol. launch starts a headless Chromium with a disposable profile, connects to it and returns a droppable Browser that shuts it down when released. Its handle is the shared *BrowserHandle; launch_handle, adopt, shutdown_on and open_page_on take it. call sends a command to the browser or a session, and each subscribe gets every other message as events. open_page opens a page in its own browser context, which close_page disposes, and every request of the page, including those of cross-site frames and workers, passes through Handlers. Also navigate and shutdown.

decode, decode_lossy, encode, encode_replace, canonical (WHATWG labels) and detect_bom for UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-32, ISO-8859-1, -2 and -15, windows-1250, -1251 and -1252, KOI8-R, IBM437 and IBM850, and windows_1252 for the code point of one windows-1252 byte. The CJK encodings are not provided.
compress(data, level), decompress(data, limit), a streaming decode and an Encoder. The decoder reads multiple streams and blocks and checks both CRCs. Randomised blocks fail with Unsupported.

The parts the compressors share: a growable Buffer that packs bits, a BitReader, two-level Huffman decode Tables, a length-limited Huffman Builder, hash-chain Chain and walk, a shared LZ77 History window (history, append, index_to, extend_back), the one-shot decompress scaffold with output_for, deliver and each_chunk, the streaming Encoder shell (encoder, encode, flush, finish), copy_match, and LEB128 varints.
Raw blocks (compress_block, decompress_block, decoded_length) and the framing format with masked CRC-32C (compress, decompress, decode, Encoder).
A ring-buffer Deque[T]: push_front, push_back, pop_front, pop_back, front, back, at and size, doubling when full.
A binary Heap[T] ordered by a less function: insert, pop, peek and size.

A least-recently-used Cache[K, V] of fixed capacity: get (refreshes the entry), put (returns the evicted key), contains, size and keys from most to least recent. All run in constant time over index-linked entries.

An AVL Tree[K, V] for ordered keys: tree, put, get, remove, contains, size, height, is_valid, first, last, floor_entry, ceiling_entry, each, each_range, keys, values, entries and the half-open range(lo, hi).
Set[T] over a map, in insertion order: set, from_slice, add and remove (both return whether the set changed), has, size, items, union, intersection, difference and is_subset.
Sorted[T], an ordered set over ordered.Tree: sorted, from_slice, add, remove, has, size, items, first, last, floor_item, ceiling_item and range.
random, which reads getrandom and panics when the generator fails.

Aead values for AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and XChaCha20-Poly1305 (xchacha20_poly1305, 24-byte nonce). The AES block functions for 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys (aes_key, encrypt_block_into, decrypt_block, decrypt_block_into). The ChaCha20 functions chacha20_xor (takes the RFC 8439 block counter) and hchacha20.
BLAKE3: sum, xof, keyed_hash, derive_key, an incremental Hasher with finalize and seekable finalize_at, and algorithm(), a hash.Algorithm for HMAC.

AES in CBC, raw (cbc_encrypt, cbc_decrypt) or with PKCS#7 padding (cbc_seal, cbc_open, pkcs7_pad, pkcs7_unpad); in CTR with a 128-bit big-endian counter (ctr); and in XTS with ciphertext stealing (xts, xts_encrypt, xts_decrypt). There is no ECB, and CBC provides no integrity: use an Aead.

A DER cursor and the ASN.1 values the other crypto modules share. Reading: reader, read, peek, done, expect, enter, finish, whole, with unsigned, small_int, boolean, bits, named_bits, oid and time for the primitive types; it rejects indefinite and non-minimal lengths. Writing: encode, integer and sequence; trim_zeros drops the leading zero bytes of a big-endian magnitude. prime256v1 and secp384r1 return the named-curve OIDs that std/crypto/ecdsa and std/crypto/x509 share. std/crypto/x509, std/crypto/rsa and std/crypto/ecdsa build on it.

ECDH and ECDSA on P-256 and P-384, with RFC 6979 nonces and SEC1 private keys. It owns the curve sizes (scalar_size), the named-curve lookup (curve_by_oid) and the uncompressed point encoding (uncompressed, coordinates) that std/crypto/x509, std/crypto/jose and std/webauthn use.
Algorithm and cloneable Digest, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512, HMAC (hmac, and hmac_keyed for the keyed inner and outer digests that PBKDF2 clones), HKDF and constant-time equal.

JSON Web Tokens: compact JWS with HS256/384/512, RS256/384/512, PS256/384/512, ES256, ES384 and EdDSA, JWK sets, and claim checks. asymmetric_algorithms lists the public key algorithms and token_kid reads the key id from a token header.

Fixed-width limb arithmetic the big-integer code shares: carry and borrow out of a 64-bit step, add, sub and add_masked over limb slices, from_bytes and to_bytes between big-endian bytes and limbs, and the constant-time same, mask_of, blend, choose, gather, equal and is_zero. std/crypto/ecdsa, std/crypto/rsa and std/crypto/ed25519 build on it.
MD5 as a hash.Algorithm, so HMAC, HKDF and PBKDF2 work over it, and sum. For interop and checksums, not security.
HOTP (RFC 4226) and TOTP (RFC 6238) over SHA-1, SHA-256 and SHA-512: hotp, totp, verify_totp with a window, verify_hotp, generate_secret, base32 secrets, and otpauth:// uri and parse_uri.

Password hashes in PHC strings: Argon2id, scrypt (RFC 7914, with a memory limit checked before allocating) and PBKDF2. bcrypt ($2b$; passwords over 72 bytes are rejected). verify handles all of them and $2a$ and $2y$ bcrypt strings. BLAKE2b.
RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS signing and verification, and PKCS#1 keys. integer strips the leading zeros that key integers from JWK and COSE carry.
SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, SHAKE128 and SHAKE256.

PEM (pem_blocks, pem_certificates, pem_private_key), certificates, PKCS#8 private keys, the system roots, chain validation and the TLS signature scheme table (signature_schemes, signing_schemes, authentication, verify_signature, sign).

RFC 4180 records with quoted fields, doubled quotes, embedded newlines and CRLF or LF line ends. parse and parse_with a separator fail with the line of an unterminated or bare quote. format, format_with and append_record quote only fields that need it.

.env files. parse and read return a map from NAME=value lines. They allow export, blank lines, # comments (inline after whitespace in unquoted values), single quotes taken literally, and double quotes with \n, \t and \r escapes that may span lines. Errors carry the line.

Opening: open, create, append and update return a droppable File whose handle is a copyable FileHandle. On a File: read, write, write_all, seek, sync, truncate, close, info and stat. On a FileHandle: read_on, write_on, write_all_on, close_on and stream_on. Whole files and directories: exists, read_file, read_text, write_file, write_text, remove, remove_dir, rename, mkdir, mkdir_all, list and stream. read_file sizes its buffer from the file's size; a file that reports no size, such as one under /proc, is read into a 64 KB buffer that doubles when full. Permission bits: create_mode, write_file_mode, write_text_mode, mkdir_mode and mkdir_all_mode take them, the other creators use 0o644 for files and 0o755 for directories, all are filtered by the process umask, and chmod is not. Locks: try_lock and unlock are advisory flock locks that report a held lock as false instead of waiting. remove_all removes a tree without following symbolic links. temp_dir creates a private directory under os.temp_dir_path(), which is TMPDIR when set and /tmp otherwise; temp_file and temp_dir_pattern use it when dir is empty and all three draw the random name suffix from getrandom. child_path joins a directory and an entry name. Info also carries regular, link, accessed, uid, gid, device and inode. Further functions: lstat, is_dir, is_file, is_symlink, symlink, link, readlink, realpath, chown, lchown, set_times, disk_usage and read_dir_info. walk is a sorted depth-first walk that uses lstat, never descends into symbolic links and lets its callback return Continue, Skip or Stop. glob matches each segment with path.matches and supports **. copy and copy_dir keep file modes and recreate symbolic links. temp_file(dir, pattern) creates a uniquely named file with O_EXCL and mode 0600 and returns a droppable TempFile that closes and removes it unless keep is called. temp_dir_pattern makes a 0700 directory the same way.

inotify. watch and watch_with take paths and Options (recursive, access) and return a droppable Watcher with a copyable WatcherHandle. On a watcher: add, remove, next, events and stop. next parks the green thread until an Event (watched, name, path, kind, dir, cookie) arrives. events is a chan[Event] fed by a forwarding green thread. Kind is Created, Modified, Deleted, MovedFrom, MovedTo, Attrib, Closed, ClosedUnmodified, Opened, Accessed, SelfDeleted, SelfMoved or Overflow.
Command-line flags from Specs with help text, booleans and defaults: --name value, --name=value, single-dash forms and --. get, enabled, number, the remaining arguments, and usage.

One-shot and incremental forms of CRC-32, CRC-32C, Adler-32, CRC-64 and xxHash32/64. Also FNV-1 and FNV-1a in 32 and 64 bits; SipHash-2-4 and SipHash-1-3 with a 16-byte key in 64- and 128-bit forms; MurmurHash3 (murmur3_32, murmur3_128); wyhash final 4.2; jump consistent hashing; and rendezvous hashing.

The header primitives below std/http, std/multipart and std/mail: Header, get, values, has, add, set, remove, token, token_byte, valid_value, valid, quote, and parse_value with param, which resolve RFC 2231 and 5987 parameters.
An HTML tokenizer: a pull Tokenizer returning StartTag, EndTag, Text, Comment, Doctype and End tokens, attribute lookup, unescape for character references and escape for text and attribute values.

Server types: Request, Response, header helpers over header.Header and parse_url. Request.token is cancelled when the client goes away and when the handler returns. Request.remote is the client's IP address for connections served by serve, serve_tls and serve_conn. Serving: serve, serve_tls, serve_conn and serve_stream, and serve_quic for HTTP/3 over a std/quic listener; the _on forms (serve_on, serve_tls_on, serve_conn_on, serve_quic_on) take the listener's or connection's view. Client: a pooled client configured through client() and with_* builders, per-request builders, send, stream_to and download. with_version(Http3) sends https requests over QUIC. with_interface binds every connection to a network interface. with_resolver substitutes for net.lookup on host names; TLS keeps the host name for SNI and certificate checks. with_cancel makes a request fail with Io(Aborted) once its token is cancelled. URLs: parse_url, resolve and with_query_pair build on std/uri. connect returns a droppable Connection that closes its stream when released; detach hands the stream on. Proxies: with_proxy, with_http_proxy, with_https_proxy, with_no_proxy, with_proxy_from_environment and with_dialer send requests through an http:// proxy (absolute-form for http targets, CONNECT for https targets) or a socks5://, socks5h://, socks4:// or socks4a:// proxy. no_proxy follows Go's matching rules. The one content-coding table gives each coding its encoder and decoder; accepts_coding, negotiate_coding and encode_body read it, and the client's decompression and std/web compression and static files share it. Cookie is the one cookie model: the jar stores it, request_cookies reads the cookie headers into it and set_cookie and format_set_cookie write it, and std/web sessions use it. CookieJar is a shared RFC 6265 jar (cookie_jar, cookie_jar_on for a jar that reads a clock.Clock, with_cookie_jar, jar_set, jar_header, jar_cookies, jar_clear) that enforces the Secure rules and the __Secure- and __Host- prefixes and has no public-suffix check. A Response whose stream is a chan[[]u8] is written as it is produced, chunked on HTTP/1.1 and as DATA frames on HTTP/2, until the handler closes the channel.

serve_file and serve_file_with answer a request from a file. Content type comes from the extension, then sniffing. Weak ETag and Last-Modified work with If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since. A single Range is answered as 206 or 416, with If-Range. HEAD is supported and the body is streamed.

The static Huffman code of RFC 7541 appendix B that HPACK and QPACK share: decode, encode and encoded_size. decode fails Malformed on the EOS symbol and on padding that is longer than 7 bits or not all ones, and never panics on any input.

QPACK (RFC 9204) with no I/O. Decoder (decoder takes the maximum table capacity, the blocked stream limit and the field section size limit) keeps the dynamic table: on_encoder_stream consumes encoder stream bytes split anywhere, buffers at most 64 KiB of an incomplete instruction and returns the blocked streams that can now decode; decode returns Decoded, either Fields or Blocked, and queues a Section Acknowledgment; cancel_stream queues a Stream Cancellation; take_decoder_stream returns the queued decoder stream bytes plus one Insert Count Increment. Encoder writes field sections with the static table only, so they never block and nothing goes on the encoder stream; on_decoder_stream accepts Stream Cancellations and fails Malformed on any other instruction. decompression_failed, encoder_stream_error and decoder_stream_error return the HTTP/3 codes 0x200, 0x201 and 0x202 for failures of decode, on_encoder_stream and on_decoder_stream. Every entry point fails Malformed on hostile input: integers are capped at 2^62-1, and strings, indexes, Required Insert Counts, Bases, entry sizes and capacities are checked before use. static_table, insert_count, table_size and table_entries expose the tables.

Server-sent events. Shared: Event (id, event, data, retry), format, comment and keepalive. Server: stream, stream_with, serve_events, serve_events_with, Emitter and last_event_id. Client: parser, feed, parse and listen, which reads a text/event-stream response with any chunking and CR, LF or CRLF line ends.

accept (the 101 goes through http.upgrade) and dial over ws and wss return a droppable Socket that sends a normal close when released. Operations: receive, send_text, send_binary, ping and close, with _on forms, and adopt and detach on the *SocketHandle.
Bitmaps, pixel operations and resizing, with PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP, QOI and lossless WebP codecs.
INI files with sections, = or :, ; and # comments, quoted values, continuations and duplicate keys (last wins, or all with collect): parse, get, get_all, sections, set, format.

Error, the error type shared by the I/O, codec and protocol modules. Stream, a copyable struct of read, write and close closures that views a resource. Guard and Lease (guard, enter, retire), the shared state that makes a closed descriptor fail with NotConnected instead of reaching a reused descriptor. A buffered Reader over a stream or, with bytes_reader, over a buffer, with read_line, read_exact, read_up_to, read_some, read_byte, buffered and fill. write_all, read_all, buffer(n), copy, and the fixed-width integer codec in both byte orders: reads (be16, be24, be32, be64 and the le forms as i64, u16_be, u32_be, u64_be and the _le forms as unsigned types, uint_be and uint_le for any width from 1 to 8 bytes as u64, and u16_le_str, u32_le_str and u64_le_str over a str), appends (put_be16 through put_be64, put_le16 through put_le64, and put_be and put_le for any width up to 8 bytes) and in-place stores (set_be16 through set_be64, set_le16 through set_le64).

A reader and writer over UTF-8 bytes, the Value document model with member builders (text_member, int_member, bool_member, base64url_member, object_member, array_member) and typed getters (field, field_text, field_int, text_of, int_of), equal (compares numbers numerically and objects without regard to member order), and serialize[T] and deserialize[T] with naming policies.
RFC 6902 apply (atomic, failing with the operation's index) and diff; RFC 7396 merge_patch and merge_diff.
RFC 9535 JSONPath: compile, query, find, values and paths, with slices, filters, match, search, length, count and value, normalised paths, and syntax errors at a byte offset.
RFC 6901 pointers: escape, unescape, parse, format, get, has, set, add, replace, remove and relative pointers. Edits return a new document.

JSON Schema 2020-12. compile and compile_with check the schema, resolve $ref, $anchor, $dynamicRef and registered resources, and precompile patterns. validate returns Violations with the instance pointer, the keyword pointer and a message. unevaluatedProperties and unevaluatedItems use annotations from the branches that passed. format annotates or asserts.

Leveled line logging (debug, info, warn, error) to a descriptor (stderr by default) as level prefix: message, without timestamps so journald and other collectors add their own. with_prefix nests a prefix. A Logger also carries attributes (str_attr, int_attr, float_attr, bool_attr, with_attrs, and the _with level forms), a Format of Text (key=value, quoting what needs it) or Json (one object per line), a Sink (a descriptor, an io.Stream, a line closure or a Record handler), optional RFC 3339 timestamps, and a level from parse_level or the LOG_LEVEL variable. Each record is one write, so lines from green threads do not interleave. A failed write is passed to Logger.on_error (set with with_error_handler), which ignores it by default.
Message building: Message with text and HTML alternatives and attachments, RFC 2047 encoded words, quoted-printable, base64 wrapped at 76, RFC 5322 dates, and rejection of CR and LF in any header.
keys, values, sorted_keys, entries, from_pairs, clone, merge (the right map wins), filter, map_values, has, get_or, invert, count_by and group_by.

libm's trigonometric, hyperbolic, exponential and rounding functions, pi, tau, e, infinity, nan, is_nan, is_inf, generic abs, min, max, clamp and compare, and integer ipow, gcd, floor_div and floor_mod.

Media types by file extension and back (by_extension, extension) for web, image, font, archive, audio, video and subtitle formats. sniff recognises content by its magic bytes or its leading text and falls back to plain text or application/octet-stream.
MessagePack: the Value model with timestamps and extensions, a decoder with depth and length limits that reports the offset of an error, the smallest-form encode, and serialize[T] and deserialize[T].

multipart parsing and writing (RFC 7578, RFC 2046): a streaming Reader with limits and a spill sink for large parts, RFC 2231 and 5987 parameters, Writer (write_field, write_file and write_form_part) and Form; std/http reads and writes them with multipart_reader, multipart_form, set_multipart and with_multipart.

Addresses: IPv4 and IPv6 Addr, parse_ip, format_ip, parse_addr, format, in_network (tests an address against a CIDR prefix) and is_global (false for addresses the IANA special-purpose registries mark as not globally reachable, and for multicast). Types: the droppable Listener, Conn and Socket, each with a copyable ListenerHandle, ConnHandle or SocketHandle in its handle field; adopt and detach convert between a ConnHandle and a Conn, and adopt_socket and detach_socket between a SocketHandle and a Socket. TCP: listen, accept, accept_handle (returns the connection's view for a green thread to adopt), connect, dial and their _within forms with a connect timeout, connect_through (binds the socket to a network interface first), connect_first (tries a list of addresses in order through an optional interface) and interface_index. Connection I/O: read, write, write_all, close, shutdown_write, set_nodelay, read and write timeouts and stream, with read_on, write_on, write_all_on, close_on and stream_on on the view. UDP: bind_udp, send_to, receive_from and close_socket, with send_to_on, receive_from_on and close_socket_on on the view; a SocketHandle has separate fd and out descriptors, so one green thread can wait to receive while another waits to send. lookup tries an IP literal, then /etc/hosts, then A and AAAA queries to each /etc/resolv.conf nameserver. An Addr with an empty ip is a Unix address: listen_unix, connect_unix, connect_unix_within and socketpair return the same Listener and Conn, abstract names start with @ or NUL, and a listener unlinks its pathname when closed. peer_credentials returns the peer's credentials. listen_with and bind_udp_with take ListenOptions (reuse_addr, reuse_port, backlog). Socket options: set_keepalive and set_buffer_sizes. UDP multicast: join_group, leave_group, set_multicast_ttl, set_multicast_loop and set_multicast_interface. Dialer is a function value that makes a connection; direct_dialer is the plain one.
Typed queries over field references, row mapping, inserts, updates and deletes, tables created from types, and raw queries mapped onto structs, over an sql.ConnectionHandle.

Process state: args and environment (from the argument and environment vectors the program started with), env as str?, umask (sets the creation mask and returns the previous one), pid and exit. Queries: getcwd, chdir, hostname, uid, gid, euid, egid, ppid, executable, uptime, cpu_count, and lookup_user and user_name from /etc/passwd. set_env and unset_env are seen by env, environment, process.find and the environment process.run passes on. Directories: home_dir, cache_dir, config_dir, data_dir and state_dir (XDG variables when absolute, otherwise under $HOME), and temp_dir_path.

Signal (Hangup, Interrupt, Quit, IllegalInstruction, Trap, Abort, BusError, FloatingPoint, Kill, User1, SegmentationFault, User2, Pipe, Alarm, Terminate, Child, Continue, Stop, TerminalStop, TerminalInput, TerminalOutput, UrgentData, CpuLimit, FileSizeLimit, VirtualAlarm, ProfilingAlarm, WindowChange, IoReady, PowerFailure, BadSystemCall and Other(number) for any other number), the one signal vocabulary of std/process, with number, name, from_number and catchable. notify returns a droppable Watch (copyable WatchHandle) whose signals channel delivers the caught signals, with wait_for, wait_timeout, wait_any and stop. Also ignore, reset, send and raise. Kill and Stop cannot be caught and fail with Invalid.

OpenTelemetry traces, metrics and logs with W3C propagation, OTLP/HTTP protobuf and JSON, OTLP/gRPC and console exporters, and the instrumentation used by std/http, std/web, std/sql/driver and std/orm.

Slash-separated path manipulation: clean (lexical, resolving . and ..), join, base, dir, ext, stem and is_absolute. matches matches shell globs with *, ?, [...] classes (ranges, ! or ^ negation) and \ escapes; no wildcard crosses a /.

Pipelines. A Pipe owns a Reader and a Writer, each droppable so that releasing it completes it, with copyable ReaderHandle and WriterHandle views for green threads (adopt_reader, adopt_writer and the _on operations). Also segmented buffers, backpressure, Sequence and SequenceReader, and adapters between pipes and streams.

Command with arguments, an optional replacement environment, a working directory, Inherit, Piped or Null for each standard stream, and an optional new process group. start returns a droppable Child that kills and reaps an unwaited process and closes its pipes when released. start_handle, adopt, wait, kill (which takes a std/os/signal Signal; an Exit is Exited(code) or Signaled(signal) with the same type), and wait_on, wait_exit_on (waits without reaping, so the process group can still be signalled) and kill_on on the shared ChildHandle. run feeds input and collects both outputs. find searches PATH. success.
Java .properties: parse, get, set, format, with \u escapes and surrogate pairs.
The protobuf wire format: an encoder with nested messages and packed fields, and a field decoder.

QUIC version 1 (RFC 9000, 9001 and 9002) over UDP. Config holds the tls.Config (ALPN required), idle and handshake timeouts, keep-alive, the flow control and stream limits advertised to the peer, and retry. Server: listen returns a droppable Listener with a copyable ListenerHandle, and accept and accept_handle wait for an established connection; close_listener and close_listener_on. Client: dial, dial_handle, connect and connect_handle complete the handshake before returning. The droppable Connection closes with code 0 when released; its *ConnectionHandle holds the negotiated protocol, the addresses, group, suite, peer_certificates and, once ended, close_code, close_reason, closed_by_peer and application_close. adopt, detach, close_connection, close_on, stats and stats_on (a Stats snapshot), and update_keys and update_keys_on. Streams: open_stream, open_uni_stream, accept_stream and accept_uni_stream with _on forms return a copyable Stream; read, write, finish, reset, stop and stream, which adapts it to an io.Stream.

RFC 9002 loss detection and congestion control with no I/O: recovery makes a Recovery that on_sent, on_ack, on_timeout and discard_space drive per packet number Space. It keeps the RTT estimate, declares packets lost by packet and time thresholds, runs the probe timeout and NewReno with persistent congestion, and answers can_send, deadline and pto_duration. skip records a packet number left unsent, and an ACK covering one fails Malformed.

QUIC encoding with no I/O: a bounds-checked Cursor with varints and packet numbers, parse_header for long and short headers, version_negotiation, packet protection (keys, initial_keys, next_keys, seal, open, peek_key_phase) with header protection, Retry packets and their integrity tag (retry_packet, retry_tag, retry_valid), the frames as one Frame enum (parse_frames, put_frame, frame_size, put_stream_frame, ack_eliciting, ack_delay_ns), transport parameters (encode_parameters, decode_parameters) and the transport error codes. Every parser fails Malformed on hostile input and never panics.

A seedable, non-cryptographic xoshiro256** generator: seeded, rng (all 256 bits of state from std/crypto), next, unbiased below and between, float, chance, shuffle and pick. pcg32, pcg64 and chacha (seeded from 32 bytes; chacha_rng seeds from entropy) produce an Rng that every function accepts, and next32 draws 32 bits. Distributions: normal, exponential, gamma, beta, poisson, binomial, geometric, zipf, weighted_pick, cumulative with pick_cumulative, sample and permutation. Use std/crypto for secrets.

Bucket (token bucket in exact nanosecond units) with allow, allow_n, reserve, wait and set_rate. Window, a sliding log. Keyed, a bounded per-key set of buckets with idle eviction. All take a clock.Clock.

RESP2 and RESP3 over TCP or TLS: a droppable Client with a ClientHandle, connect with AUTH, SELECT and HELLO 3, command, typed helpers for strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets and publish, pipelining, transaction, pub/sub through a channel usable in select, command timeouts, and limits on bulk size and nesting.

Linear-time regular expressions in the RE2 style: compile and compile_with with Flags, generated (a pattern compiled into specialised code at build time), is_match, find, full_match, find_all, replace_all (with a closure receiving each Match), split and split_n. A match offers start, end, text, group and span, with byte offsets.

Policy with attempts, base, multiplier, maximum delay, Jitter (None, Full, Equal, Decorrelated), a deadline, a seeded Rng and a cancel token. delay; a loop driver start with next (reserve then commit) and at_least; run over a Step (Done, Retry, RetryAfter, Fatal) giving an Outcome.
Semantic Versioning 2.0.0: parse (with an optional v, failing at the offset of the first bad part), format, and compare and less with prerelease precedence, ignoring build metadata.

The Writer and Reader protocols, write[T], read[T] and schema[T] (which the compiler derives for every type), and Field[T, F]. Readers share parse_integer, parse_unsigned and syntax_at, which builds the Syntax error for a line and column; the helpers the derived code calls are private. Tree, Node and Member are the value shape that CBOR, MessagePack, TOML, YAML and template data share: to_tree builds one from any value, tree_reader reads a T from one, and key_text and unsigned_tree hold the key text and the u64 range rule. A format maps its own value type V to a tree with node_of and a Shape[V] function, and back with value_of and a Rebuild[V].
Vector reads and writes, splat, mask, blend, min, max, lane access, byte shuffles and find_byte.
Group[K, V] with do, do_shared, forget and in_flight, which run one call per key while the others wait for its result. Expiring[V], a value refreshed at most once per interval.

Queries and transforms: contains, index, clone, concat, reverse, map, filter, fold, scan, any, all, sum, min and max (as optionals), sorted. Sorting: sort and sort_by are unstable and in place, a quicksort with median-of-three pivots that recurses into the smaller side and finishes runs of 16 or fewer with insertion sort. sort_stable and sort_stable_by are a top-down merge sort; sort_by_key is stable. Also reduce, count, find, find_index, first, last, equal, compare, starts_with, ends_with, unique (adjacent duplicates), flat_map, flatten, repeat, lower_bound, binary_search (the first match) and binary_search_by. take, skip, chunks and windows share the source's elements. partition and zip work over Pair[A, B]. fill, swap, rotate, insert and remove are in place. They chain as calls on the slice: xs.sort(), words.map(fn(w) w.len).sum().|> slices.sort()`.
