Fails with Launch(NotFound) when no executable is found, Launch(TimedOut) when the endpoint is not announced within Options.startup, Launch(Aborted) as soon as the browser exits without announcing it, Launch(Eof) when the browser closes its standard error without announcing the endpoint and keeps running, and Launch(error) for any other failure to create the profile directory, start the process or connect. A failed launch kills the process and removes the profile directory.
Starts a headless browser like launch and returns its handle. The caller is responsible for calling shutdown_on. Fails with the same errors as launch.

Ends the page: its events stop and its browser context, with every target in it, is disposed. Fails with the errors of call when the browser cannot dispose the context; the page's events have stopped by then.
fn navigate(p: Page, url: str, referrer: str) ! Error

Starts navigating the page to url. A non-empty referrer is sent as the referrer. Returns once the browser accepts the navigation, without waiting for the page to load. Fails with Protocol(text) when the browser rejects the navigation, for example because the host cannot be resolved, and with the errors of call otherwise.
Returns a channel that is closed once s has been ended with unsubscribe.
struct Bom { pub name: str pub len: i64 }
A byte order mark found at the start of data. The canonical name of the encoding the mark selects, such as UTF-16LE. The length of the mark in bytes, which a caller skips to reach the text.
enum Error { UnknownEncoding Malformed(i64) Unmappable(i64, u32) }

Why a character set conversion failed. The label does not name a supported encoding. The input is not valid in the encoding. at is the byte offset in the input where the invalid data starts. A character has no representation in the target encoding. Carries the byte offset at of the character in the string being encoded and its code point c.

Returns the canonical encoding name for label, or none when the label is unknown. The label is trimmed and compared case-insensitively. Aliases such as latin1, ascii, cp1252 and utf8 resolve to a canonical name; the supported names are UTF-8, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE, UTF-32LE, UTF-32BE, ISO-8859-1, ISO-8859-2, ISO-8859-15, windows-1250, windows-1251, windows-1252, KOI8-R, IBM437 and IBM850. The labels utf-16 and utf-32 mean the little-endian forms, and ascii and us-ascii mean windows-1252.
fn decode(label: str, data: []u8) -> str ! Error

Decodes data written in the encoding named by label into a UTF-8 string. A leading UTF-8 byte order mark is dropped. For UTF-16 and UTF-32 a leading byte order mark selects the byte order over the one the label names and is dropped. Single-byte encodings accept every byte: values below 0x80 map to themselves and the rest through the encoding's table. Fails with UnknownEncoding when label is not recognised and with Malformed at the byte offset of the first invalid UTF-8 sequence, lone UTF-16 surrogate or invalid UTF-32 code point. An odd trailing byte in UTF-16, or one to three trailing bytes in UTF-32, fails at the start of the incomplete unit.
fn decode_lossy(label: str, data: []u8) -> str ! Error
Decodes data written in the encoding named by label into a UTF-8 string, replacing invalid input with U+FFFD. Byte order marks are handled as in decode. Fails only with UnknownEncoding.
Returns the byte order mark at the start of data, or none when there is none. FF FE 00 00 is reported as UTF-32LE before FF FE is considered as UTF-16LE.
fn encode(label: str, s: str) -> []u8 ! Error

Encodes s in the encoding named by label. UTF-16 and UTF-32 are written without a byte order mark. Invalid UTF-8 in s is written as U+FFFD. Fails with UnknownEncoding when label is not recognised and with Unmappable for the first character a single-byte encoding cannot represent.
fn encode_replace(label: str, s: str, replacement: str) -> []u8 ! Error

Encodes s in the encoding named by label, writing replacement for each character a single-byte encoding cannot represent. The UTF-8 bytes of replacement are written unchanged. Fails only with UnknownEncoding.

Returns the code point that Windows-1252 assigns to the byte b. Bytes below 0x80 and from 0xA0 map to themselves, and 0x80 to 0x9F map through the Windows-1252 table, which leaves 0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90 and 0x9D as the control characters of the same value.

A streaming Brotli encoder made by encoder. encode takes input in any chunking, flush ends the data written so far on a byte boundary, and finish ends the stream. After finish, encode, flush and finish fail with Invalid. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Compresses data and passes the compressed bytes that are ready to the encoder's sink. Input is buffered and written in meta-blocks of up to 256 KiB, so a call can produce no output. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the buffered input and the last meta-block, ending the stream. Fails with Invalid when the stream is already finished, and with any error sink returns.

Writes the buffered input and an empty metadata meta-block that pads the output to a byte boundary, so a decoder can read everything encoded so far. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Returns data compressed as a Brotli stream. level is clamped to 0..11; 0 stores the data in uncompressed meta-blocks. The window is sized from data.len, up to 22 bits.
fn decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes a Brotli stream from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. Decoding stops at the end of the stream. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Returns the bytes decoded from a Brotli stream in data. Bytes after the end of the stream are Malformed. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.
fn encoder(level: i64, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) -> *Encoder
Returns an encoder that writes a Brotli stream with a 22-bit window to sink. level is clamped to 0..11; 0 stores the data in uncompressed meta-blocks.

A streaming bzip2 encoder made by encoder. encode takes input in any chunking and finish ends the stream. After finish, encode and finish fail with Invalid. Each block holds up to level * 100000 bytes of run-length encoded input. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Adds data to the current block and passes each completed block to the encoder's sink. Input is buffered until a block is full, so a call can produce no output. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the final block and the stream trailer with the combined checksum. Fails with Invalid when the stream is already finished, and with any error sink returns.
Returns data compressed as a bzip2 stream. level is clamped to 1..9 and sets the block size to level * 100000 bytes.
fn decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes bzip2 from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. Concatenated streams are decoded in turn. Input with no stream is Malformed, and a randomised block (a bzip2 0.9.0 feature) is Unsupported. Block and stream checksums are verified. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Returns the bytes decoded from bzip2 in data. Concatenated streams are decoded in turn; input with no stream is Malformed. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.
fn encoder(level: i64, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) -> *Encoder
Returns an encoder that writes a bzip2 stream to sink. level is clamped to 1..9 and sets the block size to level * 100000 bytes.
struct BitReader { pub before_read: fn() ! io.Error ... }

A reader that hands out bits from the least significant end of each byte, from a slice or an io.Reader. Every read that runs past the end of the input fails with Malformed. A reader made by stream_reader calls before_read each time it is about to ask its source for more bytes, so a decoder can pass its pending output to a sink first. Called before the source is read.
struct Buffer { pub data: []u8 pub len: i64 ... }

A growable byte buffer that also packs bits from the least significant end of each byte. Every write is infallible, so an encoder core builds its output here and the caller decides when to hand it to a sink. Whole bytes land in data as bits are packed, and a partial byte waits in the accumulator until align or more bits complete it. Use the byte writes with no bits pending, or after align. The backing storage. The first len bytes are written. The number of bytes written to data.
The scratch space build and lengths need, sized for an alphabet.

A hash chain over a byte history: a table of the latest position for each hash of a few bytes and a ring of the position before each one with the same hash. Made by chain. Positions are stored one above their value, so zero marks the end of a chain.
struct Code { pub lens: []u8 pub codes: []u32 pub used: i64 pub first: i64 }

The code lengths and bit patterns of a canonical Huffman code, ready for put_code. Made by code and filled by build. A pattern is stored bit-reversed, so writing it least significant bit first emits the code from its first bit. The length in bits of each symbol's code, 0 for a symbol that does not occur. The bit-reversed pattern of each symbol's code. The number of symbols that occur. The first symbol that occurs, or 0 when none does.

A streaming encoder over a format's core, made by encoder. encode, flush and finish run the format's steps on its output buffer and pass the bytes that are ready to sink. After finish, all three fail with Invalid.
struct History { pub data: []u8 pub fill: i64 pub pos: i64 pub short: *Chain pub long: *Chain pub window: i64 ... }

The input window of an LZ77 encoder: the bytes seen so far, the position up to which they have been written out, and a short-match and a long-match hash chain over them. Made by history. append fills it and slides it forward when it is full, index_to adds positions to the chains, and the chains answer searches through walk. The window storage. The first fill bytes hold input. The number of bytes of data that hold input. The position in data of the first byte not yet written out. The chain over the short match width. The chain over eight-byte matches. The farthest back, in bytes, that a match may reach.
A position in a Buffer that rewind can return to. The number of bytes written when the mark was taken.
struct Match { pub len: i64 pub off: i64 }
The best match a search has found so far. The length in bytes, or the length to beat when the search starts. The distance back from the search position to the start of the match.

Space for the two-level lookup tables that decode canonical Huffman codes read least significant bit first. Made by tables. Each table built into pool starts at the base build_table returns: 1 << root entries indexed by the next root bits, followed by second-level blocks for codes longer than root. An entry holds the symbol in bits 8 and up and the code length in the low four bits. An entry that links to a second-level block holds its offset from the base in bits 8 and up, 0x80, and the number of index bits in the low four. A single-symbol table has length zero and 0x40 set. An entry of 0 is a bit pattern no code uses. The entries of every table built since the last reset_tables.
Discards the bits left in the current byte.
Returns the number of bits buffered in the accumulator, which modulo eight is the position within the current byte.
Discards the next n bits, which must already be buffered by a peek or a take. Fails with Malformed when fewer than n bits remain.
Returns true when at least one more whole byte can be read, asking the source when the buffer is empty.
fn peek(r: *BitReader, n: i64) -> i64 ! io.Error

Returns the next n bits without consuming them, for an n from 0 to 56, loading more input when fewer are buffered. Near the end of the input fewer than n bits can remain, and the missing high bits read as zero.
Fills dst with the next whole bytes, which must start on a byte boundary. Fails with Malformed when the input ends first. Call align_input first when a partial byte is pending.

Loads bytes into the accumulator until it holds more than 56 bits or the input ends. Stops early, without asking the source for more, once the accumulator holds need bits and the buffered input is used up.
fn symbol(r: *BitReader, pool: []u32, base: i64, root: i64) -> i64 ! io.Error
Reads one symbol from r with the table at base in pool, built with the same root. Fails with Malformed when the bits read are a pattern no code uses or the input ends first.
fn take(r: *BitReader, n: i64) -> i64 ! io.Error
Reads n bits as a number with the first bit read in the lowest position, for an n from 0 to 56. Fails with Malformed when fewer than n bits remain.
Pads with zero bits to the next byte boundary and writes everything pending.
Returns a sink function that appends each chunk to b, for the one-shot decoders.
Returns the bytes written so far, not counting bits still pending. The slice views the buffer's storage, so a later write or reset can change it.
fn deliver(b: *Buffer, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) ! io.Error
Passes the whole bytes ready in b to sink and empties b of them, calling sink only when there are some. Fails with any error sink returns.
Returns the whole bytes ready to send and empties the buffer of them, keeping a partial byte pending. The slice is valid until the next write.
fn encoder(out: *Buffer, chunk: i64, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, feed: fn([]u8), sync: fn(), close: fn()) -> *Encoder

Returns an encoder that delivers out to sink. feed takes at most chunk bytes of input, sync ends the data written so far on a boundary a decoder can read, and close writes the end of the stream. All three write into out.
Writes the whole bytes pending in the bit accumulator to data, leaving fewer than eight bits.
Returns the current position of b, including any bits pending.
Returns the number of bits waiting in the accumulator, including whole bytes not yet written to data. The result modulo eight is the position within the current byte.
fn put_bits(b: *Buffer, v: i64, n: i64)
Appends the low n bits of v, least significant bit first, for an n from 0 to 32. Bits of v above n must be zero.
Appends data, after writing any whole bytes still pending in the bit accumulator. Call align first when a partial byte is pending.
Writes the code of sym to out.
fn put_le(b: *Buffer, v: i64, n: i64)
Appends the low n bytes of v in little-endian order, for an n from 0 to 8.
Makes room for n more bytes after len.
Discards everything written and everything pending, keeping the storage.
Discards everything written to b since m was taken. The buffer must not have been drained or reset since.
Fills codes with the bit-reversed canonical codes for the lengths lens, shorter codes first and equal lengths in symbol order. Lengths run from 0, which skips the symbol, to 15.
fn build(b: *Builder, freq: []i64, c: *Code, limit: i64)
Builds the code for freq into c, with no code longer than limit bits. Sets c.used and c.first. With fewer than two symbols present no lengths are assigned, and the code of c.first is 0.
fn lengths(b: *Builder, freq: []i64, lens: []u8, limit: i64) -> i64

Fills lens with the lengths of a Huffman code for the symbol frequencies freq, none longer than limit bits, and returns the number of symbols with a nonzero frequency. The code is complete when two or more symbols occur. With fewer than two the lengths stay zero and the caller picks the format's form for a one-symbol code. limit is at most 15.
Adds position i of hist to the chain. Reads 8 bytes from i, so i + 8 must not pass the end of hist.
Moves every remembered position back by delta, for a history that has slid forward by that much, and forgets those that fall off the front.
fn walk(c: *Chain, hist: []u8, p: i64, end: i64, window: i64, nice: i64, tries: i64, found: *Match)

Walks the chain for position p of hist and records in found any match longer than found.len, nearest candidates first. At most tries candidates are checked, none more than window bytes back or older than the chain remembers, and a match may not reach past end. The walk stops once a match of nice bytes is found.
Feeds data in pieces of at most the encoder's chunk size, passing the output that is ready to the sink after each piece. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error the sink returns.
Closes the format, marks the encoder finished and passes the output to the sink. Fails with Invalid when the encoder is already finished, and with any error the sink returns.
Syncs the format and passes the output to the sink. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error the sink returns.

Copies the start of input after the bytes already held and returns the number copied. A history that is full first slides forward so that only window bytes before pos stay, which moves fill, pos and every position in the chains back by the same amount.
fn extend_back(h: *History, p: i64, anchor: i64, off: i64) -> i64
Returns the number of bytes, at most p - anchor, by which a match found at p with distance off also matches the bytes just before p.
fn index_to(h: *History, target: i64, deep: bool)
Adds the positions from the first one not yet added up to target to the long chain, when deep, and to the short chain.
fn build_single(t: *Tables, sym: i64, root: i64) -> i64
Builds a table of 1 << root entries in which every bit pattern decodes to sym with no bits consumed, and returns its base.
fn build_table(t: *Tables, lens: []u8, root: i64) -> i64 ! io.Error

Builds the decoding table for the canonical code with the lengths lens and returns its base in pool. Lengths run from 0, which marks an unused symbol, to 15, and root is the number of bits the first level indexes. Fails with Malformed when the lengths over-subscribe the code. An incomplete code is accepted, and the bit patterns it leaves unused decode to the entry 0.
Forgets every table built so far so the pool can be reused.
Returns an empty buffer with room for capacity bytes, and at least 16.
Returns scratch space for building codes over alphabets of up to max_symbols symbols.
fn chain(width: i64, hash_bits: i64, link_bits: i64) -> *Chain
Returns a hash chain that hashes width bytes into hash_bits bits and remembers the last 1 << link_bits positions. width runs from 1 to 8, and positions must be below 2^32 - 1.
Returns a code for an alphabet of n symbols with every length zero.
Returns the total number of bits that coding the symbol counts freq takes with the lengths of c.
fn copy_match(out: []u8, pos: i64, distance: i64, length: i64)
Copies length bytes from distance bytes behind pos to pos in out. The ranges can overlap, in which case the copy repeats the last distance bytes written, as LZ77 decoders need.
fn decompress(data: []u8, limit: i64, decode: fn(*io.Reader, fn([]u8) ! io.Error, i64) ! io.Error) -> []u8 ! io.Error
Returns everything decode writes to its sink when it reads data, for a one-shot decompress. Fails with any error decode returns.
fn each_chunk(data: []u8, size: i64, step: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) ! io.Error
Calls step with consecutive pieces of data of at most size bytes. Fails with the first error step returns.
fn history(window: i64, span: i64, short_width: i64, hash_bits: i64, link_bits: i64) -> *History

Returns an empty history of span bytes with matches reaching back up to window bytes. The short chain hashes short_width bytes. Both chains hash into hash_bits bits and remember the last 1 << link_bits positions.

Builds the Huffman tree over the n leaf weights in weight[..n], which must be in ascending order, and replaces each of them with the depth of its leaf. weight and parent need room for 2 * n - 1 entries; the entries past n are overwritten.
fn match_length(hist: []u8, a: i64, b: i64, limit: i64) -> i64
Returns the number of leading bytes at a that equal the bytes at b in hist, up to limit.
Returns an empty buffer for the output of decoding input, sized for typical expansion and never above limit.
Appends v to out as a base-128 varint of one to ten bytes.
Reads exactly dst.len bytes from source into dst. Fails with Malformed when the source ends first, and with any error the source returns.

Fills head from the start of the next frame or chunk and returns true, or returns false when the input has ended cleanly before its first byte. Fails with Malformed when the input ends partway through head, and with any error the source returns.
fn read_varint(data: []u8, mut at: i64, max_bytes: i64) -> u64 ! io.Error

Reads the varint that starts at data[at] and advances at past it. Fails with Malformed when the input ends inside the varint, it runs past max_bytes bytes, or the value does not fit in 64 bits. A varint longer than necessary is accepted. max_bytes is at most 10.
Subtracts shift from every position in table, setting those that would go below zero to zero.
Returns the symbol when exactly one length in lens is nonzero, and -1 otherwise.
Reads and discards n bytes from source. Fails with Malformed when the source ends first, and with any error the source returns.
Returns a reader over all of data.
Returns a reader that pulls from source through a buffer of size bytes.
fn tables(max_symbols: i64, max_root: i64, pool_size: i64) -> *Tables
Returns table space for codes over alphabets of up to max_symbols symbols and first-level sizes up to 1 << max_root, with room for pool_size entries that grows when needed.
fn write_varint(buf: []u8, at: i64, v: u64) -> i64

Writes v as a base-128 varint, seven bits per byte with the least significant group first, into buf starting at at, and returns the position after it. A varint takes one to ten bytes, so buf needs room for ten from at.

A streaming DEFLATE encoder made by encoder, producing a raw, zlib or gzip stream. encode takes input in any chunking, flush ends the data written so far on a byte boundary, and finish writes the end of the stream and any trailer. After finish, encode, flush and finish fail with Invalid. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

The container around a DEFLATE stream. A bare DEFLATE stream (RFC 1951) with no header or checksum. A zlib stream (RFC 1950): a two byte header, the DEFLATE stream and an Adler-32 checksum. A gzip member (RFC 1952): a ten byte header, the DEFLATE stream and a CRC-32 and size trailer.

Compresses data and passes the compressed bytes that are ready to the encoder's sink, updating the checksum for the zlib and gzip formats. Input is buffered, so a call can produce no output. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the buffered input, the final block and, for zlib and gzip, the checksum trailer. Fails with Invalid when the stream is already finished, and with any error sink returns.

Writes the buffered input and an empty stored block that pads the output to a byte boundary, so a decoder can read everything encoded so far. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
fn encoder(format: Format, level: i64, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) -> *Encoder

Returns an encoder that writes a stream in format to sink; a zlib or gzip header is written immediately. level is clamped to 0..9, with a negative value meaning 6; 0 stores the data without compression.
Returns data compressed as a raw DEFLATE stream. level is clamped to 0..9, with a negative value meaning 6; 0 stores the data without compression.
fn decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes a raw DEFLATE stream from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. Decoding stops after the final block. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Returns the bytes decoded from a raw DEFLATE stream in data. Bytes after the final block are ignored. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.

Returns data compressed as a single gzip member. level is clamped to 0..9, with a negative value meaning 6; 0 stores the data without compression. The header carries no name, comment or modification time and marks the operating system as unknown.
fn gzip_decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes gzip from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. Concatenated members are decoded in turn. The header checksum, the CRC-32 and the size in each trailer are verified. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Returns the bytes decoded from gzip in data. Concatenated members are decoded in turn. The header checksum, the CRC-32 and the size in each trailer are verified. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.
Returns data compressed as a zlib stream. level is clamped to 0..9, with a negative value meaning 6; 0 stores the data without compression.
fn zlib_decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes a zlib stream from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. The header and the Adler-32 checksum are verified. A stream that needs a preset dictionary is Unsupported. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Returns the bytes decoded from a zlib stream in data. The header and the Adler-32 checksum are verified, and bytes after the stream are ignored. A stream that needs a preset dictionary is Unsupported. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.

A streaming LZ4 frame encoder made by encoder. encode takes input in any chunking, flush writes the buffered input as blocks, and finish writes the end mark and the content checksum. After finish, encode, flush and finish fail with Invalid. The frame uses linked blocks of up to 64 KiB. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Compresses data and passes each completed 64 KiB block to the encoder's sink. Input is buffered until a block is full, so a call can produce no output. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.

Writes the buffered input, the end mark and the content checksum. An encoder that received no input still writes a complete empty frame. Fails with Invalid when the stream is already finished, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the buffered input as blocks, so a decoder can read everything encoded so far. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Returns data compressed as one LZ4 frame. level is clamped to 1..12. The frame header records the content size.
fn decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes LZ4 frames from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. Concatenated frames are decoded in turn and skippable frames are ignored. Content and block checksums are verified. Input with no frame is Malformed; the legacy frame format and frames that need a dictionary are Unsupported. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Returns the bytes decoded from LZ4 frames in data. Concatenated frames are decoded in turn and skippable frames are ignored. Input with no frame is Malformed; the legacy frame format and frames that need a dictionary are Unsupported. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.
fn encoder(level: i64, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) -> *Encoder
Returns an encoder that writes one LZ4 frame to sink. level is clamped to 1..12; higher levels search more candidates and, from 3, parse lazily. The frame header carries no content size.

A streaming encoder for the Snappy framing format made by encoder. encode takes input in any chunking and writes it as chunks of up to 64 KiB, storing a chunk uncompressed when compression saves less than an eighth. After finish, encode, flush and finish fail with Invalid. The stream identifier is the first output. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Compresses data and passes each completed 64 KiB chunk to the encoder's sink. Input is buffered until a chunk is full, so a call can produce no output beyond the stream identifier. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the buffered input as a chunk. The format has no trailer, so this equals flush. Fails with Invalid when the stream is already finished, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the buffered input as a chunk, so a decoder can read everything encoded so far. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Returns data compressed in the Snappy framing format.

Returns data compressed as one Snappy block, which is the raw block format with no framing. The block holds the whole of data. compress and encoder write the framing format, which splits input into 64 KiB chunks.
fn decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes the Snappy framing format from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. Chunk checksums are verified. Skippable chunks are ignored; a reserved unskippable chunk type is Unsupported, and input without the leading stream identifier is Malformed. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.
Returns the decoded length stored in the header of the Snappy block data. Reads only the leading varint. Fails with Malformed when it is truncated, longer than five bytes or above 0xFFFFFFFF.

Returns the bytes decoded from the Snappy framing format in data. Chunk checksums are verified. Input without the leading stream identifier is Malformed. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.

Returns the bytes decoded from the Snappy block data, which is the raw block format with no framing. Fails with TooLarge when the decoded length in the header exceeds limit and with Malformed when the header is invalid, claims more than 22 times the compressed size or the block does not decode to exactly that length.
Returns an encoder that writes the Snappy framing format to sink.

A streaming xz encoder made by encoder. encode takes input in any chunking and finish writes the end of the stream. The file holds at most one block of LZMA2 chunks with a CRC-64 integrity check. After finish, encode and finish fail with Invalid. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Compresses data and passes the compressed bytes that are ready to the encoder's sink. Input is buffered, so a call can produce no output. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the buffered input, the block padding and check, the index and the stream footer. Fails with Invalid when the stream is already finished, and with any error sink returns.
Returns data compressed as an xz file. level is clamped to 0..9; the dictionary is reduced for inputs smaller than it.
fn decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes an xz file from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. Concatenated streams are decoded in turn, with zero padding in multiples of four bytes allowed between them. The CRC-32 of each header and the index and the integrity check of each block (none, CRC-32, CRC-64 or SHA-256) are verified. Filters other than LZMA2 and delta, and other check types, are Unsupported. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Returns the bytes decoded from an xz file in data. Streams are handled as in decode. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.
fn encoder(level: i64, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) -> *Encoder
Returns an encoder that writes an xz file to sink. level is clamped to 0..9 and selects the dictionary size, from 256 KiB at 0 to 64 MiB at 9, and the match search effort.
Returns data compressed in the .lzma format: a 13 byte header of properties, dictionary size and uncompressed size, then an LZMA stream. level is clamped to 0..9. The header records the size of data.

Returns the bytes decoded from data in the .lzma format: a 13 byte header of properties, dictionary size and uncompressed size, then an LZMA stream. The uncompressed size can be unknown, in which case the stream ends with an end marker. Fails with TooLarge when the declared size or the output exceeds limit and with Malformed when the header is invalid or the data does not decode to the declared size.

A streaming Zstandard encoder made by encoder. encode takes input in any chunking, flush writes the buffered input as blocks, and finish writes the last block and the content checksum. After finish, encode, flush and finish fail with Invalid. The frame carries no content size. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Compresses data and passes each completed block to the encoder's sink. Input is buffered until a block is full, so a call can produce no output. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the buffered input as the last block, followed by the low 32 bits of the XXH64 content checksum. Fails with Invalid when the stream is already finished, and with any error sink returns.
Writes the buffered input as blocks, so a decoder can read everything encoded so far. Fails with Invalid after finish, and with any error sink returns.
Returns data compressed as one Zstandard frame. level is clamped to 1..22. The frame header records the content size and the window is reduced for small inputs.
fn decode(r: *io.Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error, limit: i64) ! io.Error

Decodes Zstandard frames from r and passes the decoded bytes to sink in chunks until the input ends. Concatenated frames are decoded in turn and skippable frames are ignored. A frame's content checksum is verified when present. Input with no frame is Malformed; frames that need a dictionary or a window above 2 GiB are Unsupported. A frame whose declared content size exceeds limit fails with TooLarge before any of it is decoded. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes, Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated, and with any error r or sink returns. A chunk is valid only during the call to sink.

Returns the bytes decoded from Zstandard frames in data. Concatenated frames are decoded in turn and skippable frames are ignored. Input with no frame is Malformed; frames that need a dictionary or a window above 2 GiB are Unsupported. Fails with TooLarge when the output would exceed limit bytes and with Malformed when the input is invalid or truncated.
fn encoder(level: i64, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) -> *Encoder
Returns an encoder that writes one Zstandard frame to sink. level is clamped to 1..22; the window is at most 8 MiB and higher levels search more candidates.
A double-ended queue stored in a ring buffer. Pushes and pops at either end take amortised constant time. The buffer doubles when it is full. Mutating functions take the deque as mut.
fn at[T](d: Deque[T], i: i64) -> T?
Returns the item i places from the front of d, where 0 is the front, or none when i is negative or at least size(d).
Returns the item at the back of d without removing it, or none when it is empty.
Returns the item at the front of d without removing it, or none when it is empty.
Removes and returns the item at the back of d, or none when it is empty.
Removes and returns the item at the front of d, or none when it is empty.
fn push_back[T](mut d: Deque[T], item: T)
Adds item at the back of d. Takes amortised constant time; a full buffer is doubled and its items are copied.
fn push_front[T](mut d: Deque[T], item: T)
Adds item at the front of d. Takes amortised constant time; a full buffer is doubled and its items are copied.
Returns the number of items in d.
A binary heap that yields its smallest item first, as decided by a less function. Create one with heap. Mutating functions take the heap as mut.
fn insert[T](mut h: Heap[T], item: T)
Adds item to h. Sifts the item up with O(log n) calls to less.
Returns the item that pop would return, or none when h is empty. Takes constant time.
Removes and returns the item that less ranks first, or none when h is empty. Items that compare equal leave in no defined order. Sifting down takes O(log n) calls to less.
Returns the number of items in h.
fn heap[T](less: fn(T, T) -> bool) -> Heap[T]

Returns an empty heap ordered by less. less(a, b) returns true when a must leave the heap before b. It must be a strict weak ordering. For a max-heap, pass a function that compares in the opposite direction.

A least-recently-used cache with a fixed capacity. Create one with cache. When a new key is added to a full cache the least recently used entry is evicted. get and put count as a use; contains and keys do not. Lookup, insertion and eviction take constant time on average. Mutating functions take the cache as mut.
fn contains[K: Hash, V](c: Cache[K, V], key: K) -> bool
Returns true when key is in c. Does not change the order of use.
fn get[K: Hash, V](mut c: Cache[K, V], key: K) -> V?
Returns the value stored under key, or none when it is absent. Makes the entry the most recently used.
fn keys[K: Hash, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> []K
Returns the keys of c from the most recently used to the least recently used. Does not change the order of use.
fn put[K: Hash, V](mut c: Cache[K, V], key: K, value: V) -> K?

Stores value under key and makes the entry the most recently used. Returns none when key was already present, in which case its value is replaced, or when the cache had room. Returns the evicted key when a full cache dropped its least recently used entry to make room.
fn size[K: Hash, V](c: Cache[K, V]) -> i64
Returns the number of entries in c.
fn cache[K: Hash, V](capacity: i64) -> Cache[K, V]
Returns an empty cache that holds at most capacity entries. Panics when capacity is less than 1.
struct Entry[K, V] { pub key: K pub value: V }
A key and its value in a Tree. The key. The value stored under the key.

A map from keys to values kept in ascending key order, implemented as an AVL tree. Create one with tree. Lookup, insertion, removal and the nearest-key queries take O(log n) time. Keys are compared with < and >. Nodes are shared between copies of a Tree, so keep a single copy and mutate it through mut.
fn ceiling_entry[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V], key: K) -> Entry[K, V]?
Returns the entry with the smallest key that is at least key, or none when every key is smaller.
fn contains[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V], key: K) -> bool
Returns true when key is in t.
fn each[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V], visit: fn(K, V))
Calls visit with each key and value of t in ascending key order.
fn each_range[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V], lo: K, hi: K, visit: fn(K, V))
Calls visit in ascending key order with each key and value whose key is at least lo and less than hi. Skips subtrees outside the range, so it takes O(log n + m) time for m visited entries.
fn entries[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V]) -> []Entry[K, V]
Returns the entries of t in ascending key order.
fn first[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V]) -> Entry[K, V]?
Returns the entry with the smallest key, or none when t is empty.
fn floor_entry[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V], key: K) -> Entry[K, V]?
Returns the entry with the largest key that is at most key, or none when every key is greater.
fn get[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V], key: K) -> V?
Returns the value stored under key, or none when it is absent.
fn height[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V]) -> i64
Returns the height of t in levels, which is 0 for an empty tree.
fn is_valid[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V]) -> bool

Returns true when t satisfies the AVL invariants. Checks that keys are ordered, that subtree heights differ by at most one and are recorded correctly, and that the stored size matches the number of nodes. Visits every node.
fn keys[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V]) -> []K
Returns the keys of t in ascending order.
fn last[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V]) -> Entry[K, V]?
Returns the entry with the largest key, or none when t is empty.
fn put[K: Ord, V](mut t: Tree[K, V], key: K, value: V) -> bool
Stores value under key, replacing the value when the key is already present. Returns true when key was new and false when an existing value was replaced.
fn range[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V], lo: K, hi: K) -> []Entry[K, V]
Returns the entries whose key is at least lo and less than hi, in ascending key order. The range is half-open: hi is excluded. The result is empty when lo is not less than hi.
fn remove[K: Ord, V](mut t: Tree[K, V], key: K) -> bool
Removes key from t. Returns true when the key was present and false when t did not change.
fn size[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V]) -> i64
Returns the number of keys in t.
fn values[K: Ord, V](t: Tree[K, V]) -> []V
Returns the values of t in ascending order of their keys.
fn tree[K: Ord, V]() -> Tree[K, V]

A set of values kept in a hash map, so items must be hashable. Create one with set or from_slice. Membership, insertion and removal take constant time on average. Mutating functions take the set as mut.
fn add[T: Hash](mut s: Set[T], item: T) -> bool
Adds item to s. Returns true when the item was new and false when it was already present.
fn difference[T: Hash](a: Set[T], b: Set[T]) -> Set[T]
Returns a new set of the items of a that are not in b. Neither argument changes.
fn has[T: Hash](s: Set[T], item: T) -> bool
Returns true when item is in s.
fn intersection[T: Hash](a: Set[T], b: Set[T]) -> Set[T]
Returns a new set of the items that are in both a and b. Neither argument changes.
fn is_subset[T: Hash](a: Set[T], b: Set[T]) -> bool
Returns true when every item of a is also in b. An empty set is a subset of every set.
Returns the items of s as a slice in insertion order.
fn remove[T: Hash](mut s: Set[T], item: T) -> bool
Removes item from s. Returns true when the item was present and false when s did not change.
Returns the number of items in s.
fn union[T: Hash](a: Set[T], b: Set[T]) -> Set[T]
Returns a new set of the items that are in a or b. Neither argument changes.
Returns a set of the items of xs, ignoring duplicates.

A set of ordered values kept in ascending order, backed by an ordered.Tree. Create one with sorted or from_slice. Membership, insertion, removal and the nearest-item queries take O(log n) time. Mutating functions take the set as mut. Nodes are shared between copies, so keep a single copy.
fn add[T: Ord](mut s: Sorted[T], item: T) -> bool
Adds item to s. Returns true when the item was new and false when it was already present.
fn ceiling_item[T: Ord](s: Sorted[T], item: T) -> T?
Returns the smallest item that is at least item, or none when every item is smaller.
Returns the smallest item, or none when s is empty.
fn floor_item[T: Ord](s: Sorted[T], item: T) -> T?
Returns the largest item that is at most item, or none when every item is greater.
fn has[T: Ord](s: Sorted[T], item: T) -> bool
Returns true when item is in s.
Returns the items of s in ascending order.
Returns the largest item, or none when s is empty.
fn range[T: Ord](s: Sorted[T], lo: T, hi: T) -> []T
Returns the items that are at least lo and less than hi, in ascending order.
fn remove[T: Ord](mut s: Sorted[T], item: T) -> bool
Removes item from s. Returns true when the item was present and false when s did not change.
Returns the number of items in s.
Returns a sorted set of the items of xs, ignoring duplicates.

Returns n bytes from the operating system's cryptographically secure random generator. Reads through the getrandom system call with no flags, so the call blocks until the kernel pool is initialised. A short or interrupted read is retried until n bytes are filled. An n of 0 returns an empty slice. Panics if the generator reports an error, because continuing without secure random bytes would be unsafe.
struct Aead { pub key_size: i64 pub nonce_size: i64 pub tag_size: i64 pub seal: fn([]u8, []u8, []u8) -> []u8 pub open: fn([]u8, []u8, []u8) -> []u8 ! io.Error }

An authenticated cipher bound to a key, which seals and opens messages. Built by aes_gcm, chacha20_poly1305 or xchacha20_poly1305. A nonce must not be reused with the same key. The length in bytes of the key the cipher was built from. The length in bytes of the nonce seal and open expect. The length in bytes of the authentication tag seal appends to the ciphertext. Encrypts and authenticates a message. The arguments are the nonce, the plaintext and the additional data. The additional data is authenticated but neither encrypted nor included in the output. Returns the ciphertext followed by the tag, plaintext.len + tag_size bytes. Verifies and decrypts a sealed message. The arguments are the nonce, the ciphertext followed by the tag, and the additional data. Returns the plaintext, tag_size bytes shorter than the sealed input. Fails with io.Error.Invalid when the sealed input is shorter than the tag, the tag does not match or the nonce length is not accepted by the cipher. The tag is compared in constant time and no plaintext is returned on failure.
An expanded AES encryption key with the lookup tables used to encrypt 16-byte blocks (FIPS 197).
The decryption key schedule and lookup tables derived from an Aes key, used to decrypt 16-byte blocks (FIPS 197).
Returns the decryption schedule matching the encryption key a.
Returns the encryption of the 16-byte block as a new 16-byte slice, applying the raw block cipher with no chaining or padding.
fn encrypt_block_into(a: *Aes, src: []u8, from: i64, dst: []u8, to: i64)
Encrypts the 16-byte block of src at offset from and writes the 16-byte result into dst at offset to. Applies the raw block cipher with no chaining or padding. src and dst may be the same slice.
Returns the decryption of the 16-byte block as a new 16-byte slice, applying the raw block cipher with no chaining or padding.
fn decrypt_block_into(a: *AesInverse, src: []u8, from: i64, dst: []u8, to: i64)
Decrypts the 16-byte block of src at offset from and writes the 16-byte result into dst at offset to. Applies the raw block cipher with no chaining or padding. src and dst may be the same slice.
Builds an AES encryption key from key. key is 16 bytes (AES-128) or 32 bytes (AES-256). Fails with io.Error.Invalid for any other length, including 24; aes_key accepts 24.

Returns an AES-GCM Aead keyed with key (NIST SP 800-38D). key is 16 bytes (AES-128) or 32 bytes (AES-256); fails with io.Error.Invalid for any other length. The tag is 16 bytes and nonce_size is 12. A 12-byte nonce is used directly; seal and open also accept other nonce lengths, which are hashed with GHASH as the standard defines. open fails with io.Error.Invalid when the sealed input is shorter than 16 bytes or the tag does not match.
Builds an AES encryption key from key. key is 16, 24 or 32 bytes (AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256). Fails with io.Error.Invalid for any other length.
Returns the 64-byte ChaCha20 block function output for block counter (RFC 8439 section 2.3). key is 32 bytes and nonce is 12 bytes. The lengths are not validated.

Returns a ChaCha20-Poly1305 Aead keyed with the 32-byte key (RFC 8439 section 2.8). The nonce is 12 bytes and the tag is 16 bytes. Fails with io.Error.Invalid when key is not 32 bytes. seal requires a 12-byte nonce. open fails with io.Error.Invalid when the nonce is not 12 bytes, the sealed input is shorter than 16 bytes or the tag does not match.
fn chacha20_xor(key: []u8, counter: u32, nonce: []u8, data: []u8) -> []u8 ! io.Error

Returns data XORed with the ChaCha20 keystream that starts at block counter (RFC 8439 section 2.4). key is 32 bytes and nonce is 12 bytes. Encryption and decryption are the same operation, and the result is as long as data. Fails with io.Error.Invalid when key or nonce has the wrong length. No authentication is applied.

Returns the 32-byte HChaCha20 subkey derived from key and nonce (draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha section 2.2). key is 32 bytes and nonce is 16 bytes. Fails with io.Error.Invalid when either has the wrong length.

Computes the Poly1305 one-time authenticator of message (RFC 8439 section 2.5). key is 32 bytes and must authenticate one message only. Returns the 16-byte tag. Fails with io.Error.Invalid when key is not 32 bytes. An empty message is accepted.

Returns an XChaCha20-Poly1305 Aead keyed with the 32-byte key (draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha). The nonce is 24 bytes and the tag is 16 bytes. The first 16 nonce bytes derive a subkey with hchacha20; the last 8 bytes, preceded by four zero bytes, form the ChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce. Fails with io.Error.Invalid when key is not 32 bytes. seal requires a 24-byte nonce. open fails with io.Error.Invalid when the nonce is not 24 bytes, the sealed input is shorter than 16 bytes or the tag does not match.
The failure of a BLAKE3 operation. The key is not 32 bytes.
An incremental BLAKE3 hash computation. Created by hasher, keyed_hasher or derive_key_hasher, fed with update and read with finalize or finalize_at.
Returns an independent copy of h with the same mode and input so far.
Returns the first length bytes of the extendable output of h. A length of 32 is the standard BLAKE3 hash. h is not modified.
fn finalize_at(h: *Hasher, offset: i64, length: i64) -> []u8

Returns length bytes of the extendable output of h, starting at byte offset. h is not modified, so the call can be repeated and more input can be added afterwards. offset and length must not be negative.
Appends data to the input of h. It can be called any number of times, and empty data has no effect.
Returns the hash.Algorithm for BLAKE3. The name is blake3, the digest is 32 bytes and the block size is 64 bytes.
fn derive_key(context: str, material: []u8, length: i64) -> []u8
Returns length bytes of key material derived from material under context with BLAKE3 key derivation mode.
Returns a Hasher in key derivation mode for context. The key material is fed with update. context should be a fixed string that is unique to the application and purpose.
Returns a Hasher in the default hash mode.
Returns the 32-byte BLAKE3 keyed hash of data under the 32-byte key. Fails with Error.BadKey when key is not 32 bytes.
Returns a Hasher in keyed hash mode with the 32-byte key. Fails with Error.BadKey when key is not 32 bytes.
Returns the 32-byte BLAKE3 hash of data.
Returns length bytes of the BLAKE3 extendable output for data in the default hash mode.
An AES key prepared for encrypting and decrypting 16-byte blocks, used by the CBC and CTR modes.
enum Error { InvalidKey InvalidIv InvalidLength InvalidPadding }

The failure of a block cipher mode operation. The key length is not valid for the cipher. The IV, initial counter block or tweak is not 16 bytes. The data length is not valid for the mode. The PKCS#7 padding is malformed.
A pair of AES keys, one for the data and one for the tweak, used by XTS mode.

Decrypts data in CBC mode with the 16-byte iv (NIST SP 800-38A). No padding is removed, so data must be a multiple of 16 bytes; empty input returns an empty slice. The result is as long as data. Fails with Error.InvalidIv when iv is not 16 bytes and Error.InvalidLength when data is not a multiple of 16 bytes. CBC does not authenticate the data.

Encrypts data in CBC mode with the 16-byte iv (NIST SP 800-38A). No padding is applied, so data must be a multiple of 16 bytes; empty input returns an empty slice. The result is as long as data. Fails with Error.InvalidIv when iv is not 16 bytes and Error.InvalidLength when data is not a multiple of 16 bytes.

Decrypts ciphertext in CBC mode with the 16-byte iv and removes the PKCS#7 padding. Fails with Error.InvalidLength when ciphertext is empty or not a multiple of 16 bytes, Error.InvalidIv when iv is not 16 bytes, and Error.InvalidPadding when the padding is malformed. CBC does not authenticate the data.

Pads plaintext with PKCS#7 and encrypts it in CBC mode with the 16-byte iv. The result is plaintext.len rounded up to the next multiple of 16, so empty input returns 16 bytes. Fails with Error.InvalidIv when iv is not 16 bytes.

Returns data XORed with the AES-CTR keystream (NIST SP 800-38A). iv is the 16-byte initial counter block. The block is incremented as a 128-bit big-endian integer after each 16 bytes of keystream. Encryption and decryption are the same operation, and the result is as long as data. Fails with Error.InvalidIv when iv is not 16 bytes. CTR does not authenticate the data.

Decrypts data in XTS mode under the 16-byte tweak, usually the sector number. data must be at least 16 bytes. A length that is not a multiple of 16 uses ciphertext stealing. The result is as long as data. Fails with Error.InvalidIv when tweak is not 16 bytes and Error.InvalidLength when data is shorter than 16 bytes.

Encrypts data in XTS mode under the 16-byte tweak, usually the sector number. data must be at least 16 bytes. A length that is not a multiple of 16 uses ciphertext stealing. The result is as long as data. Fails with Error.InvalidIv when tweak is not 16 bytes and Error.InvalidLength when data is shorter than 16 bytes.
Returns a Block for key. key is 16, 24 or 32 bytes (AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256, FIPS 197). Fails with Error.InvalidKey for any other length.

Returns data extended with PKCS#7 padding to a multiple of block_size (RFC 5652 section 6.1). Appends between 1 and block_size bytes, each holding the pad length, so input that already fills whole blocks gains a full block of padding. block_size must be between 1 and 255; this is not checked.

Returns data without its PKCS#7 padding. The result shares memory with data. Fails with Error.InvalidPadding when block_size is outside 1 to 255, data is empty, its length is not a multiple of block_size, or the pad length or pad bytes are invalid.
Returns an Xts for key (IEEE 1619). key is the data key followed by the tweak key, 32 bytes for AES-128 or 64 bytes for AES-256. Fails with Error.InvalidKey for any other length.

An element of the prime field GF(2^255 - 19) in five 51-bit limbs, least significant limb first. Operations return limbs below 2^52 and the type has no canonical form until to_bytes, so compare values with equal rather than field by field.
fn add(a: Fe, b: Fe) -> Fe
Returns the sum a + b modulo 2^255 - 19.
fn choose(a: Fe, b: Fe, choice: u64) -> Fe
Returns b when choice is 1 and a when it is 0, without branching on choice. choice must be 0 or 1; any other value mixes the limbs of both inputs.
fn equal(a: Fe, b: Fe) -> bool
Reports whether a and b encode the same field element. Both are reduced to canonical bytes and compared without an early exit.
Returns the multiplicative inverse z^(p - 2) modulo p = 2^255 - 19. The inverse of zero is zero. The exponentiation is a fixed sequence of squarings and multiplications, independent of the value.
Returns 1 when the canonical encoding of f has its low bit set and 0 otherwise.
fn mul(f: Fe, g: Fe) -> Fe
Returns the product f * g modulo 2^255 - 19.
Returns z^((p - 5) / 8) modulo p = 2^255 - 19, the exponentiation used to take square roots when decompressing Ed25519 points.
Returns the square f * f modulo 2^255 - 19.
fn sub(a: Fe, b: Fe) -> Fe
Returns the difference a - b modulo 2^255 - 19.
fn swap(mut a: Fe, mut b: Fe, choice: u64)
Exchanges a and b when choice is 1 and leaves them unchanged when it is 0, without branching on choice. choice must be 0 or 1.
Encodes the element as 32 little-endian bytes in canonical form, fully reduced below 2^255 - 19.

Returns k cut or padded to 32 bytes and clamped as a Curve25519 scalar (RFC 7748 section 5): the low three bits and the top bit cleared and the second-highest bit set. A shorter k is padded with zero bytes before clamping.

Decodes 32 little-endian bytes into an element. Bit 255 is ignored, so the top bit of the last byte never contributes. A value in [2^255 - 19, 2^255) is accepted and reduces modulo 2^255 - 19. The slice must hold at least 32 bytes.
fn limbs(l0: u64, l1: u64, l2: u64, l3: u64, l4: u64) -> Fe
Returns the element whose limbs are l0 (least significant) to l4. The limbs are used as given and are not reduced.
struct Der { pub data: []u8 pub at: i64 }
A cursor over DER encoded bytes. Made by reader. The bytes being read. The offset of the next element in data.
struct Element { pub tag: u8 pub content: []u8 pub raw: []u8 }

One DER element: a tag, its content and its complete encoding. The identifier octet, class and constructed bits included. The content octets, a slice of the input. The whole encoding, from the tag through the content, as a slice of the input.
Returns whether d has read all of its bytes.
Reads the next element, which must have the given tag, and returns a cursor over its content. Fails as expect does. Call finish on the result to require that the content was fully consumed.
fn expect(d: *Der, tag: u8) -> Element ! io.Error
Reads the next element and fails with Malformed when its tag is not tag.
Fails with Malformed unless d has read all of its bytes.
Returns the tag of the next element without consuming it, or -1 at the end of the data.

Reads the next element and advances past it. Fails with Malformed when the data is truncated, the length is indefinite, longer than 4 octets or not minimally encoded, or the content runs past the end, and with Unsupported for a multi-octet tag.

Reads the next element, which must be an INTEGER holding a non-negative value in minimal form, and returns its magnitude without the sign octet. The value zero returns an empty slice. The result is a slice of the input. Fails with Malformed when the tag is not 0x02, the content is empty or negative, or a leading zero octet is not needed to keep it positive.

Returns the Unix time in seconds of a UTCTime or GeneralizedTime element. Only the forms RFC 5280 section 4.1.2.5 allows are accepted: YYMMDDHHMMSSZ with two-digit years 50 to 99 meaning 1950 to 1999 and 00 to 49 meaning 2000 to 2049, and YYYYMMDDHHMMSSZ. Fails with Malformed for any other form or an invalid date or time.
The OBJECT IDENTIFIER of the named curve prime256v1 (NIST P-256) as dotted decimal text.
The OBJECT IDENTIFIER of the named curve secp384r1 (NIST P-384) as dotted decimal text.
Returns the bytes of a BIT STRING whose last octet has no unused bits. Fails with Malformed when the content is empty or its unused-bits count is not 0.
Returns the value of a DER BOOLEAN. Fails with Malformed unless the content is a single octet that is 0x00 or 0xFF.
Returns the DER encoding of an element with the given tag and content. The length is written in the short form below 128 and otherwise in the long form with as few octets as it needs.

Returns the DER INTEGER for the non-negative big-endian number magnitude. Leading zero octets are dropped, a zero octet is added when the top bit would otherwise mark the value negative, and an empty magnitude encodes zero.

Returns the set bits of a BIT STRING as an integer, where bit n of the string, counting from the most significant bit of the first octet, is bit n of the result. Fails with Malformed for empty content, an unused-bits count above 7, more than 8 octets of bits, or an unused bit that is set.

Returns an OBJECT IDENTIFIER as dotted decimal text such as 2.5.4.3. Fails with Malformed for empty content, an unterminated arc or an arc with a padding octet, and with Unsupported for an arc that does not fit in 48 bits.
Returns a cursor positioned at the start of data.
Returns a DER SEQUENCE whose content is parts joined in order. Each part is already encoded, for example by integer or encode.
Returns the value of a non-negative DER INTEGER with at most 7 content octets. Fails with Malformed for an empty or longer content, a negative value or a non-minimal encoding.
Returns the big-endian number magnitude without its leading zero bytes. Returns an empty slice when magnitude is empty or all zero. The result shares the memory of magnitude.
fn whole(data: []u8, tag: u8) -> Element ! io.Error
Returns the single element with the given tag that makes up all of data. Fails with Malformed when the tag differs or bytes follow the element.
struct Coordinates { pub x: []u8 pub y: []u8 }
The affine coordinates of an uncompressed point. The x coordinate as big-endian bytes, scalar_size long. The y coordinate as big-endian bytes, scalar_size long.
An elliptic curve supported by the module. NIST P-256 (secp256r1, FIPS 186-4), with 32-byte scalars and field elements. NIST P-384 (secp384r1, FIPS 186-4), with 48-byte scalars and field elements.
struct Key { pub curve: Curve pub private: []u8 pub public: []u8 }

A parsed SEC1 elliptic curve private key together with its public point. The curve the key belongs to. The private scalar as big-endian bytes, 32 for P-256 or 48 for P-384. The public point in uncompressed SEC1 form, 0x04 || X || Y, 65 bytes for P-256 or 97 for P-384.
Returns the coordinates of the uncompressed SEC1 point point, or none when it is not 0x04 followed by two scalar_size(curve) byte coordinates. The point is not checked to lie on the curve.
fn ecdh(curve: Curve, private: []u8, peer: []u8) -> []u8 ! io.Error

Computes ECDH (the shared secret Z of SEC 1 and NIST SP 800-56A) between private and the peer point peer. Returns the affine x coordinate of the shared point as big-endian bytes, 32 for P-256 or 48 for P-384. The bytes are not hashed. peer must be an uncompressed SEC1 point, 0x04 || X || Y, on the curve with both coordinates below the field prime. Fails with Invalid when peer does not meet that, when private is the wrong size or outside [1, n - 1], or when the shared point is the point at infinity.
Returns a new private scalar for curve as big-endian bytes, 32 for P-256 or 48 for P-384. The scalar is drawn from crypto.random and redrawn until it lies in [1, n - 1], where n is the group order.

Returns the public point for private in uncompressed SEC1 form, 0x04 || X || Y, 65 bytes for P-256 or 97 for P-384. Fails with Invalid when private is not exactly the curve's scalar size or is not in [1, n - 1].
Returns the size in bytes of a scalar, a field element and so of each coordinate of a point on curve: 32 for P-256, 48 for P-384.
fn sign(curve: Curve, private: []u8, digest: []u8) -> []u8 ! io.Error
Signs digest like sign_raw and returns the signature as an ASN.1 DER Ecdsa-Sig-Value, SEQUENCE { r INTEGER, s INTEGER }. Fails with Invalid under the same conditions as sign_raw.
fn sign_raw(curve: Curve, private: []u8, digest: []u8) -> []u8 ! io.Error

Signs digest with ECDSA (FIPS 186-4) and returns the raw signature r || s, each half big-endian and padded to the scalar size, 64 bytes for P-256 or 96 for P-384. The nonce is deterministic (RFC 6979), with HMAC over SHA-512, SHA-384 or SHA-256 chosen by digest.len (64, 48, otherwise 32), so signing the same digest with the same key gives the same signature. digest is the hash of the message, not the message. A digest longer than the scalar size is truncated to its leftmost bytes. Fails with Invalid when private is the wrong size or outside [1, n - 1].
Returns the uncompressed SEC1 point 0x04 || x || y for the coordinates x and y, or none when either is not exactly scalar_size(curve) bytes. The point is not checked to lie on the curve.
fn verify(curve: Curve, public: []u8, digest: []u8, signature: []u8) -> bool

Reports whether the DER-encoded signature is a valid ECDSA signature of digest under the public point public. signature is a SEQUENCE of two minimally encoded, non-negative INTEGERs with no trailing bytes; any other encoding returns false. public is an uncompressed SEC1 point. Returns false, never an error, for an invalid point or a mismatch.
fn verify_raw(curve: Curve, public: []u8, digest: []u8, signature: []u8) -> bool

Reports whether signature is a valid ECDSA signature of digest under the public point public. signature is the raw form r || s produced by sign_raw and must be exactly twice the scalar size. public is an uncompressed SEC1 point. Returns false, never an error, for a wrong-sized or out-of-range signature, an invalid point, or a mismatch. A digest longer than the scalar size is truncated to its leftmost bytes.
Returns the curve whose named-curve OBJECT IDENTIFIER is the dotted text oid, such as 1.2.840.10045.3.1.7, or none for any other.

Parses a DER SEC1 ECPrivateKey (RFC 5915) into a Key. The key must have version 1. The curve comes from the optional [0] named-curve OID, prime256v1 or secp384r1; when the OID is absent it is inferred from the private key length, 32 or 48 bytes. The optional [1] public key must be an uncompressed point and is checked against the point computed from the private scalar. public in the result is always the computed point. Fails with Malformed for DER that does not follow this layout or has trailing bytes. Fails with Invalid for an unsupported curve, a private key that is not a valid scalar for the curve, or a public key that does not match.
Returns a new 32-byte Ed25519 seed, the private key, from random in std/crypto.
Returns the 32-byte Ed25519 public key for the 32-byte seed (RFC 8032). The length of seed is not validated.

Returns the 64-byte Ed25519 signature of message under the 32-byte seed (RFC 8032 section 5.1). The signature is the 32-byte encoded point R followed by the 32-byte scalar S. Signing is deterministic: the same seed and message give the same signature. The length of seed is not validated.

Returns whether signature is a valid Ed25519 signature of message under the 32-byte public key (RFC 8032 section 5.1.7). Returns false when signature is not 64 bytes, S is not below the group order, or public does not decode to a curve point. Otherwise it compares the encoding of [S]B - [k]A with R.
struct Algorithm { pub name: str pub size: i64 pub block: i64 pub digest: fn() -> Digest }

A hash function: its name, sizes and a constructor for running computations. The lowercase name of the algorithm, such as sha256. The digest length in bytes. The internal block length in bytes that HMAC pads the key to. For SHA-3 it is the sponge rate. Starts a new Digest with empty input.
struct Digest { pub update: fn([]u8) pub finish: fn() -> []u8 pub clone: fn() -> Digest }

A running hash computation, a copyable struct of closures over the hash state. Feeds bytes into the hash. Returns the digest of the bytes fed so far. The state is not consumed, so more bytes can be fed afterwards. Returns an independent Digest with the same state.
struct Keyed { pub inner: Digest pub outer: Digest }
The two digests of an HMAC (RFC 2104) keyed with one key, each already fed its padded key block. The digest to feed the message into. The digest to feed the finished inner digest into.
fn hkdf_expand(a: Algorithm, prk: []u8, info: []u8, length: i64) -> []u8

Computes HKDF-Expand (RFC 5869 section 2.3) from the pseudorandom key prk and context info. Returns length bytes. length must not exceed 255 * a.size because the block counter is one byte; this is not checked. A length of 0 or less returns an empty slice.
Computes HKDF-Extract (RFC 5869 section 2.2) over the input keying material ikm. Returns the a.size-byte pseudorandom key. An empty salt is replaced by a.size zero bytes.

Computes the HMAC of message under key with the hash a (RFC 2104, FIPS 198-1). Returns a.size bytes. A key longer than a.block is hashed first and a shorter one is padded with zeros. Any key length is accepted, including empty.

Returns the keyed inner and outer digests of the HMAC of key with the hash a. A key longer than a.block is hashed first and a shorter one is padded with zeros. Any key length is accepted, including empty. Clone the digests to compute several MACs under one key.
Returns the digest of data under the algorithm a, a.size bytes long.

Returns whether a and b hold the same bytes. Slices of different lengths are unequal and return at once. For equal lengths the running time does not depend on the contents, so the call is suitable for comparing MACs and tags.

Returns the Algorithm for SHA-1 (FIPS 180-4). The name is sha1, the digest is 20 bytes and the block size is 64 bytes. SHA-1 is not collision resistant; use it only where a protocol requires it, such as HMAC-SHA-1 or the WebSocket handshake.
Returns the Algorithm for SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4). The name is sha256, the digest is 32 bytes and the block size is 64 bytes.
Returns the Algorithm for SHA-384 (FIPS 180-4). The name is sha384, the digest is 48 bytes and the block size is 128 bytes.
Returns the Algorithm for SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4). The name is sha512, the digest is 64 bytes and the block size is 128 bytes.
struct Claims { pub iss: str? pub sub: str? pub aud: []str pub exp: i64? pub nbf: i64? pub iat: i64? pub jti: str? pub extra: json.Value }

The registered claims of a JSON Web Token (RFC 7519), parsed from the payload. The issuer (iss), or none when absent. The subject (sub), or none when absent. The audience (aud), as a list whether the token carried a string or an array. Empty when absent. The expiry time (exp) in Unix seconds, or none when absent. The time before which the token is not valid (nbf) in Unix seconds, or none when absent. The issue time (iat) in Unix seconds, or none when absent. The token identifier (jti), or none when absent. The whole payload object, including the registered claims, for reading custom claims.
struct Jwk { pub kid: str pub key: Key pub alg: str }

A JSON Web Key (RFC 7517) with the metadata used to select it. The key identifier (kid), or the empty string when the key has none. The key material. The algorithm the key is restricted to (alg), or the empty string when it may be used with any algorithm its type suits.
enum Key { Hmac([]u8) Rsa(rsa.PublicKey, rsa.PrivateKey?) Ec(ecdsa.Curve, []u8, []u8?) Ed([]u8, []u8?) }

The key material of a JSON Web Key. A shared secret for the HMAC algorithms (kty of oct). An RSA key (kty of RSA): the public key and, when the JWK carries all of d, p, q, dp, dq and qi, the private key. An elliptic curve key (kty of EC, curve P-256 or P-384): the public point as an uncompressed SEC 1 encoding (0x04 followed by x and y) and, when present, the private scalar d. An Ed25519 key (kty of OKP, crv of Ed25519): the 32-byte public key and, when present, the 32-byte private seed.
struct Options { pub algorithms: []str pub issuer: str pub audience: str pub leeway: i64 pub now: i64 }

The checks verify applies to a token. The alg values to accept, such as ["ES256"]. An empty list accepts no token. The required iss. The empty string, the default, skips the check. The value that must appear in aud. The empty string, the default, skips the check. The clock skew in seconds tolerated on exp and nbf. Defaults to 60. The current time in Unix seconds. 0, the default, reads the system clock.

Returns the JSON text of the public part of k. Private members (d and the RSA primes) are never written. An HMAC key writes its secret k; use jwks_json to publish a set without symmetric keys. The use member is always sig, and kid and alg are written when not empty.
Returns the names of the public key signature algorithms that sign and verify_jws support:RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384 and EdDSA.
Returns the JSON text of a JWK Set holding the public parts of keys. HMAC keys are left out so a shared secret is never published. Private members are never written.

Parses a JWK Set (RFC 7517 section 5) or a single JWK from JSON text. A top-level object with a keys member is read as a set; any other object is read as one key. Keys that cannot be used are skipped, not reported: an unsupported kty or curve, a use other than sig, a missing member, malformed Base64url or a coordinate of the wrong length. Leading zero bytes of RSA integers are stripped. Fails with Malformed when the text is not JSON, is not an object, or has a keys member that is not an array.
fn sign(alg: str, kid: str, key: Key, payload: json.Value) -> str ! io.Error

Returns the compact JWS (RFC 7515) of payload signed with key under the algorithm alg. The result is header.payload.signature, each part Base64url without padding. The header holds alg, typ of JWT and, when kid is not empty, kid. The payload is the compact JSON of payload. Supported algorithms are HS256, HS384, HS512, RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384 and EdDSA (RFC 7518, RFC 8037). ECDSA signatures are the fixed-width r and s concatenation, not DER. Fails with Invalid when alg is not supported, the key type does not suit it, the key has no private part, an HMAC secret is shorter than the hash output or an Ed25519 seed is not 32 bytes.
Returns the kid in the header of the compact JWS token. Returns the empty string when the header has no kid or token has no header that verify_jws could read. The signature is not checked.
fn verify(token: str, keys: []Jwk, options: Options) -> Claims ! io.Error

Verifies a signed JWT and returns its claims. The signature is checked with verify_jws. The payload must be a JSON object without repeated members. The token is rejected when exp is present and the time, less leeway, has reached it; when nbf is present and the time, plus leeway, is before it; when options.issuer is set and iss differs; or when options.audience is set and aud does not contain it. A token with no exp does not expire. iat is parsed but not checked. Fails with Malformed when the token, payload or a registered claim has the wrong shape, and with Invalid when the signature or any check fails.
fn verify_jws(token: str, keys: []Jwk, algorithms: []str) -> []u8 ! io.Error

Verifies the compact JWS token against keys and returns its decoded payload. Only an alg named in algorithms is accepted, so the caller, not the token, chooses the algorithms. A key is tried when its kid matches the header's (or either has none) and its alg is empty or equal to the header's, and its type suits the algorithm. The first key whose signature verifies wins. HMAC comparison is constant-time. Fails with Malformed when the token does not have three Base64url parts, the header is not a JSON object or repeats a member, or alg or kid is not a string. Fails with Invalid when the header has a crit member, the algorithm is not allowed or supported, or no key verifies the signature. The payload is not parsed.

Sets out to a + b over the limbs of out, least significant limb first, and returns the final carry as 0 or 1. a and b must have at least as many limbs as out. out can be the same slice as a. The running time does not depend on the values.
fn add_masked(out: []u64, x: []u64, mask: u64) -> u64
Adds x to out in place wherever mask is all ones, and returns the final carry as 0 or 1. mask is 0 to add nothing or all ones to add x. x must have at least as many limbs as out.
fn blend(mask: u64, a: u64, b: u64) -> u64
Returns a where mask is all ones and b where it is 0.
fn borrow(a: u64, b: u64, diff: u64) -> u64
Returns the borrow out of the 64-bit subtraction a - b whose wrapped result is diff, as 0 or 1.
fn carry(a: u64, b: u64, sum: u64) -> u64
Returns the carry out of the 64-bit addition a + b whose wrapped result is sum, as 0 or 1.
fn choose(out: []u64, a: []u64, b: []u64, mask: u64)
Sets each limb of out to the matching limb of a where mask is all ones and of b where it is 0. a and b must have at least as many limbs as out.
Returns whether a and b hold the same limbs, comparing all of them. b must have at least as many limbs as a. The running time does not depend on the values.
Returns data, read as a big-endian integer, as k limbs, least significant limb first. Bytes above the top limb are dropped and a short data is padded with zeros.
Ors the limbs of row into out wherever mask is all ones, for a table lookup that reads every row. row must have at least as many limbs as out.
Returns whether every limb of a is zero, comparing all of them.
Returns the mask that is all ones when bit is 1 and 0 when it is 0.
fn same(a: u64, b: u64) -> u64
Returns 1 when a equals b and 0 otherwise, without a branch that depends on the values.

Sets out to a - b over the limbs of out, least significant limb first, and returns the final borrow as 0 or 1. a and b must have at least as many limbs as out. out can be the same slice as a. The running time does not depend on the values.
Returns the low size bytes of x as a big-endian integer, padded with zeros above the top limb.
Returns the hash.Algorithm for MD5 (RFC 1321). The name is md5, the digest is 16 bytes and the block size is 64 bytes. MD5 is not collision resistant; use it only where a protocol requires it.
Returns the 16-byte MD5 digest of data (RFC 1321).
struct Encapsulated { pub ciphertext: []u8 pub shared: []u8 }

The result of encapsulation: a ciphertext for the key holder and the shared secret that goes with it. The ciphertext, 768, 1088 or 1568 bytes for ML-KEM-512, -768 and -1024. The shared secret, always 32 bytes.
struct Keys { pub encapsulation: []u8 pub decapsulation: []u8 }

An ML-KEM key pair in the byte encodings of FIPS 203. The encapsulation (public) key, ek, 800, 1184 or 1568 bytes for ML-KEM-512, -768 and -1024. The decapsulation (private) key, dk, 1632, 2400 or 3168 bytes for ML-KEM-512, -768 and -1024. It carries the encapsulation key, its SHA3-256 hash and the implicit rejection value z.

An ML-KEM parameter set (FIPS 203). ML-KEM-512: encapsulation key 800 bytes, decapsulation key 1632 bytes, ciphertext 768 bytes. ML-KEM-768: encapsulation key 1184 bytes, decapsulation key 2400 bytes, ciphertext 1088 bytes. ML-KEM-1024: encapsulation key 1568 bytes, decapsulation key 3168 bytes, ciphertext 1568 bytes.
fn decapsulate(level: Level, dk: []u8, ciphertext: []u8) -> []u8 ! io.Error

Recovers the 32-byte shared secret from ciphertext with the decapsulation key dk (ML-KEM.Decaps, FIPS 203). Fails with Invalid when dk or ciphertext has the wrong length for level, or when the hash of the encapsulation key embedded in dk does not match the stored hash. A ciphertext that was not produced for this key does not fail: the result is then a pseudorandom 32-byte value derived from the rejection value z and the ciphertext (implicit rejection), and the comparison that selects it runs without branching on secret data.
fn encapsulate(level: Level, ek: []u8) -> Encapsulated ! io.Error

Encapsulates a fresh shared secret to the encapsulation key ek, drawing the 32-byte message from crypto.random (ML-KEM.Encaps, FIPS 203). Fails with Invalid when ek has the wrong length for level or fails the coefficient range check.
fn encapsulate_seeded(level: Level, ek: []u8, m: []u8) -> Encapsulated ! io.Error
