The kind of the token a Reader is at. No token: the reader has not read yet, or has reached the end of the document. {. }. [. ]. An object member name, which get_string reads. A string value, which get_string reads. A number, which get_i64, get_u64 and get_f64 read. The literal true. The literal false. The literal null.
enum Value { Null Bool(bool) Int(i64) Float(f64) Str(str) Array([]Value) Object([]Member) }

A JSON value (RFC 8259) held in memory. parse builds one and stringify writes one. The literal null. The literal true or false. A number written without a fraction or exponent that fits an i64. Any other number: one with a fraction or an exponent, or an integer outside the i64 range. A string, with its escapes decoded. An array, in order. An object, as members in the order they appear. Names may repeat; the lookup functions use the first.

A JSON text builder that appends to an internal buffer, made by writer. Call start_object, property, the value functions and end_object in document order, then read the text with written_text or written_bytes. Commas, colons and indentation are added automatically. Strings are escaped: " and \ with a backslash, newline, carriage return and tab as \n, \r and \t, and the other control characters below 0x20 as \u00XX. Everything else, including non-ASCII text and /, is written as it is; the text is not checked for UTF-8. The writer does not check that calls form a valid document.

Returns the number of containers that are open at the current token. After a StartObject or StartArray it counts that container, and after the matching end token it does not. It is 0 at the top level.
Returns the value of the current True or False token. Fails with serde.Error.Mismatch when the token is neither.
Returns the current Number token as an f64. Fails with serde.Error.Mismatch when the token is not a number.
Returns the current Number token as an i64. Fails with serde.Error.Mismatch when the token is not a number, or the number has a fraction or exponent, and with Range when it does not fit an i64.

Returns the string of the current String or PropertyName token with its escapes decoded. A \u surrogate pair becomes one character and a lone surrogate becomes U+FFFD. Fails with serde.Error.Mismatch when the token is neither. The string views the input when it has no escapes.

Returns the current Number token as a u64. Fails with serde.Error.Mismatch when the token is not a number, or the number is negative or has a fraction or exponent, and with Range when it does not fit a u64.
Returns the byte offset in the input that the reader has reached, just past the current token, or past the colon for a PropertyName. Errors report it.

Advances to the next token and returns true, or returns false once the top-level value has been read completely and only whitespace remains, leaving the token as None. An object member is two tokens, PropertyName and then the value. Fails with serde.Error.Syntax at the byte offset of malformed input, for example an unexpected character, a trailing comma, a bad escape, a control character or invalid UTF-8 in a string, an unterminated string, a number with a leading zero, an unexpected end of data or data after the top-level value, and with TooDeep when containers nest deeper than the reader allows.

Skips the current value. When the token is a PropertyName it skips the member's value; when the value is an object or array it reads through to the matching end token, and the end token becomes current. For other tokens it does nothing. Fails like read.
Returns the kind of the current token, or None before the first read and at the end of the document.

Returns the raw bytes of the current token as a view of the input: the text of a number or literal, the bracket of a container token, and, for a string or name, the characters between the quotes with any escapes still undecoded.
fn at(v: Value, index: i64) -> Value?
Returns the element of the array v at index, or none when v is not an array or index is out of range, including a negative index.
fn equal(a: Value, b: Value) -> bool

Returns whether a and b are equal as JSON values. An Int equals a Float of the same numeric value. Objects are equal when they have the same members regardless of order, and arrays when they have equal elements in the same order. Values of different kinds are not equal, so Null equals only Null. A Float NaN equals nothing.
fn field(v: Value, name: str) -> Value
Returns the member name of the object v, or Null when v is not an object or has no such member. The first member with that name is used.
fn field_int(v: Value, name: str) -> i64?
Returns the integer member name of the object v, or none when v is not an object, has no such member, or the member is neither an integer nor a float. A floating point member is truncated.
fn field_text(v: Value, name: str) -> str?
Returns the string member name of the object v, or none when v is not an object, has no such member, or the member is not a string.
fn get(v: Value, name: str) -> Value?
Returns the value of the first member of the object v called name, or none when v is not an object or has no such member.
fn int_of(v: Value, name: str) -> i64
Returns the integer member name of the object v, or 0 where field_int gives none.
fn stringify(v: Value, indent: i64) -> str

Returns v as JSON text. indent is the number of spaces per nesting level; 0 writes compact text with no whitespace, and a positive value puts each member and element on its own line. A non-finite Float is written as null, since JSON has no representation for it. See Writer for the escaping of strings.
fn text_of(v: Value, name: str) -> str
Returns the string member name of the object v, or an empty string where field_text gives none.

Returns a serde.Writer that writes derived values as JSON through the Writer w, with field and variant names spelled as naming says. []u8 is written as a base64 string. A none is written as null. Maps are written as objects with their keys as they are. An enum variant without fields is its name as a string, and one with fields an object with a single member named by the variant. Use it to write a value with serde.write into a writer that already holds other output.
Writes x as a JSON number, or null when it is NaN or infinite, which JSON cannot represent.
Writes n as a JSON number.
Writes the name of the next member of the current object. The value that follows is that member's value.
Writes json into the output as it is, in the place of a value. The text is not checked or reindented, so it must be a complete valid JSON value.
Writes s as a JSON string.
Writes n as a JSON number.
Returns the bytes written so far. The slice views the writer's buffer, so it changes as more is written.
Returns the text written so far. The string views the writer's buffer, so it changes as more is written.
Returns a Member called name holding an array of items.
Returns a Member called name holding data as a Base64url string without padding.
fn bool_member(name: str, value: bool) -> Member
Returns a Member called name holding the boolean value.
Decodes the JSON text data into a T with default Options. See deserialize_with.
fn deserialize_with[T](data: []u8, options: Options) -> T ! serde.Error

Decodes the JSON text data into a T, as options says. The text must be one complete JSON value; data after it fails with serde.Error.Syntax. A struct is read from an object: unknown members are skipped, a missing member takes the field's default or none for an optional, and any other missing member fails with Missing. null reads as none. Integers must be written without a fraction or exponent, and a []u8 is read from a base64 string. An enum variant is read from a string or an object with one member. Failures are serde.Error: Syntax for malformed JSON, Mismatch for a value of the wrong type, Range for a number that does not fit, TooDeep and UnknownVariant.
fn int_member(name: str, value: i64) -> Member
Returns a Member called name holding the integer value.
fn member(name: str, value: Value) -> Member
Returns the Member called name holding value.
Returns a Member called name holding an object made of members.
Returns an object made of members as a Value.

Parses data as one JSON text into a Value. The input is UTF-8 and follows RFC 8259 strictly: no comments, no trailing commas, no leading zeros, no control characters in strings, and invalid UTF-8 is rejected. A leading byte order mark and whitespace around the value are accepted. A number without a fraction or exponent that fits an i64 becomes Int, any other number Float. A lone surrogate escape in a string becomes U+FFFD. Duplicate member names are kept. Nesting deeper than 64 fails with serde.Error.TooDeep. Other failures, including empty input and data after the value, are serde.Error.Syntax at the byte offset of the problem.
Returns a reader over data, which is not copied. A leading UTF-8 byte order mark is skipped. Nesting deeper than 64 containers fails with serde.Error.TooDeep.
fn rename(name: str, naming: Naming) -> str
Returns name spelled as naming says, the conversion that serialize_with applies to field names and variant names.
Returns v as compact JSON text, with default Options.
fn serialize_with[T](v: T, options: Options) -> str

Returns v as JSON text, as options says. A struct becomes an object of its fields, a map an object, a slice an array, an optional null or its value, and []u8 a base64 string. An enum variant without fields becomes a string, and a variant with fields an object with one member named by the variant, holding an object of its labelled fields or an array of its positional ones. Non-finite floats become null.

Returns a serde.Reader over the JSON text data, to pass to serde.read. Names are matched as they are, the nesting limit is 64, and data after the first value is not checked. Failures are reported as serde.Errors.
fn text_member(name: str, value: str) -> Member
Returns a Member called name holding the string value.
Returns the string value as a Value.

Returns an empty writer. indent is the number of spaces per nesting level. With 0 the text is compact, with no whitespace. With a positive value each member and element starts on its own line and a space follows each colon.
enum Error { Malformed(i64, str) Pointer(i64, pointer.Error) TestFailed(i64, str) }

The error returned by apply. Each variant carries the zero-based index of the operation that failed. An operation is not valid: it is not an object, op or path is missing or not a string, value or from is missing, op is unknown, or a move targets a location inside its own source. index is -1 when the patch itself is not an array. The operation's pointer is invalid or does not fit the document; cause is the pointer.Error. A test operation found a value different from the expected one. path is the tested pointer.
fn apply(doc: json.Value, patch: json.Value) -> json.Value ! Error

Applies the RFC 6902 patch to doc and returns the new document. patch is an array of operations, applied in order, each an object with op and path. add, replace and test also take value; move and copy take from. remove, replace, move and copy need an existing source or target; test compares with json.equal. Extra members are ignored. Moving a value onto its own location changes nothing. The patch is atomic: doc is never changed, and a failure reports the first operation that failed. Fails with Malformed, Pointer or TestFailed.
fn diff(a: json.Value, b: json.Value) -> json.Value

Returns an RFC 6902 patch that turns a into b, so that apply(a, diff(a, b)) equals b. Equal values give an empty patch. Objects are compared member by member, with remove operations and nested changes in the order of a's members followed by add operations for new members. Arrays are compared element by element: shared positions are diffed, extra elements of a are removed from the end backwards and extra elements of b are added at the end. Values of different kinds, and scalars that differ, become a replace. Only add, remove and replace are produced.
fn merge_diff(a: json.Value, b: json.Value) -> json.Value

Returns an RFC 7396 merge patch that turns a into b, so that merge_patch(a, diff) equals b. When a and b are both objects the result is an object of the changes: a member that b lacks becomes null, new members are copied and changed ones are diffed recursively; otherwise it is b. Equal objects give an empty object. A merge patch cannot set a member to null, so the result is only exact when b has no null members.
fn merge_patch(target: json.Value, patch: json.Value) -> json.Value

Applies the RFC 7396 merge patch to target and returns the result. When patch is not an object it replaces target. Otherwise each member of patch is merged into target, which is treated as an empty object when it is not an object: a null member removes that member of the target, and any other value is merged recursively. Arrays are replaced as a whole. Neither argument is changed.

The error returned when a JSONPath query is invalid (RFC 9535). The query text is not a valid JSONPath query. at is the byte offset in the query where the problem is and message describes it, for example an unknown function, a comparison of a query that is not singular, or a literal outside the exact integer range.
struct Node { pub value: json.Value pub path: str }

A value selected by a query, with its location. The selected value. The normalised path of the value in the queried document, such as $['store']['book'][0]. Member names are single-quoted with \', \\ and control characters escaped, and array elements are written by index.
A compiled JSONPath query, made by compile. A Path can be used with query on any number of documents.

Compiles the JSONPath query source (RFC 9535). The query starts with $ and holds segments: .name, .*, .. for descendants, and bracketed selectors that are names, *, indexes, slices start:end:step and filters ?expr. A filter takes comparisons, existence tests, &&, ||, !, nested queries starting with @ or $, and the functions length, count, match, search and value. Fails with Syntax for anything else, including a malformed filter, wrong function arguments, a leading zero in an integer or a bare literal used as a test.
fn find(v: json.Value, source: str) -> []Node ! Error
Compiles source and returns the nodes it selects from v. Fails with Syntax when the query is invalid. See compile and query.
Returns the normalised paths of nodes, in order.

Returns the nodes that p selects from v, in the order the query produces them. Each node carries its normalised path. A node can appear more than once when several selectors or segments reach it, and an empty result means nothing matched. A missing member or an index out of range selects nothing and is not an error.
Returns the values of nodes, in order.
enum Error { Syntax(i64, str) NotFound(str) Mismatch(str) CannotRemoveRoot }

The error returned by the pointer functions (RFC 6901). The pointer text is malformed. at is the byte offset in the text where the problem is and message describes it. The pointer is well formed but the value it names does not exist: an object has no such member or an array no such index. pointer is the prefix of the pointer up to and including the token that failed. A token does not suit the value it is applied to: the value is a string, number, boolean or null, or an array and the token is not an array index. pointer is the prefix up to and including the token. A removal named the whole document with the empty pointer.
fn add(doc: json.Value, pointer: str, value: json.Value) -> json.Value ! Error

Returns a copy of doc with value added at pointer, as the RFC 6902 add operation does. On an object the member is replaced when it exists and added at the end otherwise. On an array the value is inserted before the element at the index, which shifts the later elements, and an index equal to the length or - appends. The empty pointer returns value. The parent of the target must exist. doc is not changed. Fails with Syntax, NotFound or Mismatch as get does, and with NotFound for an array index past the length.
Returns token escaped for use in a pointer: ~ becomes ~0 and / becomes ~1.
Returns the pointer for tokens, each escaped and preceded by /; no tokens give the empty string.
fn get(doc: json.Value, pointer: str) -> json.Value ! Error

Returns the value in doc that pointer names. The empty pointer returns doc. An object member is found by name, using the first member of that name, and an array element by index: decimal digits with no leading zero, at most 18 of them. The - token never names an element when reading. Fails with Syntax for a malformed pointer, NotFound when a member or index does not exist and Mismatch when a token does not suit the value it is applied to.
fn has(doc: json.Value, pointer: str) -> bool
Returns whether pointer names a value in doc. It is false for a malformed pointer.

Splits pointer into its unescaped reference tokens. The empty string is the whole document and has no tokens. Any other pointer starts with /, and each /-separated part is a token, so / is one empty token and /a//b has three. Fails with Syntax when the pointer does not start with / or a token has a bad escape.
fn relative(doc: json.Value, current: str, reference: str) -> json.Value ! Error

Returns the value that the relative pointer reference names, evaluated from the location current in doc (Relative JSON Pointer). reference is a non-negative integer with no leading zero and at most nine digits, which says how many levels to go up from current, followed either by # or by a JSON pointer to follow from the level reached. With # the result is the key of that level as a Str, or its index as an Int when its parent is an array. Index offsets such as 1+1 are not supported. Fails with Syntax when the integer is missing or malformed, NotFound when it goes up past the root, and otherwise with the errors of get.
fn remove(doc: json.Value, pointer: str) -> json.Value ! Error

Returns a copy of doc without the value at pointer. On an array the later elements move down. The target must exist and - never names an element. doc is not changed. Fails with CannotRemoveRoot for the empty pointer, and with Syntax, NotFound or Mismatch as get does.
fn replace(doc: json.Value, pointer: str, value: json.Value) -> json.Value ! Error

Returns a copy of doc with the value at pointer replaced by value. The target must exist and - never names an element. The empty pointer returns value. doc is not changed. Fails with Syntax, NotFound or Mismatch as get does.
fn set(doc: json.Value, pointer: str, value: json.Value) -> json.Value ! Error

Returns a copy of doc in which pointer names value. On an object the member is replaced, or added at the end when it is missing. On an array an index below the length replaces that element, and an index equal to the length or - appends. The empty pointer returns value. The parent of the target must exist. doc is not changed, and the copy shares the parts that were not edited. Fails with Syntax, NotFound or Mismatch as get does.
Returns token with its ~0 and ~1 escapes decoded. Fails with Syntax when a ~ is not followed by 0 or 1.

The error returned when a schema cannot be compiled. The schema is not valid. at is the JSON Pointer to the offending keyword in the schema and message says what is wrong, for example a keyword of the wrong type, an unknown type, a duplicate in a list, an invalid pattern or an $id with a fragment. A $ref or $dynamicRef names a schema that is not in the schema document or among Options.resources. reference is the reference resolved against its base URI. References are never fetched.

How the format keyword is treated. format is only an annotation and never makes an instance invalid. This is the default. format is checked for the formats date-time, date, time, email, uuid, uri, hostname, json-pointer and regex; a string that does not match is a violation. Other format names are not checked.
struct Options { pub formats: Formats pub resources: []json.Value }

Settings for compile_with. Whether format is asserted; defaults to Annotate. Further schema documents that references may resolve to. Each one must have an $id; compile_with fails with Malformed when one does not.
A compiled JSON Schema (draft 2020-12), made by compile or compile_with. A Schema can validate any number of instances.
struct Violation { pub instance: str pub keyword: str pub message: str }

One way in which an instance fails a schema. The JSON Pointer to the part of the instance that failed, "" for the instance itself. The JSON Pointer to the keyword in the schema that failed, such as /properties/age/minimum. A keyword reached through a reference has the $ref or $dynamicRef keyword in its path. A description of the failure.
fn is_valid(s: Schema, instance: json.Value) -> bool
Returns whether instance is valid against s; equivalent to validate(s, instance).len == 0.

Returns every way in which instance fails s; the result is empty when it is valid. Annotations from the branches of allOf, anyOf, oneOf, if and the other applicators that passed decide what unevaluatedProperties and unevaluatedItems cover. Validation does not stop at the first failure.
Compiles schema with default Options. See compile_with.
fn compile_with(schema: json.Value, options: Options) -> Schema ! Error

Compiles the JSON Schema 2020-12 document schema. It checks the schema, resolves $ref, $anchor, $dynamicRef and the schemas in options.resources by their $id, and precompiles every pattern and patternProperties expression. A schema is an object or a boolean. Fails with Malformed for an invalid schema and Unresolved for a reference that resolves to nothing.
enum Attr { Str(str, str) Int(str, i64) Float(str, f64) Bool(str, bool) }
A key and a typed value attached to a log record. A string value. An integer value. A floating-point value. A boolean value.

The line layout a Logger renders records in. [time ]level[ prefix]: message key=value .... Values that are empty or contain a space, control byte, " or = are quoted. One JSON object per line with time (when timestamps are on), level, msg, prefix (when set) and one property per attribute.
enum Level { Debug Info Warn Error }

The severity of a log record. Detailed diagnostic output, shown only when the logger level is Debug. Routine progress and state changes; the default logger level. A condition that is unexpected but does not stop the operation. A failure of an operation.
struct Logger { pub level: Level pub prefix: str pub format: Format pub sink: Sink pub attrs: []Attr pub timestamps: bool pub clock: fn() -> i64 pub on_error: fn(io.Error) }

A leveled logger. A Logger is a value; the with_ functions return a modified copy and leave the original unchanged. The minimum level that is delivered; lower levels are discarded. Defaults to Info. The text shown before the message. with_prefix nests prefixes with .. Defaults to empty. The line layout. Defaults to Text. Where records go. Defaults to Fd(2), standard error. Attributes added to every record. Defaults to none. Whether records carry a timestamp taken from clock. Defaults to false. Returns the current time in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch for timestamps. Defaults to time.now_nanos. Receives the error of a failed write to the Fd or Stream sink, after which the line is lost. Defaults to a function that does nothing.
The error returned by parse_level. The text is not a level name.
struct Record { pub level: Level pub message: str pub prefix: str pub attrs: []Attr pub time: i64? }

A log event as it reaches a Handler sink, before any formatting. The record's severity. The message text. The logger's prefix, or an empty string when none is set. The attributes bound to the logger followed by those passed to the call. The timestamp in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, or none when the logger has timestamps off.
enum Sink { Fd(i64) Stream(io.Stream) Lines(fn(str)) Handler(fn(Record)) }

Where a Logger delivers each record. Writes the formatted line to the descriptor. Short writes and EINTR are retried and EAGAIN waits until the descriptor is writable; any other error is passed to Logger.on_error. Writes the formatted line, with a trailing newline, to an io.Stream. A write error is passed to Logger.on_error. Passes the formatted line, without a trailing newline, to the function. Passes the unformatted Record to the function, ignoring Logger.format.
Returns the level named by the LOG_LEVEL environment variable, or fallback when the variable is unset or not a level name.
fn debug_with(l: Logger, message: str, attrs: []Attr)
Logs message at Debug with attrs.
fn emit(l: Logger, level: Level, message: str)
Logs message at level with no attributes beyond those bound to the logger.
fn enabled(l: Logger, level: Level) -> bool
Reports whether a record at level would be delivered by this logger, which is when level is at least l.level.
fn error_with(l: Logger, message: str, attrs: []Attr)
Logs message at Error with attrs.
fn info_with(l: Logger, message: str, attrs: []Attr)
Logs message at Info with attrs.
fn log(l: Logger, level: Level, message: str, attrs: []Attr)
Logs message with attrs at level. Nothing is formatted or delivered when the level is below the logger's. Attributes bound to the logger come first, then attrs.
fn warn_with(l: Logger, message: str, attrs: []Attr)
Logs message at Warn with attrs.
Returns a copy of the logger whose records also carry attrs, after the attributes it already has.
fn with_clock(l: Logger, clock: fn() -> i64) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that reads the time for timestamps from clock, which returns nanoseconds since the Unix epoch.
Returns a copy of the logger whose level comes from the LOG_LEVEL environment variable, keeping the current level when the variable is unset or invalid.
fn with_error_handler(l: Logger, f: fn(io.Error)) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that passes the error of a failed Fd or Stream write to f.
fn with_fd(l: Logger, fd: i64) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that writes to the descriptor fd, replacing any other sink.
fn with_format(l: Logger, format: Format) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that renders records in format.
fn with_handler(l: Logger, f: fn(Record)) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that passes each Record to f, replacing any other sink. The format is not applied.
fn with_level(l: Logger, level: Level) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger with its minimum level set to level.
fn with_lines(l: Logger, f: fn(str)) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that passes each formatted line, without a newline, to f, replacing any other sink.
fn with_prefix(l: Logger, prefix: str) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that shows prefix before each message. When the logger already has a prefix, the result is the old prefix, . and prefix.
fn with_stream(l: Logger, s: io.Stream) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that writes lines to the stream s, replacing any other sink.
fn with_timestamps(l: Logger, on: bool) -> Logger
Returns a copy of the logger that stamps records with the time when on is true, and omits it when false. Timestamps are UTC, RFC 3339 with millisecond precision, taken from the logger's clock.
fn bool_attr(key: str, value: bool) -> Attr
fn float_attr(key: str, value: f64) -> Attr
fn int_attr(key: str, value: i64) -> Attr
Parses a level name, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace. Accepts debug, info, warn, warning and error; any other text fails with Unknown.
fn str_attr(key: str, value: str) -> Attr
struct Address { pub email: str pub name: str }
An email address with an optional display name. The address in local@domain form. valid_email defines what is accepted. The display name. Empty for a bare address.
struct Attachment { pub filename: str pub data: []u8 pub content_type: str }

A file attached to a message. The file name offered to the recipient. Non-ASCII names are written with the RFC 2231 filename* form. The file content. It is sent base64 encoded. The media type, which must contain a /. Defaults to application/octet-stream.
enum Error { InvalidAddress(str) HeaderInjection(str) InvalidHeader(str) NoRecipients ClockUnavailable }

The error type for building and validating messages. address is not a valid email address. A value written to the header header contains a control character other than tab, which could start a new header line. The header header has an invalid name or value: an empty or malformed header name, a boundary with disallowed characters, a content type without a / or a message ID containing a space. The message has no to, cc or bcc recipients. The current time could not be read for the Date header of a message without a date.

struct Message { pub from: Address pub to: []Address pub cc: []Address pub bcc: []Address pub reply_to: []Address pub subject: str pub date: zoned.Zoned? pub message_id: str pub text: str pub html: str pub attachments: []Attachment pub headers: []header.Header pub boundary: str pub eight_bit: bool }

An email message. render turns it into RFC 5322 text and std/smtp sends it. A message with both text and html becomes multipart/alternative; any attachments wrap the body in multipart/mixed. The sender, shown in the From header and used as the SMTP envelope sender. The primary recipients. The copied recipients. The blind copied recipients. They receive the message but are never written to the rendered headers. The addresses replies should go to. The header is omitted when empty. The subject line. The header is omitted when empty. The Date header value. When none, render uses the current time in UTC. The Message-ID header value. When empty, render generates one from the domain of from. Angle brackets are added when missing. It must not contain a space. The plain text body. Omitted when empty. The HTML body. Omitted when empty. The files to attach. Additional header fields, written after MIME-Version. The MIME multipart boundary. When empty, render generates a random one. It may contain only letters, digits and -_=.+. The nested alternative part of a message with attachments uses the boundary with -alt appended. Allows a body to be sent as 8bit instead of quoted-printable when it is not 7-bit safe (it has non-ASCII text or a line over 78 bytes) but has no control characters and no line over 998 bytes. Set it only when the server advertises 8BITMIME; needs_8bit reports when it applies.

Returns the address as written in a header: the bare email when there is no name, otherwise name <email>. A name made of plain characters is written as is, one with specials such as commas or quotes is double quoted with backslash escapes, and one with non-ASCII characters becomes encoded words.

Returns whether render would send the text or HTML body with the 8bit transfer encoding, which requires the SMTP 8BITMIME extension. This is the case only when eight_bit is set and the body is not already 7-bit safe.
Returns whether any address of the message (from, to, cc, bcc or reply_to) contains non-ASCII characters, which requires the SMTP SMTPUTF8 extension.

Returns the envelope recipients of the message: the addresses of to, cc and bcc in that order, with duplicates removed ignoring case. Fails with InvalidAddress or HeaderInjection for the first bad address and with NoRecipients when the list would be empty.

Returns the message as RFC 5322 text with \r\n line endings, ready to send as SMTP data. Headers are written in the order Date, From, To, Cc, Reply-To, Subject, Message-ID, MIME-Version, then headers; Bcc is never written. Header values are folded to 76 columns and non-ASCII values are encoded. Bodies use 7bit, 8bit or quoted-printable as needed, attachments base64. Fails with InvalidAddress, HeaderInjection or InvalidHeader when a field is invalid. A message without a body or attachments renders an empty plain text body.
Returns an Address for email with no display name. The address is not validated.
fn encode_words(s: str, used: i64) -> str

Encodes s as RFC 2047 encoded words (=?utf-8?b?...?=) for use in a header value. used is the number of columns already taken on the first line, typically the header name and its colon and space. Words are sized so that lines stay within 76 columns, and are joined with \r\n so the result folds correctly. A UTF-8 sequence is never split across words. Returns an empty string for empty input.
fn named(name: str, email: str) -> Address
Returns an Address for email with the display name name. The address is not validated.
Returns a new Message-ID value of the form <token@domain>, where token is 24 hexadecimal digits from the system's random source.

Parses s as local@domain or Name <local@domain>. Surrounding whitespace is ignored. A display name in double quotes has the quotes removed and backslash escapes resolved. Fails with InvalidAddress(s) when the angle brackets are unbalanced or the address is not valid. Comments and groups are not supported.

Encodes s as quoted-printable. Line breaks (
 or 
) become 
. Bytes outside printable ASCII, =, and a space or tab at the end of a line are written as =XX with uppercase hexadecimal digits. Lines are soft-wrapped with =
 so that none exceeds 76 columns. No line break is added at the end.

Returns whether s is a usable email address. The text before the last @ is the local part and must be 1 to 64 bytes; the text after it is the domain and must be 1 to 255 bytes. Neither may start or end with a . or contain .., spaces, control characters or any of ()<>[]:;@\,". Non-ASCII characters are accepted. Quoted local parts and domain literals are not.
Returns the base64 encoding of data broken into lines of 76 characters separated by \r\n. There is no line break after the last line. Empty input gives an empty string.
fn clone[K: Hash, V](m: [K: V]) -> [K: V]
Returns a new map with the same entries as m. Changing the copy does not change m.
fn count_by[T, K: Hash](xs: []T, key: fn(T) -> K) -> [K: i64]
Returns how many elements of xs produce each key under key. Keys appear in order of first occurrence.
fn entries[K: Hash, V](m: [K: V]) -> []slices.Pair[K, V]
Returns the entries of m as pairs in insertion order, with the key in first and the value in second.
fn filter[K: Hash, V](m: [K: V], keep: fn(K, V) -> bool) -> [K: V]
Returns a new map of the entries of m for which keep returns true, in their original order.
fn from_pairs[K: Hash, V](pairs: []slices.Pair[K, V]) -> [K: V]

Returns a map built from pairs, taking each key from first and its value from second. When a key appears more than once, the last pair's value wins and the key keeps the position of its first appearance.
fn get_or[K: Hash, V](m: [K: V], key: K, fallback: V) -> V
Returns the value stored under key in m, or fallback when there is no entry.
fn group_by[T, K: Hash](xs: []T, key: fn(T) -> K) -> [K: []T]
Groups the elements of xs by the key that key returns for each. Every group keeps its elements in their original order, and groups appear in order of first occurrence of their key.
fn has[K: Hash, V](m: [K: V], key: K) -> bool
Returns true when m has an entry for key.
fn invert[K: Hash, V: Hash](m: [K: V]) -> [V: K]
Returns a new map from the values of m to their keys. When several keys share a value, the key that comes last in insertion order is kept.
Returns the keys of m in insertion order.
fn map_values[K: Hash, V, U](m: [K: V], f: fn(V) -> U) -> [K: U]
Returns a new map with the keys of m and f applied to each value.
fn merge[K: Hash, V](base: [K: V], over: [K: V]) -> [K: V]
Returns a new map holding the entries of base and then those of over. When a key is in both, the value from over wins and the key keeps its position from base. Neither argument changes.
fn sorted_keys[K: Hash + Ord, V](m: [K: V]) -> []K
Returns the keys of m in ascending order.
Returns the values of m in the insertion order of their keys.
Euler's number e, the base of the natural logarithm.
A quiet not-a-number value with the sign bit clear.
Pi, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
Returns the absolute value of x, which is -x when x is less than zero and x otherwise. The negation has the overflow behaviour of T, so the minimum value of a signed integer type stays negative.
Returns the arc cosine of x in radians, in the range 0 to pi. Returns nan when x is outside -1 to 1.
Returns the arc sine of x in radians, in the range -pi/2 to pi/2. Returns nan when x is outside -1 to 1.
Returns the arc tangent of x in radians, in the range -pi/2 to pi/2.
extern fn atan2(y: f64, x: f64) -> f64
Returns the angle in radians, in the range -pi to pi, of the point at x along the horizontal axis and y along the vertical axis. The signs of both arguments choose the quadrant.
Returns the real cube root of x, which is negative for a negative x.
Returns the smallest whole number that is at least x.
fn clamp[T: Ord](x: T, lo: T, hi: T) -> T
Returns x limited to the range lo to hi. Returns lo when x is below it and hi when x is above it. lo must not be greater than hi.
fn compare[T: Ord](a: T, b: T) -> i64
Returns -1, 0 or 1 when a is less than, equal to or greater than b.
Returns the cosine of x, an angle in radians.
Returns the hyperbolic cosine of x.
fn floor_div(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
Returns a divided by b, rounded toward negative infinity. Panics when b is zero.
fn floor_mod(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
Returns the remainder of a divided by b with the sign of b, so that floor_div(a, b) * b + floor_mod(a, b) is a. Panics when b is zero.
extern fn fmod(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64
Returns the remainder of x divided by y, with the sign of x. The quotient is truncated toward zero, so the result is x - n * y for the integer n that gives a result smaller in magnitude than y.
fn gcd(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64
Returns the greatest common divisor of a and b, which is never negative. The signs of the arguments are ignored and gcd(0, 0) is 0.
extern fn hypot(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64
Returns the length of the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs x and y, which is sqrt(x * x + y * y) without intermediate overflow.
fn ipow(base: i64, exp: i64) -> i64
Returns base raised to the integer power exp, computed by repeated squaring. Returns 1 when exp is zero or negative. Overflow wraps like i64 multiplication.
Returns true when x is positive or negative infinity.
Returns true when x is not a number. nan is the only value that is not equal to itself, so this is the way to test for it.
Returns the natural logarithm of x. Returns negative infinity for zero and nan for a negative x.
Returns the base 10 logarithm of x. Returns negative infinity for zero and nan for a negative x.
Returns the base 2 logarithm of x. Returns negative infinity for zero and nan for a negative x.
fn max[T: Ord](a: T, b: T) -> T
Returns the larger of a and b. Returns a when they are equal. When either is not a number, returns a.
fn min[T: Ord](a: T, b: T) -> T
Returns the smaller of a and b. Returns a when they are equal. When either is not a number, returns a.
extern fn pow(x: f64, y: f64) -> f64
Returns x raised to the power y.
Returns the whole number nearest to x, with halfway cases rounded away from zero.
Returns the sine of x, an angle in radians.
Returns the hyperbolic sine of x.
Returns the tangent of x, an angle in radians.
Returns the hyperbolic tangent of x.
Returns x with its fractional part removed, which rounds toward zero.
Returns the content type for a file extension, or none when it is not known. The extension may start with a dot and is matched without regard to case. Text types carry charset=utf-8.

Returns the file extension, without a dot, for a content type, or none when it is not known. Parameters such as charset are ignored and the type is matched without regard to case. When several extensions share a type, such as jpg and jpeg, the first is returned.

Returns the content type that the leading bytes of data suggest. Images, audio, video, archives, PDF and WebAssembly are recognised by their signatures. After leading whitespace, <!doctype html and <html give text/html; charset=utf-8, <?xml gives application/xml, and a first byte of { or [ gives application/json without checking that the rest is valid. Anything else is text/plain; charset=utf-8 unless it contains control bytes, which give application/octet-stream. Empty data is plain text.
struct Entry { pub key: Value pub value: Value }
A key and value pair of a Map. The key. It can be any Value. The value for the key.
enum Error { Truncated(i64) Invalid(i64) BadUtf8(i64) BadTimestamp(i64) TooDeep(i64) TooLong(i64) Trailing(i64) }

The error returned when decoding MessagePack fails. Every variant carries the byte offset from the start of the input; offset reads it back and message formats it. The input ends before a value is complete. at is the offset where bytes were missing; when a string, binary, array or map declares more elements than remain, it is the length of the input. The format byte 0xC1, which the specification never uses, appears at at. A string is not valid UTF-8. at is the offset of its format byte. A timestamp extension has a payload that is not 4, 8 or 12 bytes, or holds nanoseconds above 999999999. at is the offset of its format byte. Arrays and maps nest deeper than Options.max_depth. at is the offset of the offending array or map. A string, binary, extension payload, array or map declares a length over Options.max_length. at is the offset of its format byte. Bytes remain after the value. at is the offset where they start, which is the length of the value.
struct Item { pub value: Value pub length: i64 }
A decoded value together with the number of bytes it occupied. The decoded value. The number of bytes of the input that the value used.
struct Options { pub max_depth: i64 pub max_length: i64 }

Limits for decoding. The deepest nesting of arrays and maps accepted, counting a top-level array or map as depth 1. Defaults to 64. The largest length that any one string, binary, extension payload, array or map entry count may declare. Defaults to 16777216. It bounds memory before anything is allocated.
enum Value { Nil Bool(bool) Int(i64) Uint(u64) Single(f32) Double(f64) Str(str) Bin([]u8) Array([]Value) Map([]Entry) Ext(i64, []u8) Timestamp(i64, i64) }

A MessagePack value (the MessagePack specification). encode writes each value in its smallest form and decode reads every format of the specification. The nil value (0xC0). A boolean (0xC2, 0xC3). A signed integer. The decoder produces Int for every integer that fits an i64, whether it was stored as signed or unsigned. An unsigned integer too large for an i64. The decoder produces Uint only above 9223372036854775807; encode writes any Uint in the unsigned formats. A 32-bit float (float 32). encode writes it as float 32 and the decoder returns it unchanged. A 64-bit float (float 64). A UTF-8 string (fixstr, str 8, str 16, str 32). The decoder rejects invalid UTF-8. A byte string (bin 8, bin 16, bin 32). An array (fixarray, array 16, array 32). A map (fixmap, map 16, map 32), kept as entries in order. Keys can be any value and may repeat. An extension (fixext, ext 8, ext 16, ext 32) with an application kind from -128 to 127 and its payload data. kind -1 is the timestamp extension, which decodes to Timestamp and is never returned as Ext. encode writes only the low 8 bits of kind. A timestamp extension (type -1) as seconds and nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. nanoseconds is 0 to 999999999; encode carries an out-of-range value into seconds. encode uses the 32-bit form when the nanoseconds are 0 and the seconds fit in 0 to 4294967295, the 64-bit form when the seconds are non-negative and below 2^34, and the 96-bit form otherwise.
Returns a one-line description of the error, including the byte offset.
Returns the byte offset that the error refers to.
Returns the value of an Int, or of a Uint that fits an i64, and none for any other value.

Returns a one-line text description of v, in a notation like JSON that also shows the types JSON lacks. Maps print as {key: value} with keys of any type, arrays as [...]. Strings are quoted, with \" and \\ escaped and every character outside printable ASCII written as \uXXXX, using a surrogate pair above U+FFFF. Floats print as NaN, Infinity, -Infinity or a decimal that always contains a .; a Single has an f suffix. Other values print as nil, true, false, plain integers, h'hex' for Bin, ext(kind, h'hex') and timestamp(seconds, nanoseconds).

Encodes v as MessagePack. Every integer, length and container uses its smallest format: fixint and the shortest signed or unsigned width for integers, fixstr below 32 bytes, fixarray and fixmap below 16 entries, and fixext for 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 byte payloads. Binary data always uses a bin format. Single is written as float 32 and Double as float 64; NaN keeps its bit pattern. Entries are written in the order given. It cannot fail.

Converts the Value v into a T through std/serde. Struct fields are read from Str map keys, and Int, Uint and Bool keys are accepted as text for maps with integer or boolean keys. A float may be read from Single, Double, Int or Uint. An unsigned type may be read from a non-negative Int, while a Uint fails with Range when read as signed. A []u8 is read from Bin and a str from Str. An enum variant is a Str for a variant without fields, or a map with one entry that names the variant. Fails with serde.Error.Mismatch when a value has another type, with Range, Missing and UnknownVariant as serde.read describes, and with Syntax when the value has nothing to read. Timestamp and Ext values cannot be read into a type and fail with Mismatch. In errors, at counts the values consumed so far.
fn get(v: Value, key: str) -> Value?
Returns the value of the entry whose key is the string key, or none when v is not a Map or has no such entry. Only string keys are compared. When a key repeats, the last entry wins.
Decodes data, which must hold exactly one value, with default Options. Fails with Trailing when bytes follow the value. See decode_with.
fn decode_first(data: []u8, options: Options) -> Item ! Error

Decodes the value at the start of data and reports its size, ignoring any bytes after it. Use it to read a stream of back-to-back values by advancing data by Item.length. Fails like decode_with except that it never returns Trailing.
fn decode_with(data: []u8, options: Options) -> Value ! Error

Decodes data, which must hold exactly one MessagePack value. Fails with Truncated, Invalid, BadUtf8, BadTimestamp, TooDeep or TooLong for malformed or over-limit input, and with Trailing when bytes follow the value. Strings and binary data are copied, so the result does not alias data. A timestamp extension becomes Timestamp, other extensions become Ext.

Decodes MessagePack data into a T. Equivalent to decode followed by from_value, with the default Options. A decoding error becomes serde.Error.Syntax carrying the byte offset and message of the decoding error, except that TooDeep becomes serde.Error.TooDeep. Fails like from_value when the value does not fit T.
Encodes v as MessagePack bytes. Equivalent to encode(to_value(v)).

Converts v into a Value through std/serde. Structs and maps become Map with Str keys, slices become Array, []u8 becomes Bin, optionals become Nil or the value, and floats become Double. Integers become Int, except that a u64 above 9223372036854775807 becomes Uint. An enum variant without fields becomes a Str and a variant with fields a one-entry Map from its name to a Map of its labelled fields or an Array of its positional ones.
struct Body { pub data: []u8 pub size: i64 pub spilled: bool }

The content of a part read by read_spill. The content when it fit in memory. Empty when spilled is true. The size of the content in bytes. Whether the content was passed to the sink instead of being kept in data.
enum Error { BadContentType BadBoundary Malformed(i64, str) Truncated TooManyParts HeaderTooLarge TooLarge BoundaryInData InvalidHeader Finished Io(io.Error) }

The error of reading or writing a multipart body. The content type is missing or is not multipart/*. The boundary is missing, empty, longer than 70 bytes, ends in a space or has a byte a boundary may not hold. The body breaks the multipart syntax. at is the approximate byte offset and message says what is wrong. The body ended before the closing boundary. The body has more parts than Limits.max_parts. The headers of a part are larger than Limits.max_header_bytes. The body is larger than Limits.max_total_bytes, or a part held in memory is larger than Limits.max_memory. A part written to a writer with a chosen boundary contains that boundary. A header written to a writer has a name that is not a token, or a value with a carriage return, line feed or NUL. A part was written to a writer after finish. The underlying source or a Spill function failed with cause.
struct Field { pub name: str pub value: str }
A text field of a form. The field name from the name parameter of the part. The text of the part.
struct File { pub name: str pub filename: str pub content_type: str pub data: []u8 pub size: i64 pub spilled: bool pub index: i64 }

A file field of a form. The field name from the name parameter of the part. The file name the client sent. It is not checked, so do not use it as a path. The content-type header of the part, or an empty string when it has none. The content when it was held in memory. Empty when spilled is true. The size of the content in bytes, whether or not it was spilled. Whether the content was passed to the Spill sink instead of being held in data. The zero-based position of the part in the body.
struct Form { pub fields: []Field pub files: []File }
The fields and files of a multipart form, each in the order it appeared in the body. The parts without a filename. The parts with a filename.
struct Limits { pub max_parts: i64 pub max_header_bytes: i64 pub max_total_bytes: i64 pub max_memory: i64 }

Bounds on the size of a multipart body. The most parts a body may have. Defaults to 1000. The most bytes the headers of one part may take. Defaults to 16 KiB. The most bytes the whole body may take. Defaults to 64 MiB. The most bytes of one part that read_bytes, read_text and read_form hold in memory, and the point at which read_spill starts passing content to its sink. Defaults to 1 MiB.
struct Part { pub index: i64 pub headers: []header.Header pub disposition: str pub name: str pub filename: str? pub content_type: str pub params: []header.Header }

The headers of one part of a multipart body, as returned by next_part. The zero-based position of the part in the body. Every header of the part, in order. The content-disposition type in lower case, such as form-data, or an empty string when the header is absent. The name parameter of the content-disposition header, or an empty string when it has none. The filename parameter of the content-disposition header, or none when it has none. The content-type header, or an empty string when it is absent. Every parameter of the content-disposition header.
Reads a multipart body one part at a time. Made by reader or bytes_reader. Call next_part to reach a part, then read or a helper for its content. It does not read from the source until it is used.
struct Spill { pub write: fn(Part, []u8) ! io.Error pub finish: fn(Part, i64) ! io.Error }

Receives file content that is too large to keep in memory. Called with the part and a chunk of its content. The first call carries everything held so far, once it exceeds Limits.max_memory. Called with the part and its total size after its last chunk. It is not called for a file that stayed in memory.
Builds a multipart body in memory. Made by writer or writer_with. Add parts, then call finish for the body and content_type for the header that goes with it.
fn file(f: Form, name: str) -> File?
Returns the first file called name, or none when there is none.
Returns every file called name, in order.
fn value(f: Form, name: str) -> str?
Returns the value of the first field called name, or none when there is none.
Returns the values of every field called name, in order.
fn header(p: Part, name: str) -> str?
Returns the value of the first header of the part called name, or none when it is absent. The name is matched without regard to case.
Returns the media type of the part in lower case, without parameters. A part with no content-type is text/plain.

Moves to the next part and returns its headers, or none after the closing boundary. Content of the current part that was not read is skipped. Fails with Malformed, Truncated, TooManyParts, HeaderTooLarge, TooLarge or Io. Once it has returned none it keeps doing so.

Reads content of the current part into dst and returns the number of bytes. Returns 0 at the end of the part, when no part is open, or when dst is empty. Fails with Truncated when the body ends inside the part, with TooLarge when it exceeds Limits.max_total_bytes, and with Io when the source fails.
Reads the rest of the current part into memory. Fails with TooLarge when it is longer than Limits.max_memory, and with the errors of read.
fn read_form(r: *Reader, spill: Spill?) -> Form ! Error

Reads the remaining parts of the body into a Form. Parts that are not form-data or have no name are skipped. A part with a filename is a file, and any other part is a field. Without spill, a file or field larger than Limits.max_memory fails with TooLarge. With spill, a file larger than that is passed to it. Fails with the errors of next_part and read, and with Io when a Spill function fails.
fn read_spill(r: *Reader, sink: fn([]u8) ! io.Error) -> Body ! Error

Reads the rest of the current part, passing it to sink once it is longer than Limits.max_memory. Shorter content is returned in Body.data. Longer content is passed to sink in chunks starting with everything read so far, and the body returns empty with spilled set. Fails with Io when sink fails, and with the errors of read.
Reads the rest of the current part as text. The bytes are not checked for UTF-8. Fails like read_bytes.
Returns the boundary of the writer.
Returns the multipart/form-data content type with the boundary of the writer.
Returns the multipart/ content type with subtype and the boundary of the writer. The boundary is quoted when it holds a byte that is not allowed in a bare token.
Ends the body with the closing boundary and returns it. It is safe to call again, and returns the same bytes. Adding a part afterwards fails with Finished.
fn write_field(w: *Writer, name: str, value: str) ! Error
Adds a form-data text field called name. Fails like write_part.
fn write_file(w: *Writer, name: str, filename: str, content_type: str, data: []u8) ! Error
Adds a form-data file field with a filename and content_type, which defaults to application/octet-stream when empty. Fails like write_part.
fn write_form_part(w: *Writer, name: str, filename: str?, content_type: str, data: []u8) ! Error

Adds a form-data part called name with data, as write_field and write_file do. A filename of none makes a plain field, which has a Content-Type only when content_type is not empty. A file name makes a file field, whose content_type defaults to application/octet-stream when empty. Fails like write_part.

Adds a part with headers and data. Fails with Finished after finish, with InvalidHeader for a header that is not valid, and with BoundaryInData when the boundary was chosen and the data contains it. Nothing is added when it fails.
Returns the boundary of a multipart/* content type. Fails with BadContentType for any other type, and with BadBoundary when the parameter is missing or invalid.
fn bytes_reader(data: []u8, boundary: str, limits: Limits) -> *Reader ! Error
Returns a reader for the multipart body in data. See reader.
Fails with BadBoundary unless boundary is 1 to 70 bytes of letters, digits and '()+_,-./:=? , and does not end in a space.
fn reader(source: *io.Reader, boundary: str, limits: Limits) -> *Reader ! Error
Returns a reader for a multipart body read from source and delimited by boundary. Fails with BadBoundary when the boundary is invalid. Reads from source block until data arrives.
Returns a writer with a random 48-character boundary. The boundary is random, so the data of a part is not searched for it.
Returns a writer that uses boundary. Fails with BadBoundary when it is invalid. write_part then fails with BoundaryInData for data that contains the boundary.
struct Addr { pub ip: []u8 pub port: i64 pub path: str }

A network address: an IP address and port, or a Unix socket path. The ip field tells the kinds apart: 4 bytes for IPv4, 16 for IPv6 and empty for a Unix address, as is_unix reports. The address bytes in network order: 4 for IPv4, 16 for IPv6, empty for a Unix address. The port number, 0 for a Unix address. The socket path of a Unix address, empty for an IP address. A name that starts with @ or NUL is in the abstract namespace and is not a file.
struct BufferSizes { pub receive: i64 pub send: i64 }
The kernel buffer sizes of a socket, in bytes, as the kernel reports them. The receive buffer size. The send buffer size.
The owner of a connection. Dropping it closes the connection unless detach took the view. The copyable view of the connection.
struct ConnHandle { pub fd: i64 pub out: i64 pub remote: Addr pub timeouts: *Timeouts ... }

A copyable view of a TCP or Unix stream connection. Every copy shares the connection, its timeouts and its closed state, so one green thread can read while another writes. The view does not close the connection when released; close_on does, and Conn does when dropped. The descriptor used for reading. The descriptor used for writing, from sys.write_view, which waits for buffer space independently of reads from fd. The address of the peer, as known when the connection was made. The read and write timeouts, shared by every copy of the handle.
struct ConnPair { pub first: Conn pub second: Conn }
Two connected Conn values made by socketpair. One end of the pair. The other end of the pair. Data written to one end is read from the other.
struct Credentials { pub pid: i64 pub uid: i64 pub gid: i64 }
The identity of the process at the other end of a Unix socket. The process id. The user id. The group id.
struct Dialer { pub dial: fn(str, i64) -> ConnHandle ! io.Error }

A function value that opens connections, so that code can connect directly or through a proxy. Opens a connection to the host name or address and port and returns its view, which the caller must close.
struct Keepalive { pub enabled: bool pub idle: i64 pub interval: i64 pub count: i64 }

The TCP keep-alive settings of a connection. Whether keep-alive probes are sent. Seconds the connection is idle before the first probe. Seconds between probes. Number of unanswered probes after which the connection is dropped.
struct ListenOptions { pub reuse_addr: bool pub reuse_port: bool pub backlog: i64 }

Options for listen_with and bind_udp_with. Whether to set SO_REUSEADDR before binding, which lets a restarted program bind a port still in TIME_WAIT. Whether to set SO_REUSEPORT before binding, which lets several sockets bind the same port. The length of the queue of connections waiting to be accepted. UDP sockets ignore it.
The owner of a listening socket. Dropping it closes the socket unless detach_listener took the view. The copyable view of the listener.
struct ListenerHandle { pub fd: i64 pub addr: Addr ... }

A copyable view of a listening socket. Every copy shares the socket and its closed state. The view does not close the socket when released; close_listener_on does, and Listener does when dropped. The descriptor of the listening socket. The address the socket is bound to, with the actual port when port 0 was requested.
struct Packet { pub size: i64 pub from: Addr }

A received datagram: its length and sender. The number of bytes written into the receive buffer. A datagram longer than the buffer is truncated to the buffer's length. The address the datagram came from.
The owner of a UDP socket. Dropping it closes the socket unless detach_socket took the view. The copyable view of the socket.
struct SocketHandle { pub fd: i64 pub out: i64 pub addr: Addr pub timeouts: *Timeouts ... }

A copyable view of a UDP socket. Every copy shares the socket, its timeouts and its closed state. The view does not close the socket when released; close_socket_on does, and Socket does when dropped. The descriptor used for receiving. The descriptor used for sending, from sys.write_view, which waits for buffer space independently of receives from fd. The address the socket is bound to, with the actual port when port 0 was requested. The timeouts, shared by every copy of the handle.
struct Timeouts { pub read: i64 pub write: i64 }

The read and write timeouts of a connection or socket, in milliseconds. A value of 0 or less means no timeout. All copies of a handle share one Timeouts. The longest a read waits for data. The longest a write waits for buffer space.
Connects to the TCP or Unix address a. Parks the green thread while the connection is in progress, with no time limit of its own. Does the same as connect_within with no timeout.
fn connect_through(a: Addr, device: str, millis: i64) -> Conn ! io.Error

Connects to a through the network interface device. Binds the socket to device before connecting, which usually needs privileges. An empty device leaves the choice to the system. millis is the timeout as for connect_within.
fn connect_within(a: Addr, millis: i64) -> Conn ! io.Error

Connects to a, failing with TimedOut if the connection takes longer than millis milliseconds. A millis of 0 or less means no limit. Parks the green thread while the connection is in progress. Fails with Refused or Unreachable as the system reports.
Returns a as text: host:port for IPv4, [host]:port for IPv6 and unix:path for a Unix address.
Returns whether a is a Unix socket address, which has no IP address.
Returns the receive and send buffer sizes of c. Fails with NotConnected if c is closed.
Closes the connection c. Does the same as close_on on its handle.
Stops c from closing the connection when dropped, and returns its view. The caller must close the connection with close_on.
Returns the keep-alive settings of c. Fails with NotConnected if c is closed.
Returns the local address of c. Fails with NotConnected if c is closed.
Returns the process id, user id and group id of the peer of c, as recorded when the connection was made. Meaningful for Unix socket connections. Fails with NotConnected if c is closed.
fn read(c: Conn, buf: []u8) -> i64 ! io.Error

Reads up to buf.len bytes from c into buf and returns the count, or 0 at end of input. Parks the green thread until data arrives. If the read timeout elapses first, the connection is shut down and the call fails with TimedOut. Fails with NotConnected after the connection is closed, including while the call is waiting.
fn set_buffer_sizes(c: Conn, receive: i64, send: i64) ! io.Error

Sets the receive and send buffer sizes of c in bytes. A value of 0 or less leaves that buffer unchanged. The kernel can adjust the requested size, so read it back with buffer_sizes. Fails with NotConnected if c is closed.
fn set_keepalive(c: Conn, idle: i64, interval: i64, count: i64) ! io.Error

Configures TCP keep-alive on c. An idle of 0 or less turns keep-alive off. Otherwise it sets the idle time in seconds, sets interval and count when they are greater than 0 and leaves the system default otherwise, and turns keep-alive on. Fails with NotConnected if c is closed.
fn set_nodelay(c: Conn, on: bool) ! io.Error
Sets TCP_NODELAY on c, which sends small writes at once instead of waiting to combine them. Fails with NotConnected if c is closed.
Sets how long reads on c wait for data, in milliseconds, with 0 or less meaning no limit. Applies to later reads on every copy of the handle. A read that times out shuts the connection down.

Sets how long writes on c wait for buffer space, in milliseconds, with 0 or less meaning no limit. Applies to later writes on every copy of the handle. A write that times out shuts the connection down.
Closes the sending side of c while leaving it open for reading. Does the same as shutdown_write_on on its handle.
Returns an io.Stream over c. Its read, write and close call read, write and close on the connection.
fn write(c: Conn, data: []u8) -> i64 ! io.Error

Writes a prefix of data to c and returns how many bytes were written, which can be fewer than data.len. Parks the green thread while the send buffer is full. If the write timeout elapses first, the connection is shut down and the call fails with TimedOut. A peer that has closed the connection gives BrokenPipe or Reset and never raises SIGPIPE. Fails with NotConnected after the connection is closed.
Writes all of data to c. Repeats write until nothing is left and fails with its first error.
Returns the Conn that owns the connection behind h, which closes it when dropped.

Closes the connection behind h. Shuts the connection down so green threads waiting to read or write wake and fail, and releases the descriptors once the last operation in progress has finished. Later reads and writes fail with NotConnected. Later calls do nothing.
Returns the process id, user id and group id of the peer behind h. Fails with NotConnected if the connection is closed.
fn read_on(h: ConnHandle, buf: []u8) -> i64 ! io.Error

Reads up to buf.len bytes from the connection behind h into buf and returns the count, or 0 at end of input. Parks the green thread until data arrives. If the read timeout elapses first, the connection is shut down and the call fails with TimedOut. Fails with NotConnected after the connection is closed, including while the call is waiting.

Closes the sending side of the connection behind h while leaving it open for reading. The peer then reads end of input after the data already sent. Fails with NotConnected if the connection is closed.
Returns an io.Stream over the connection behind h. Its read, write and close call read_on, write_on and close_on.
Writes all of data to the connection behind h. Repeats write_on until nothing is left and fails with its first error.
fn write_on(h: ConnHandle, data: []u8) -> i64 ! io.Error

Writes a prefix of data to the connection behind h and returns how many bytes were written, which can be fewer than data.len. Parks the green thread while the send buffer is full. If the write timeout elapses first, the connection is shut down and the call fails with TimedOut. A peer that has closed the connection gives BrokenPipe or Reset and never raises SIGPIPE. Fails with NotConnected after the connection is closed.
Accepts the next connection on l. Parks the green thread until a connection arrives. Fails with NotConnected once the listener is closed, including while the call is waiting.
Closes the listener l. Does the same as close_listener_on on its handle.
Stops l from closing the socket when dropped, and returns its view. The caller must close the socket with close_listener_on.

Accepts the next connection on the listener behind h and returns its view. Parks the green thread until a connection arrives. The caller owns the connection, usually by passing the view to a green thread that binds it with adopt. Fails with NotConnected once the listener is closed, including while the call is waiting. A connection reset before it was accepted is skipped.

Closes the listener behind h. Wakes a green thread waiting in accept, which fails with NotConnected. The socket is released once no accept is in progress, and a Unix socket file is removed. Later calls do nothing.
Closes the UDP socket s. Does the same as close_socket_on on its handle.
Stops s from closing the socket when dropped, and returns its view. The caller must close the socket with close_socket_on.
fn join_group(s: Socket, group: []u8, interface: str) ! io.Error

Joins the multicast group on the UDP socket s. group is 4 bytes in 224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255 or 16 bytes starting with 0xFF, and must be the same family as the socket's bound address. interface names the network interface to join on, or is empty to let the system choose. Fails with Invalid if group is not a multicast address of the socket's family, with NotFound for an unknown interface and with NotConnected if s is closed.
fn leave_group(s: Socket, group: []u8, interface: str) ! io.Error
Leaves the multicast group on the UDP socket s. Arguments and errors are as for join_group.
fn receive_from(s: Socket, buf: []u8) -> Packet ! io.Error
Receives one datagram into buf and returns its length and sender. Does the same as receive_from_on on its handle.
fn send_to(s: Socket, data: []u8, to: Addr) -> i64 ! io.Error
Sends data as one datagram to to and returns the number of bytes sent. Does the same as send_to_on on its handle.
fn set_multicast_interface(s: Socket, interface: str) ! io.Error
Sets the network interface that multicast datagrams from s leave through. An empty interface restores the system's choice. Fails with NotFound for an unknown interface.
fn set_multicast_loop(s: Socket, on: bool) ! io.Error
Sets whether multicast datagrams sent from s are also delivered to sockets on the same host.
fn set_multicast_ttl(s: Socket, ttl: i64) ! io.Error
Sets the time to live, or hop limit, of multicast datagrams sent from s to ttl.
Sets how long receive_from waits on s, in milliseconds, with 0 or less meaning no limit. A receive that times out shuts the socket down.
fn set_socket_buffer_sizes(s: Socket, receive: i64, send: i64) ! io.Error
Sets the receive and send buffer sizes of the UDP socket s in bytes. A value of 0 or less leaves that buffer unchanged. Fails with NotConnected if s is closed.
Returns the receive and send buffer sizes of the UDP socket s. Fails with NotConnected if s is closed.
Returns the Socket that owns the socket behind h, which closes it when dropped.
Closes the UDP socket behind h. Wakes green threads waiting to send or receive, which fail, and releases the descriptor once the last operation in progress has finished. Later calls do nothing.
fn receive_from_on(h: SocketHandle, buf: []u8) -> Packet ! io.Error

Receives one datagram into buf through the socket behind h and returns its length and sender. Parks the green thread until a datagram arrives. A datagram longer than buf is truncated. If the receive timeout elapses first, the socket is shut down and the call fails with TimedOut. Fails with NotConnected if the socket is closed and with Malformed if the system reports a sender address that is not IPv4 or IPv6. An empty buf receives a datagram of size 0.
fn send_to_on(h: SocketHandle, data: []u8, to: Addr) -> i64 ! io.Error

Sends data as one datagram to to through the socket behind h and returns the number of bytes sent. Parks the green thread while the send buffer is full, waiting on the write view, so another green thread can wait in receive_from_on at the same time. to must be an address of the socket's family. Fails with NotConnected if the socket is closed.
fn bind_udp(host: str, port: i64) -> Socket ! io.Error
Binds a UDP socket to host and port. Uses the default ListenOptions. host is resolved as for listen. Port 0 chooses a free port, which handle.addr.port reports.
fn bind_udp_with(host: str, port: i64, o: ListenOptions) -> Socket ! io.Error
Binds a UDP socket to host and port with the given options. host and port are used as for bind_udp. Fails with Invalid if the system rejects reuse_addr or reuse_port.
fn connect_first(ips: [][]u8, port: i64, device: str, millis: i64) -> Conn ! io.Error

Connects to the first of the addresses ips that accepts a connection on port. Tries the addresses in order, each with the timeout millis and through device as for connect_through, and moves on after a failure. The error of the last address is the one returned. Fails with NotFound if ips is empty.
Connects to the Unix stream socket at path. Parks the green thread while the connection is in progress. Fails as connect_unix_within does, with the default wait.
fn connect_unix_within(path: str, millis: i64) -> Conn ! io.Error

Connects to the Unix stream socket at path, waiting at most millis milliseconds. When the listener's backlog is full it retries every millisecond for up to millis, or 30 seconds when millis is 0 or less, and then fails with TimedOut. Fails with Invalid for a bad path, NotFound if there is no socket and Refused if nothing listens.
fn dial(host: str, port: i64) -> Conn ! io.Error
Resolves host with lookup and connects to port on the first address that accepts. Parks the green thread while resolving and connecting, with no connect timeout.
fn dial_handle(host: str, port: i64) -> ConnHandle ! io.Error
Connects to host and port as dial does and returns the view of the connection. The caller owns the connection and must close it with close_on.
fn dial_within(host: str, port: i64, millis: i64) -> Conn ! io.Error

Resolves host with lookup and connects to port, with each connection attempt limited to millis milliseconds. Parks the green thread while resolving and connecting. See connect_first for the order of attempts.
Returns a Dialer that resolves the host with lookup and connects to it directly, as dial_handle does.

Returns the text form of ip: dotted decimal for 4 bytes and lowercase hexadecimal groups for 16. The longest run of two or more zero groups in an IPv6 address is written as ::. Returns an empty string for an empty ip.
Returns whether ip lies within the CIDR range prefix, written address/bits such as 10.0.0.0/8. Returns false if prefix has no valid address or bit count, or if its address family differs from ip.

Returns the kernel index of the network interface name. Fails with Invalid if name is empty or, on Linux, longer than 15 bytes; Windows has no length limit. Fails with NotFound if there is no such interface.

Returns whether ip is a globally reachable unicast address. Returns false for the ranges the IANA special-purpose registries mark as not globally reachable, such as loopback, private, link-local, documentation and unique-local ranges, and for multicast and reserved ranges. The registries' globally reachable exceptions inside those ranges return true. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address is judged by its IPv4 part, and an ip that is neither 4 nor 16 bytes returns false.
fn listen(host: str, port: i64) -> Listener ! io.Error

Listens for TCP connections on host and port. Uses the default ListenOptions. An empty host listens on all IPv4 addresses, :: on all IPv6 addresses, and any other name is resolved with lookup and its first address is used. Port 0 chooses a free port, which handle.addr.port reports. Fails with AddrInUse if the port is taken and Denied if the caller may not bind it.

Listens for stream connections on the Unix socket path. path is validated as unix_addr does and can name an abstract socket. The backlog is 4096. Fails with AddrInUse if a file already exists at path. Closing the listener removes the socket file, except for an abstract name.
fn listen_with(host: str, port: i64, o: ListenOptions) -> Listener ! io.Error
Listens for TCP connections on host and port with the given options. host and port are used as for listen. Fails with Invalid if the system rejects reuse_addr or reuse_port.

Returns the IP addresses of host. Tries an IP literal first, then the entries of the hosts file, /etc/hosts on Linux and drivers\etc\hosts under the system directory on Windows, matching the name without regard to case, then localhost as 127.0.0.1 and ::1, and then DNS. For DNS it asks each nameserver of /etc/resolv.conf on Linux, or each IPv4 DNS server the network adapters are configured with on Windows, in turn, or 127.0.0.1 when none is listed, for A and then AAAA records over UDP port 53, with a 2 second timeout and one retry per query, and returns the addresses of the first server that has any. Search domains and TCP fallback are not used. Fails with NotFound if no address is found. Parks the green thread during the network queries and blocks the OS thread while it reads the two files.

Parses host:port into an Addr. The text is split at its last :. The host must be an IP literal, in square brackets if desired, and the port a number from 0 to 65535. Host names are not resolved. Fails with Invalid for any other form.

Parses an IPv4 dotted-quad or an IPv6 literal and returns its 4 or 16 bytes. An address containing : is read as IPv6, with :: compression and an optional trailing dotted IPv4 part. Brackets, zone identifiers and host names are not accepted. Fails with Invalid if s is not an address.
Returns two connected, unnamed Unix stream sockets.

Returns the Unix address for the socket path. A path that starts with @ or NUL names an abstract socket and is returned as @ followed by the rest of the name. Fails with Invalid if path is empty, longer than 107 bytes or, for a filesystem path, contains NUL.
Returns whether ip is an IPv6 address, meaning it has 16 bytes.
enum Condition[T] { Compare(str, Op, sql.Value) IsNull(str) NotNull(str) OneOf(str, []sql.Value) All([]Condition[T]) Any([]Condition[T]) Not(*Condition[T]) Raw(str, []sql.Value) }

A condition on the rows of a table T, rendered into a WHERE clause with every value passed as a statement parameter. Build conditions with eq, lt, not, the All and Any variants and the other functions of this module. The column compared with a value by op. The column is NULL. The column is not NULL. The column equals one of the values. An empty list matches no row. Every part holds. An empty list matches every row. At least one part holds. An empty list matches no row. The inner condition does not hold. A SQL fragment in which each ? is replaced by the next value as a parameter. A ? with no value left stays in the text as written. The text itself is not checked or quoted.
enum Op { Eq Ne Lt Le Gt Ge Like }

How a column is compared with a value. The column equals the value. The column differs from the value, rendered as <>. The column is less than the value. The column is less than or equal to the value. The column is greater than the value. The column is greater than or equal to the value. The column matches the value as a SQL LIKE pattern.
A select over a Table[T], built from from by adding conditions, ordering and paging. A Query is a copyable value; each function returns a changed copy and leaves its argument alone.
struct Table[T] { pub name: str pub key: str }

A database table that stores values of type T, one column per field of T. Fields of T map to columns of the same name. Scalars, strings, byte slices and unit enums are stored natively; other values, such as structs, sequences, maps and enum variants with data, are stored as JSON text. The table name, quoted for the dialect when it is used. The column that holds the primary key. Defaults to id.
Returns the condition that c does not hold.
fn filter[T](q: Query[T], c: Condition[T]) -> Query[T]
Returns q with c added. All conditions of a query must hold.
fn order_by[T, F](q: Query[T], f: serde.Field[T, F]) -> Query[T]
Returns q ordered by field f ascending, after any earlier ordering.
fn order_by_desc[T, F](q: Query[T], f: serde.Field[T, F]) -> Query[T]
Returns q ordered by field f descending, after any earlier ordering.
fn skip[T](q: Query[T], n: i64) -> Query[T]
Returns q that skips the first n rows of the result. A value of zero or less skips nothing.
fn take[T](q: Query[T], n: i64) -> Query[T]
Returns q limited to n rows. A negative n removes the limit. Without an ordering, which rows come first is up to the database.
Returns the query that selects every row of t, in database order and without limit.
fn count[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, q: Query[T]) -> i64 ! sql.Error
