Returns the number of rows that match q. Ordering and paging of q are ignored. Fails with Protocol if the database returns no result row and Conversion if the count is not an integer.
fn create_table[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, t: Table[T]) ! sql.Error
Creates the table for t on db. Fails with the database error, including when the table already exists.
fn create_table_sql[T](d: sql.Dialect, t: Table[T]) -> str

Returns the CREATE TABLE statement for t in dialect d. Columns follow the fields of T and are NOT NULL unless the field is optional. The column types come from d.types. An integer key becomes an identity primary key; any other key becomes a plain PRIMARY KEY column, with the short text type for a string key. Booleans, integers, floats, strings and byte slices get native types, a 64-bit unsigned integer gets the unsigned type and an enum of unit variants the enumeration type. Every other field gets the document type: jsonb on Postgres, nvarchar(max) on SQL Server and TEXT on SQLite.
fn delete_matching[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, q: Query[T]) -> i64 ! sql.Error
Deletes every row that matches q and returns the number deleted. Ordering and paging of q are ignored. A query without conditions deletes every row of the table.
fn drop_table[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, t: Table[T]) ! sql.Error
Drops the table of t on db if it exists.
fn eq[T, F: Eq](f: serde.Field[T, F], v: F) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that field f equals v. The value is converted as value_of does. A none value compares with NULL and matches no row; use is_null to test for it.
fn execute(db: sql.ConnectionHandle, text: str, values: []sql.Value) -> i64 ! sql.Error
Runs the SQL text with values as parameters and returns the number of affected rows.
fn find[T, K](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, t: Table[T], key: K) -> T? ! sql.Error
Returns the row of t whose key equals key, or none if there is none. key is converted as value_of does.
fn first[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, q: Query[T]) -> T? ! sql.Error
Returns the first row that matches q, or none if no row matches. Limits the query to one row; the row that comes first is up to the query's ordering.
fn ge[T, F: Ord](f: serde.Field[T, F], v: F) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that field f is greater than or equal to v.
fn gt[T, F: Ord](f: serde.Field[T, F], v: F) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that field f is greater than v.
fn insert[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, t: Table[T], v: T) -> sql.Value ! sql.Error

Inserts v into t and returns the key of the new row. Every field of v becomes a column. When the key field is 0 or none, it is left out so the database generates it. Postgres and SQL Server report the key through RETURNING and OUTPUT; SQLite has no such clause here, so the result is Null.
fn is_null[T, F](f: serde.Field[T, F?]) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that the optional field f is NULL.
fn le[T, F: Ord](f: serde.Field[T, F], v: F) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that field f is less than or equal to v.
fn like[T](f: serde.Field[T, str], pattern: str) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that string field f matches the SQL LIKE pattern pattern. % matches any run of characters and _ one character. Case sensitivity follows the database.
fn list[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, q: Query[T]) -> []T ! sql.Error
Returns every row that matches q, mapped onto T. Fails with Conversion when a row does not fit T, and otherwise with the database error.
fn lt[T, F: Ord](f: serde.Field[T, F], v: F) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that field f is less than v.
fn ne[T, F: Eq](f: serde.Field[T, F], v: F) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that field f differs from v. Rows where the field is NULL do not match.
fn not_null[T, F](f: serde.Field[T, F?]) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that the optional field f is not NULL.
fn one_of[T, F](f: serde.Field[T, F], values: []F) -> Condition[T]
Returns the condition that field f equals one of values. An empty values matches no row.
fn query[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, text: str, values: []sql.Value) -> []T ! sql.Error

Runs the SQL text with values as parameters and maps each result row onto T. Use it for statements Query cannot express. Fails with Conversion when a row does not fit T, and otherwise with the database error.

Returns a condition from the SQL fragment text, replacing each ? with the next of values as a parameter. The text is sent as written, so never build it from untrusted input; pass such input as values.
fn remove[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, t: Table[T], v: T) -> i64 ! sql.Error
Deletes the row of t whose key equals the key of v and returns the number of rows deleted. Returns 0 when no row has that key.
Returns the table name for T, with id as its key column.
fn to_sql[T](d: sql.Dialect, q: Query[T]) -> str

Returns the SELECT statement for q in dialect d, with placeholders in place of its values. The values are not returned, so the text is for inspection. Paging is written as LIMIT and OFFSET on Postgres and SQLite, and as OFFSET ... FETCH NEXT on SQL Server, which gets ORDER BY (SELECT NULL) when the query has no ordering.
fn transaction(db: sql.ConnectionHandle, body: fn() ! sql.Error) ! sql.Error

Runs body between a begin and a commit on db. If body fails, the transaction is rolled back and transaction fails with the same error, or with the rollback's error when the rollback fails too. A failed begin or commit returns its error; a failed commit does not roll back. body should use db for its statements. The transaction does not nest.
fn update[T](db: sql.ConnectionHandle, t: Table[T], v: T) -> i64 ! sql.Error
Updates the row of t whose key equals the key of v, setting every other field from v, and returns the number of rows updated. Returns 0 when no row has that key.

Returns the sql.Value that stores v in a column. Booleans, integers, floats, strings and byte slices become the matching Value variants. A u64 above the i64 maximum becomes Decimal, a unit enum variant becomes Text holding its name, and none becomes Null. Structs, sequences, maps and enum variants with data become Text holding their JSON.
struct User { pub name: str pub uid: i64 pub gid: i64 pub home: str pub shell: str }
An account entry from /etc/passwd. The login name. The numeric user id. The numeric id of the user's primary group. The home directory path. The login shell path.
Returns the command-line arguments the program started with, the program name first.
Returns the per-user cache directory, or none if it cannot be found. Uses XDG_CACHE_HOME when it is an absolute path, and otherwise .cache under home_dir. On Windows uses LOCALAPPDATA.

Changes the working directory of the whole process to path. Fails with NotFound, NotDir or Denied as the operating system reports. The change affects every green thread and relative paths used afterwards.
Returns the per-user configuration directory, or none if it cannot be found. Uses XDG_CONFIG_HOME when it is an absolute path, and otherwise .config under home_dir. On Windows uses APPDATA.
Returns the number of CPUs the process may run on, according to its affinity mask. Returns 1 if the mask cannot be read.
Returns the per-user data directory, or none if it cannot be found. Uses XDG_DATA_HOME when it is an absolute path, and otherwise .local/share under home_dir. On Windows uses APPDATA.

Returns the value of the environment variable name, or none if it is not set. A variable that is set to an empty string returns some(""). Changes made by set_env and unset_env take precedence over the starting environment.
Returns every environment variable as a map from name to value. Starts from the environment the program was started with and applies the changes made by set_env and unset_env.

Returns the path of the running executable. Reads /proc/self/exe on Linux, and fails with the system error of reading the link, such as NotFound when /proc is not mounted. Blocks the OS thread for the call.
Ends the process immediately with the status code. Does not run pending defer blocks or drops and does not wait for other green threads. Does not return.
Returns the absolute path of the current working directory. Fails with NotFound if the directory has been removed and with TooLarge if the path exceeds 1 MiB.

Returns the home directory of the current user, or none if it cannot be found. Uses HOME when it is set and not empty, and otherwise the home field of the effective user's /etc/passwd entry. On Windows uses USERPROFILE.
Returns the host name of the machine.

Returns the /etc/passwd entry whose user id is id, or none. Returns none as well when the file cannot be read, and always on Windows, which has no numeric user ids. Lines with fewer than seven fields or a non-numeric id are skipped. Reads the file on every call and blocks the OS thread while doing so.
Returns the process id of the parent.
fn set_env(name: str, value: str) ! io.Error

Sets the environment variable name to value for this program. The change is seen by env, environment, std/process's find and the environment std/process passes to children that do not set their own. It is kept in a shared memory region, not in the operating system's environment block, so code outside Low that reads that block does not see it. Fails with Invalid if name is empty or contains = or NUL, or value contains NUL; with NoSpace when the region (1 MiB) is full; and with Unsupported if the region cannot be set up.
Returns the per-user state directory, or none if it cannot be found. Uses XDG_STATE_HOME when it is an absolute path, and otherwise .local/state under home_dir. On Windows uses LOCALAPPDATA.

Returns the directory for temporary files: TMPDIR when it is set and not empty, and /tmp otherwise. On Windows the first of TMP, TEMP and USERPROFILE that is set and not empty, and C:\Windows\Temp otherwise.
Sets the file creation mask to mask & 0o777 and returns the previous mask. The mask is process-wide.

Removes the environment variable name from this program's view of the environment. Afterwards env returns none and environment omits the name, even when the program started with it. Fails with Invalid if name is empty or contains = or NUL, and with NoSpace or Unsupported as set_env does.
Returns the number of seconds the machine has been running.
Returns the login name of the effective user, or none if it cannot be found. Reads the effective user's /etc/passwd entry on Linux and USERNAME on Windows.

enum Signal { Hangup Interrupt Quit IllegalInstruction Trap Abort BusError FloatingPoint Kill User1 SegmentationFault User2 Pipe Alarm Terminate Child Continue Stop TerminalStop TerminalInput TerminalOutput UrgentData CpuLimit FileSizeLimit VirtualAlarm ProfilingAlarm WindowChange IoReady PowerFailure BadSystemCall Other(i64) }

A Linux signal that this module can send, catch or ignore. The terminal closed or the controlling process ended (SIGHUP, 1). Interrupt from the keyboard (SIGINT, 2). Quit from the keyboard (SIGQUIT, 3). Illegal instruction (SIGILL, 4). Trace or breakpoint trap (SIGTRAP, 5). Abnormal termination (SIGABRT, 6). Access to an invalid memory address or a misaligned access (SIGBUS, 7). Arithmetic error such as division by zero (SIGFPE, 8). Unconditional termination (SIGKILL, 9), which cannot be caught or ignored. First user-defined signal (SIGUSR1, 10). Invalid memory reference (SIGSEGV, 11). Second user-defined signal (SIGUSR2, 12). Write to a pipe or socket with no reader (SIGPIPE, 13). Timer expiry (SIGALRM, 14). Request to terminate (SIGTERM, 15). A child process stopped or ended (SIGCHLD, 17). Resume a stopped process (SIGCONT, 18). Unconditional stop (SIGSTOP, 19), which cannot be caught or ignored. Stop from the keyboard (SIGTSTP, 20). A background process read from its terminal (SIGTTIN, 21). A background process wrote to its terminal (SIGTTOU, 22). Urgent data on a socket (SIGURG, 23). CPU time limit exceeded (SIGXCPU, 24). File size limit exceeded (SIGXFSZ, 25). Virtual timer expiry (SIGVTALRM, 26). Profiling timer expiry (SIGPROF, 27). The terminal window was resized (SIGWINCH, 28). I/O is possible on a descriptor (SIGIO, 29). Power failure (SIGPWR, 30). Bad system call (SIGSYS, 31). A signal without a name here, such as a real-time signal, with its Linux number from 1 to 64.
The owner of a signal watch. Dropping it stops the watch. The copyable view of the watch.

A copyable view of a signal watch, used to receive signals and to stop the watch from another green thread. Dropping a handle does not stop the watch; stop_on or the owning Watch does. The channel the caught signals arrive on. It holds 16 signals and drops a signal that arrives while it is full. It is closed when the watch stops.
Returns whether s can be caught or ignored, which is false for Kill and Stop.
Returns the conventional name of s, such as SIGINT. A signal without a name gives SIG followed by its number.
Returns the Linux signal number of s.
Sends the signal s to the calling thread. A handler installed in this process has run by the time raise returns.
Stops the watch owned by w. Does the same as stop_on on its handle.
Parks the green thread until w delivers a signal and returns it. Fails with NotConnected once the watch has stopped.
fn wait_timeout(w: Watch, millis: i64) -> Signal?
Waits up to millis milliseconds for w to deliver a signal, and returns it, or none on timeout or when the watch has stopped. Parks the green thread while it waits.
Returns the Watch that owns the watch behind h, which stops it when dropped.

Stops the watch behind h. Restores the dispositions that were in place before the watch, except for signals whose handler another notify has replaced since. Closes the signals channel, which wakes any green thread waiting on it, and parks the calling green thread until the forwarding green thread has finished. Later calls do nothing.
Parks the green thread until the watch behind h delivers a signal and returns it. Fails with NotConnected once the watch has stopped.
fn wait_timeout_on(h: WatchHandle, millis: i64) -> Signal?
Waits up to millis milliseconds for the watch behind h to deliver a signal, and returns it, or none on timeout or when the watch has stopped. Parks the green thread while it waits.
Returns the signal with Linux number n, or none if n is outside 1 to 64. A number without a named variant gives Other(n).

Sets the disposition of each signal in signals to ignored, for the whole process. Fails with Invalid, without changing any signal, if the list contains Kill or Stop. Fails with the system error if a disposition cannot be set.
Starts delivering signals to the signals channel of the handle of the returned Watch. The watch ends when the Watch is dropped or passed to stop. Fails as notify_handle does.

Starts delivering signals to a channel and returns the view of the watch. Installs a handler for each signal, replacing the current disposition, and starts a green thread that forwards them. The caller must stop the watch with stop_on, or bind it with adopt so that dropping it does. Fails with Invalid if signals is empty or contains Kill or Stop, and with the system error if a pipe, page or handler cannot be set up, in which case nothing stays installed.
Sets the disposition of each signal in signals back to the system default, for the whole process. Fails with Invalid, without changing any signal, if the list contains Kill or Stop.
fn send(pid: i64, s: Signal) ! io.Error

Sends the signal s to the process pid. The signal is directed at the process and is delivered to any of its threads. Fails with NotFound if the process does not exist and Denied if the caller may not signal it.
Parks the green thread until one of signals arrives and returns it. Watches the signals only for the duration of the call and restores their dispositions before returning. Fails as notify does.
struct Attribute { pub key: str pub value: Value }
A key with a Value. The attribute name. The attribute value.
struct BatchOptions { pub max_queue: i64 pub max_batch: i64 pub delay: i64 pub timeout: i64 }

Settings for a batch processor. The capacity of the queue. A record offered while the queue is full is discarded and counted. Defaults to 2048. The most items passed to one export call, and the queue length that triggers an export. Defaults to 512. The time in milliseconds between exports of a partial batch. Defaults to 5000. The time in milliseconds a flush or shutdown waits for the processor. Defaults to 30000.

An instrumented operation in progress, returned by server_span and db_span and ended with end_server or end_with. A call made while no SDK is active does nothing. A call made inside an operation of the same kind joins that operation and does not end it.

struct Config { pub resource: *Resource? pub sampler: Sampler pub limits: Limits pub propagators: Propagators pub span_processors: []SpanProcessor pub metric_readers: []MetricReader pub log_processors: []LogProcessor }

The settings install builds an SDK from. With no span processors no spans are recorded, with no metric readers no metric instruments record and with no log processors no log records are emitted. The resource attached to all telemetry. none, the default, uses default_resource over the process environment. The span sampler. Defaults to a parent-based sampler that records root spans. The data limits. Defaults to Limits {}. The propagation formats. Defaults to Propagators {}. The processors that receive started and ended spans. Defaults to none. The readers that collect metrics and pass them to an exporter. Defaults to none. The processors that receive log records. Defaults to none.
struct Context { pub span: Span pub baggage: []Entry pub suppressed: bool ... }

The telemetry state of a green thread: the active span, the baggage, a flag that suppresses telemetry and the installed SDK. A Context is never modified; the with_ functions return an updated copy. A green thread holds one in its context slot, and spawn copies the slot to the new green thread. The active span, which is not recording when none was started. The baggage members in effect. Whether telemetry is switched off for work done in this context. suppressed sets it.
struct Entry { pub key: str pub value: str pub metadata: str }

A baggage member: a key and value that travel with a request across services. The member name, an HTTP token. The member value, as decoded text. The properties after the first ; in the header, kept as unparsed text, or empty.
struct Event { pub name: str pub time: i64 pub attributes: []Attribute pub dropped: i64 }

A timestamped annotation on a span. The event name. The time in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. The event attributes. The number of attributes discarded because they exceeded Limits.attributes_per_event.
enum Kind { Internal Server Client Producer Consumer }

The role a span plays in a trace. Work inside the application that does not cross a process boundary. Handling of a request from a remote caller. A request made to a remote service. The start of an asynchronous operation, such as putting a message on a queue. Handling of an asynchronous operation started by a producer.
struct Limits { pub attributes: i64 pub events: i64 pub links: i64 pub attributes_per_event: i64 pub attributes_per_link: i64 }

The most data a span or log record can hold. Data beyond a limit is discarded and counted in the matching dropped field. The most attributes on a span or log record. Defaults to 128. The most events on a span. Defaults to 128. The most links on a span. Defaults to 128. The most attributes on a span event. Defaults to 128. The most attributes on a span link. Defaults to 128.
struct Link { pub context: SpanContext pub attributes: []Attribute pub dropped: i64 }
A reference from a span to another span, usually in a different trace. The linked span. The link attributes. The number of attributes discarded because they exceeded Limits.attributes_per_link.
struct LogData { pub record: LogRecord pub observed: i64 pub context: SpanContext pub scope: Scope pub resource: *Resource pub dropped: i64 }

A log record as it reaches processors and exporters. The record, with severity_text filled in and attributes trimmed to Limits.attributes. The time emit ran, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. The span context active when the record was emitted, or an invalid context when there was no active span. The scope of the logger that emitted the record. The resource of the SDK that received the record. The number of attributes discarded because they exceeded Limits.attributes.
struct LogExporter { pub export: fn([]*LogData) -> bool pub shutdown: fn() }
Sends log records to a destination. Sends a batch of records and returns whether it was delivered. Releases the exporter's resources.
struct LogProcessor { pub on_emit: fn(*LogData) pub force_flush: fn() -> bool pub shutdown: fn() -> bool pub dropped: fn() -> i64 }

Receives log records as they are emitted. Called once for each emitted record. Exports what is pending and returns whether it succeeded. Flushes, stops and returns whether it succeeded. It also shuts the exporter down. Returns the number of records discarded because the queue was full.
struct LogRecord { pub time: i64 pub severity: i64 pub severity_text: str pub body: Value pub attributes: []Attribute pub event_name: str }

A log record built by the caller. The time of the event in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, or 0 when unknown. The severity number from 1 to 24, or 0 when unspecified. See severity_name. The severity name. When empty, emit fills it from severity. The log message or structured body. The record attributes. The name of the event the record describes, or empty.
A source of log records for one instrumentation scope. The scope recorded on every record the logger emits.

A handle to an instrument that records values of type T. Copies refer to the same instrument. An instrument made when no SDK with a metric reader is installed is inert: its calls do nothing and enabled_measure returns false. An integer T makes the metric integer valued and a floating-point T makes it floating-point.
A source of metric instruments for one instrumentation scope. The scope recorded on every instrument the meter creates.
struct MetricBatch { pub resource: *Resource pub metrics: []MetricData }
The metrics collected from one reader at one time. The resource attached to the metrics. The metrics, omitting instruments with no data points.
struct MetricData { pub scope: Scope pub name: str pub description: str pub unit: str pub kind: MetricKind pub monotonic: bool pub temporality: Temporality pub integer: bool pub points: []PointData }

A metric: the points of one instrument. The scope of the meter that created the instrument. The instrument name. The instrument description. The unit of the values, such as s or By. The aggregation kind. Whether a sum only increases. True for counters, observable counters and histograms. The temporality of the points. Not meaningful for a gauge. Whether the instrument records integers, in which case values are in PointData.int_value. The data points, one per attribute set.
struct MetricExporter { pub export: fn(MetricBatch) -> bool pub shutdown: fn() }
Sends collected metrics to a destination. Sends a batch and returns whether it was delivered. Releases the exporter's resources.

The kind of aggregation a metric holds. A running total, from a counter, an up-down counter or an observable counter. The latest value, from a gauge or an observable gauge. A distribution of recorded values in buckets.
struct MetricReader { pub exporter: MetricExporter pub interval: i64 pub timeout: i64 pub preference: Preference }

Collects metrics on a schedule and passes them to an exporter. The destination of the collected metrics. The time in milliseconds between collections. 0 or less turns periodic collection off, and the reader then exports only on a flush or shutdown. Defaults to 60000. The time in milliseconds a flush or shutdown waits for the reader. Defaults to 30000. The temporality the reader requests. Defaults to PreferCumulative.
struct Observation[T: Number] { pub value: T pub attributes: []Attribute }
One value reported by an observable instrument callback. The observed value. The attributes of the series the value belongs to. Defaults to none.

struct OtlpOptions { pub endpoint: str pub signal_endpoint: str pub headers: []header.Header pub protocol: Protocol pub gzip: bool pub timeout: i64 pub attempts: i64 pub backoff: i64 pub max_backoff: i64 }

Settings for the OTLP exporters. The collector base URL. Empty uses http://localhost:4318, or http://localhost:4317 for Grpc. Over HTTP the signal path /v1/traces, /v1/metrics or /v1/logs is appended; over gRPC only the scheme, host and port are used. The full URL of the exporter's own signal, used instead of endpoint when not empty. Nothing is appended to it. Headers added to every request. The wire protocol. Defaults to HttpProtobuf. Whether to compress the body with gzip. Defaults to false. The time in milliseconds one request may take. Defaults to 10000. The most attempts for one export, the first included. Defaults to 5. The wait in milliseconds before the first retry. It doubles for each further retry up to max_backoff, with equal jitter, so each wait is between half and all of that delay. A wait the server asks for with Retry-After or RetryInfo raises the wait but does not lower it. Defaults to 1000. The longest wait between retries in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000.
struct ParentSamplers { pub root: Sampler pub remote_sampled: Sampler pub remote_not_sampled: Sampler pub local_sampled: Sampler pub local_not_sampled: Sampler }

The samplers a ParentBased sampler uses for each kind of parent. Used when the span has no valid parent. Used when the parent came from another process and was sampled. Defaults to AlwaysOn. Used when the parent came from another process and was not sampled. Defaults to AlwaysOff. Used when the parent is in this process and was sampled. Defaults to AlwaysOn. Used when the parent is in this process and was not sampled. Defaults to AlwaysOff.

struct PointData { pub attributes: []Attribute pub start: i64 pub time: i64 pub int_value: i64 pub double_value: f64 pub count: u64 pub sum: f64 pub min: f64 pub max: f64 pub bounds: []f64 pub buckets: []u64 }

One aggregated data point of a metric, for one set of attributes. The attributes that identify the series. The start of the point's interval in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. The collection time in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. The value of a sum or gauge when MetricData.integer is true. The value of a sum or gauge when MetricData.integer is false. The number of measurements aggregated into the point. The sum of the recorded values of a histogram. The smallest value recorded in a histogram. The largest value recorded in a histogram. The upper bounds of a histogram's buckets, in increasing order. Empty for other kinds. The number of values in each bucket of a histogram. There is one more bucket than bounds: bucket i counts values up to and including bounds[i] that are above the previous bound, and the last counts values above the final bound. Empty for other kinds.

The temporality a MetricReader asks for. Every instrument reports cumulatively. Counters, histograms and observable counters report as deltas and the other instruments cumulatively. Synchronous counters and histograms report as deltas and every other instrument cumulatively.
struct Propagators { pub trace_context: bool pub baggage: bool }
Which context propagation formats inject and extract use. Whether the W3C traceparent and tracestate headers are used. Defaults to true. Whether the W3C baggage header is used. Defaults to true.
The OTLP wire protocol an exporter uses. OTLP over HTTP/1.1 with a protobuf body. OTLP over HTTP/1.1 with a JSON body. OTLP over gRPC on HTTP/2, with prior knowledge for http:// URLs.
struct Resource { pub attributes: []Attribute pub schema_url: str }
The entity that produces telemetry, described by attributes such as service.name. The resource attributes. The schema URL of the attribute conventions, or empty.
enum Sampler { AlwaysOn AlwaysOff TraceIdRatio(f64) ParentBased(*ParentSamplers) }

The rule that decides whether a new span is recorded and exported. Records every span. Records a fixed fraction of traces chosen from the trace id. ratio is the fraction from 0.0 to 1.0; 1.0 or more records every trace and 0.0 or less records none. The decision depends only on the trace id, so every service in a trace that uses the same ratio agrees. Records no span. Chooses a sampler from the span's parent, as set out in ParentSamplers.
struct Scope { pub name: str pub version: str pub schema_url: str }
The instrumentation scope: the library or component that produces telemetry. The scope name, such as the module path. The scope version, or empty. The schema URL, or empty.
An owner of an SdkHandle that shuts the SDK down when it is dropped. The SDK state.
struct SdkHandle { pub resource: *Resource pub sampler: Sampler pub limits: Limits pub propagators: Propagators pub span_processors: []SpanProcessor pub log_processors: []LogProcessor ... }

The state of an installed SDK, shared by the green threads that inherit it. Obtained from install_handle, provider or Sdk.handle. The _on functions take a handle. The resource attached to all telemetry. The span sampler. The data limits. The propagation formats. The span processors. The log processors.
The telemetry signal an OTLP exporter carries. Spans. Metrics. Log records.

A handle to a span. Copies of a Span refer to the same underlying span. A span that is not recording, such as one started without an SDK or one the sampler rejected, ignores every update and has no data. The span's context, also set on a span that is not recording.
struct SpanContext { pub trace_hi: u64 pub trace_lo: u64 pub span_id: u64 pub flags: u8 pub state: str pub remote: bool }

Identifies a span for propagation: the W3C trace context of a trace id, a span id and flags. The high 64 bits of the 128-bit trace id. The low 64 bits of the 128-bit trace id. The 64-bit span id. The W3C trace flags. Bit 0 is set when the trace is sampled. The tracestate header value that travels with the context, or empty. Whether the context was extracted from a request made by another process.

struct SpanData { pub name: str pub kind: Kind pub context: SpanContext pub parent: SpanContext pub scope: Scope pub resource: *Resource pub start: i64 pub end: i64 pub attributes: []Attribute pub events: []Event pub links: []Link pub status: Status pub dropped_attributes: i64 pub dropped_events: i64 pub dropped_links: i64 ... }

A recording span as it reaches processors and exporters. Its fields are final once end has been called. The span name, which update_name can change while the span is recording. The span's role. The span's own context. The parent's context, or an invalid context for a root span. The instrumentation scope that started the span. The resource of the SDK that recorded the span. The start time in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. The end time in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch, or 0 while the span is recording. The span attributes, at most Limits.attributes. The span events, at most Limits.events. The span links, at most Limits.links. The span outcome. The number of attributes discarded because they exceeded Limits.attributes. The number of events discarded because they exceeded Limits.events. The number of links discarded because they exceeded Limits.links.
struct SpanExporter { pub export: fn([]*SpanData) -> bool pub shutdown: fn() }
Sends finished spans to a destination. Sends a batch of ended spans and returns whether it was delivered. Releases the exporter's resources.
struct SpanProcessor { pub on_start: fn(*SpanData) pub on_end: fn(*SpanData) pub force_flush: fn() -> bool pub shutdown: fn() -> bool pub dropped: fn() -> i64 }

Receives spans as they start and end. Called when a recording span starts, before start returns. Called once when a recording span ends. Exports what is pending and returns whether it succeeded. Flushes, stops and returns whether it succeeded. It also shuts the exporter down. Returns the number of spans discarded because the queue was full.
struct StartOptions { pub kind: Kind pub parent: *Context? pub attributes: []Attribute pub links: []Link pub start: i64 }

Optional settings for start_with. The span's role. Defaults to Internal. The context to parent the span under. none, the default, uses the calling green thread's context. Attributes the span starts with. Links the span starts with. The start time in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch. 0, the default, uses the current time.
The outcome of the operation a span records. No outcome was recorded. The operation succeeded. Once set, a later Failed does not replace it. The operation failed, with a description in message.

How a metric's values are accumulated across collections. Each point covers the time from the start of the series to the collection. Each point covers the time since the previous collection, and the series starts again afterwards.
A source of spans for one instrumentation scope. The scope recorded on every span the tracer starts.
enum Value { Empty Str(str) Bool(bool) Int(i64) Double(f64) Bytes([]u8) Array([]Value) Map([]Attribute) }
A telemetry attribute value. No value. A string. A boolean. A signed 64-bit integer. A 64-bit floating-point number. A byte string. A list of values. A nested set of attributes.
fn end_server(c: Call, route: str, status: i64)

Finishes the server call c for a response with status. A non-empty route renames the span to the method and route and sets http.route. http.response.status_code is set, and a status of 500 or more also sets error.type and a failed status. A call that owns the span then ends it, restores the context that was current when the call began and records the http.server.request.duration histogram, in seconds, with the method, route, status code, protocol version and error type.

Finishes the database call c. A non-empty error_type sets error.type and a failed status carrying the same text. A call that owns the span then ends it, restores the context that was current when the call began and records the db.client.operation.duration histogram, in seconds, with the system, namespace, operation, collection, response code, server address, port and error type that were set.
Sets the attribute a on the call's span. The attribute is also kept for use as a metric attribute when the call ends. Nothing happens when the call is not recording.
Reports whether the call is tied to a span, which is false when no SDK was active when it began.

Builds an SDK from config, installs it for the calling green thread and returns the Sdk that owns it. Green threads spawned afterwards inherit it. Periodic metric readers start collecting in the background. Dropping the result shuts the SDK down, so a program keeps it for its lifetime, usually in main.
Builds an SDK from config and installs it for the calling green thread, like install, but returns the bare handle. The caller shuts it down with shutdown_on.
Makes c the calling green thread's context and returns the context it replaces. Pass the result to detach to restore it.
Returns the value of the baggage member key in c, or none when there is none.
Restores outer, a context returned by attach, as the calling green thread's context.

Returns a context with the span and baggage found in headers. A valid traceparent header becomes the active span, a remote one with the joined tracestate headers as its state, and a non-empty baggage with at least one valid member replaces the baggage. Repeated headers are joined with commas. Each part is read only when its propagator is on. Returns c itself when nothing was found.
fn in_context[T](c: *Context, body: fn() -> T) -> T
Runs body with c as the calling green thread's context and returns its result. The previous context is restored when body returns.

Writes the trace and baggage headers for c into headers, replacing any of the same name. traceparent is written when the SDK's trace-context propagator is on and c has a valid span, and tracestate with it when the state is not empty. baggage is written when the baggage propagator is on and the member list formats to something. Both propagators are on when c has no SDK.
fn set_baggage(c: *Context, key: str, value: str) -> *Context
Returns a copy of c whose baggage has key set to value and an empty metadata. An existing member with the same key is replaced, and the new member is placed last.
Returns a copy of c in which telemetry is suppressed: no spans, metrics or log records are produced and the HTTP hooks stay idle.
Returns a copy of c carrying entries as its baggage in place of the existing members.
Returns a copy of c whose active span is s.
Returns the line that describes a log record: log <scope> <severity> "<body>", then the trace and span ids when the record has a span, then the attributes.
fn batch_log_processor(exporter: LogExporter, options: BatchOptions) -> LogProcessor
Returns a processor that queues records and exports them in batches from a background green thread. Queueing, flushing and the dropped count follow batch_span_processor.

Returns a processor that exports each record, alone, from the green thread that emitted it. The result of export is ignored. force_flush returns true, shutdown shuts the exporter down and returns true, and dropped returns 0.
fn debug(l: Logger, body: str, attributes: []Attribute)
Emits a record with severity DEBUG (number 5), the string body and attributes, timestamped now.

Emits the log record r to every log processor of the installed SDK. Nothing happens when no SDK is installed, the context is suppressed, there are no log processors or the SDK has been shut down. The record's time is passed through as given. The span context of the calling green thread is attached when it has a valid one.
fn error(l: Logger, body: str, attributes: []Attribute)
Emits a record with severity ERROR (number 17), the string body and attributes, timestamped now.
fn fatal(l: Logger, body: str, attributes: []Attribute)
Emits a record with severity FATAL (number 21), the string body and attributes, timestamped now.
fn info(l: Logger, body: str, attributes: []Attribute)
Emits a record with severity INFO (number 9), the string body and attributes, timestamped now.
fn trace(l: Logger, body: str, attributes: []Attribute)
Emits a record with severity TRACE (number 1), the string body and attributes, timestamped now.
fn warn(l: Logger, body: str, attributes: []Attribute)
Emits a record with severity WARN (number 13), the string body and attributes, timestamped now.
fn add[T: Number](i: Measure[T], value: T, attributes: []Attribute)

Adds value to a counter or an up-down counter for the series identified by attributes. A counter ignores a negative value and any other kind of instrument ignores the call. Once the instrument holds 1999 series, a new attribute set is folded into one series with the attribute otel.metric.overflow set to true. A repeated key in attributes keeps its last value.
Reports whether the instrument records, which is false when it was made without an SDK or without a metric reader. Use it to skip work that only builds a measurement.
fn record[T: Number](i: Measure[T], value: T, attributes: []Attribute)

Records value on a histogram or a gauge for the series identified by attributes. A histogram ignores a negative value and any other kind of instrument ignores the call. The series limit and attribute handling are those of add.
fn counter[T: Number](m: Meter, name: str, unit: str, description: str) -> Measure[T]

Creates a counter named name, a sum that only increases; add adds to it and ignores negative values. unit and description are free text. A second instrument with the same scope and name returns the first one unchanged.
fn gauge[T: Number](m: Meter, name: str, unit: str, description: str) -> Measure[T]
Creates a gauge named name that keeps the last value record was given for each attribute set. A second instrument with the same scope and name returns the first one unchanged.
fn histogram[T: Number](m: Meter, name: str, unit: str, description: str, bounds: []f64) -> Measure[T]

Creates a histogram named name that record adds values to. bounds are the increasing upper bounds of the buckets; an empty list uses default_bounds. record ignores negative values. A second instrument with the same scope and name returns the first one unchanged.
fn observable_counter[T: Number](m: Meter, name: str, unit: str, description: str, callback: fn() -> []Observation[T])

Registers an observable counter named name whose total callback returns on every collection. The callback runs each time the reader collects; it returns the current cumulative value for each attribute set and a repeated attribute set keeps the first. With delta temporality the reported value is the change since the previous collection.
fn observable_gauge[T: Number](m: Meter, name: str, unit: str, description: str, callback: fn() -> []Observation[T])
Registers an observable gauge named name whose current value callback returns on every collection. See observable_counter for how the callback is used. A gauge always reports its latest observation.
fn observable_up_down_counter[T: Number](m: Meter, name: str, unit: str, description: str, callback: fn() -> []Observation[T])
Registers an observable up-down counter named name whose current value callback returns on every collection. See observable_counter for how the callback is used.
fn up_down_counter[T: Number](m: Meter, name: str, unit: str, description: str) -> Measure[T]
Creates an up-down counter named name, a sum that add can both increase and decrease. A second instrument with the same scope and name returns the first one unchanged.
Returns the OTLP ExportMetricsServiceRequest for batch, as protobuf, or as OTLP JSON when json_format is true. Metrics are grouped by scope under the batch's resource.

Returns the lines that describe a metric. The first line gives the scope, name, kind, temporality and unit, and each data point adds an indented line with its value, or for a histogram its count, sum, minimum, maximum and bucket counts, followed by its attributes. A gauge has no temporality.
Returns the collector base URL: o.endpoint, or the local default for the protocol when it is empty.
Returns an exporter that sends log records to the collector. Delivery, retries and shutdown follow otlp_span_exporter.
Returns an exporter that sends metric batches to the collector. Delivery, retries and shutdown follow otlp_span_exporter; export returns false after shutdown.

Returns an exporter that sends spans to the collector. export returns true once the collector accepts a batch and false when it rejects it or every attempt fails; an empty batch returns true without a request, and after shutdown every call returns false. HTTP statuses 429, 502, 503 and 504, and a failed connection, are retried after the backoff or the server's Retry-After. Over gRPC, the status codes CANCELLED, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, ABORTED, OUT_OF_RANGE, UNAVAILABLE and DATA_LOSS are retried and RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED is retried when the response carries a RetryInfo delay. The processors and metric readers call export with telemetry suppressed. shutdown closes idle connections.
Returns a new resource holding the attributes of base with extra added; an attribute in extra replaces one in base with the same key. The schema URL of base is kept and base is not modified.
Returns the sampler's description in the form the OpenTelemetry specification uses, such as AlwaysOnSampler or TraceIdRatioBased{0.25}.
Returns a ParentBased sampler that follows its parent's sampling decision and uses root for spans without a valid parent.
fn should_sample(s: Sampler, parent: SpanContext, trace_lo: u64) -> bool

Reports whether a span is sampled. parent is the parent span context, which is invalid for a root span, and trace_lo is the low 64 bits of the new span's trace id. TraceIdRatio compares the low 63 bits of the trace id with the ratio.
fn collect(sdk: Sdk, reader: i64) -> MetricBatch
Collects the metrics of the reader at index reader in Config.metric_readers without exporting them. See collect_on.
Returns the number of log records the log processors discarded because their queue was full.
Returns the number of spans the span processors discarded because their queue was full.
Flushes and stops the SDK. See shutdown_on.
Returns an Sdk that owns h, so that dropping it shuts h down. Nothing is installed.

Collects the metrics of the reader at index reader in Config.metric_readers. Delta series are reset by the call, so metrics are normally collected by the reader that exports them. Instruments with no data points are left out.
Returns the number of log records the log processors of sdk discarded because their queue was full.
Returns the number of spans the span processors of sdk discarded because their queue was full.

Exports every span and log record waiting in a processor and collects and exports every metric reader, then returns whether all of them succeeded. Each step waits up to the processor's or reader's timeout.

Flushes and stops the SDK and returns whether every processor and reader succeeded. After the call no new spans or log records are recorded, and each exporter is shut down. Returns false when the SDK was already shut down.
fn add_event(s: Span, name: str, attributes: []Attribute)
Adds an event named name with attributes, timestamped with the current time.
fn add_event_at(s: Span, name: str, attributes: []Attribute, at: i64)

Adds an event named name with attributes at the time at, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch; 0 or less uses the current time. Attributes beyond Limits.attributes_per_event are discarded and counted in the event. An event beyond Limits.events is discarded and counted in SpanData.dropped_events. Nothing happens on a span that is not recording or has ended.

Adds the link l to the span. Attributes beyond Limits.attributes_per_link are discarded. A link beyond Limits.links is discarded and counted in SpanData.dropped_links. Nothing happens on a span that is not recording or has ended.
Ends the span at the current time. See end_at.

Ends the span at at, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch; 0 or less uses the current time. The span stops recording and each span processor's on_end is called with its data. Ending a span that is not recording or has already ended does nothing.
Reports whether the span is recording, which is true from the time it starts until end is called, and always false for a span that is not recording.
fn record_exception(s: Span, kind: str, message: str)
Records an exception as an event named exception with the attributes exception.type set to kind and exception.message set to message. The span's status is not changed.

Sets the attribute a, replacing an attribute with the same key. A new key beyond Limits.attributes is discarded and counted in SpanData.dropped_attributes. Nothing happens on a span that is not recording or has ended.
Sets each attribute in attributes with set_attribute.
fn set_int(s: Span, key: str, value: i64)
Sets the integer attribute key to value.

Sets the span's status. Unset changes nothing. Ok always takes effect and is final. Failed takes effect unless the status is already Ok, and a later Failed replaces an earlier one. Nothing happens on a span that is not recording or has ended.
fn set_string(s: Span, key: str, value: str)
Sets the string attribute key to value.
Renames the span while it is recording. Nothing happens on a span that is not recording or has ended.
Returns sc as a traceparent header value of version 00, with flag 01 when sampled and 00 otherwise.
Reports whether the sampled flag is set in sc.
Returns the span id as 8 bytes, most significant first.
Returns the span id as 16 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
Returns the trace id as 16 bytes, most significant first.
Returns the trace id as 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits.
Reports whether sc has a non-zero trace id and a non-zero span id.
Returns a span that is not recording and carries sc. Use it to make a context extracted from elsewhere the parent of new spans.

Returns the lines that describe a span. The first line is span <scope> "<name>" <kind> trace=<id> span=<id> parent=<id or -> start=<ns> duration=<ns>ns status=<status> followed by the attributes as key=value. Each event adds a line starting event and each link a line starting link.
fn batch_span_processor(exporter: SpanExporter, options: BatchOptions) -> SpanProcessor

Returns a processor that queues sampled spans and exports them in batches from a background green thread. on_end never blocks: a span offered while the queue holds options.max_queue spans is discarded and counted by dropped. The worker exports when options.max_batch spans have queued and when options.delay milliseconds pass with spans waiting. force_flush and shutdown wait up to options.timeout milliseconds for the worker and return false on a timeout; shutdown also shuts down the exporter, and spans ended afterwards are ignored. Spans that are not sampled are never queued.

Returns a processor that exports each sampled span, alone, from the green thread that ended it. The result of export is ignored. force_flush returns true, shutdown shuts the exporter down and returns true, and dropped returns 0.
fn in_span[T](t: Tracer, name: str, body: fn(Span) -> T) -> T

Runs body inside a new span named name and returns its result. The span is the calling green thread's current span while body runs, so spans started in body become its children. It ends, and the previous context is restored, when body returns. When the span is not recording the context is left unchanged and body still runs.
fn start(t: Tracer, name: str) -> Span
Starts a span named name with the default StartOptions.
fn start_with(t: Tracer, name: str, o: StartOptions) -> Span

Starts a span named name under the parent chosen by o and returns it. The span is not made the calling green thread's current span; in_span does that. The span is not recording and carries its parent's context when there is no SDK, the parent context is suppressed, the SDK has no span processors or it has been shut down. Otherwise the span gets a new span id and inherits the parent's trace id and tracestate, or starts a new trace when the parent is not valid. The sampler then decides: a rejected span has the sampled flag clear and is not recorded, but its context can still be propagated. A recorded span has the sampled flag set, attributes and links trimmed to the SDK limits, and every span processor's on_start called with it. The caller ends the span with end.
Returns a readable text form of v. Empty is the empty string, bytes are hexadecimal, an array is [a, b] and a map is {key=value ...}.
fn attr(key: str, value: Value) -> Attribute
Returns an attribute holding any Value.
Returns an attribute holding the bytes value.
fn boolean(key: str, value: bool) -> Attribute
Returns an attribute holding the boolean value.

Returns an SDK configuration read from the standard OTEL_* variables in env. The span, metric and log exporters come from OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER, OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER and OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER, each a comma-separated list that defaults to otlp. otlp is an OTLP exporter built by otlp_options_from_env and console writes to standard error; any other name, including none, adds nothing. OTLP spans and logs go through batch processors set by OTEL_BSP_* and OTEL_BLRP_* (the log schedule delay defaults to 1000), console spans and logs through simple processors, and metrics through readers set by OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL and OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_TIMEOUT and, for OTLP, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE. The limits come from the OTEL_*_COUNT_LIMIT variables, the propagators from OTEL_PROPAGATORS (tracecontext and baggage) and the resource from default_resource.

Returns an exporter that passes the line from format_log for each record to write. export returns false when write fails, after which the remaining records of the batch are not written; shutdown does nothing.
Returns an exporter that passes each line from format_metric to write. export returns false when write fails, after which the remaining lines of the batch are not written; shutdown does nothing.
Returns an exporter that passes each line from format_span to write. export returns false when write fails, after which the remaining lines of the batch are not written; shutdown does nothing.
Returns the calling green thread's context, or an empty root context with no SDK when none is set.
Returns the calling green thread's active span, or a non-recording span with an invalid context when none is set.
fn db_span(scope: str, system: str, operation: str, collection: str, query: str) -> Call

Starts a client span for a database call under scope and makes it the calling green thread's context. system is the db.system.name. An empty operation is taken from the first word of query, in upper case. The span is named from the operation and collection, from the operation alone or from system, and carries the system, operation, collection and query text where present. Returns an idle call when no SDK is active, and a call that does not own the span when a database call is already in progress, so a nested call merges into the outer one.
Returns the default bucket bounds for a histogram: 0 to 10000.

Returns the resource for a process, read from the environment map env. It holds telemetry.sdk.name and telemetry.sdk.language, the pairs in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, and service.name from OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, which overrides the same key in the pairs. When no service.name results, it is unknown_service: followed by the process name from /proc/self/comm, or unknown_service when that cannot be read.
fn double(key: str, value: f64) -> Attribute
Returns an attribute holding the floating-point value.
Returns bucket bounds suited to durations in seconds: 0.005 to 10.
Reports whether telemetry is on for the calling green thread, which is when an SDK is installed and the context is not suppressed.
Returns the OTLP ExportLogsServiceRequest for logs, as protobuf, or as OTLP JSON when json_format is true. Records are grouped by resource and scope.
Returns the OTLP ExportTraceServiceRequest for spans, as protobuf, or as OTLP JSON when json_format is true. Spans are grouped by resource and scope.
Returns the current context updated with the span and baggage found in headers. See extract_into.
Returns the attributes as key=value pairs separated by spaces, formatted with format_value.
Formats baggage members as a baggage header value. Values are percent-encoded. Members whose key is not a token are skipped, and output stops at 180 members or 8192 bytes.
fn instrument_sql(db: sql.ConnectionHandle, scope: str, namespace: str, server: str, port: i64) -> sql.ConnectionHandle

Returns a connection handle whose query, each and execute run inside database calls and whose other functions are those of db. namespace is set as db.namespace when it is not empty, and server and port as server.address and server.port. The operation comes from the first word of the statement and the collection is not set. The drivers apply it once, through std/sql/driver.
fn int(key: str, value: i64) -> Attribute
Returns an attribute holding the integer value.
Returns an attribute holding an array of the integers in values.
Returns the context that identifies no span: zero ids, no flags and no state.
Returns a logger whose records carry an instrumentation scope named name.
Returns the value of the first attribute named key, or none when there is none.
Returns a meter whose instruments carry an instrumentation scope named name.

Validates and canonicalises a W3C tracestate header value. Members are trimmed and rejoined with ,; empty members are dropped. Returns none when a key or value breaks the W3C syntax, a key repeats or there are more than 32 members. An empty value returns an empty string.
fn otlp_options_from_env(env: [str: str], signal: Signal) -> OtlpOptions

Returns the OTLP exporter options for signal from the environment map env. The OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ variables ENDPOINT, HEADERS, PROTOCOL, COMPRESSION and TIMEOUT apply to all signals, and the same name with _TRACES_, _METRICS_ or _LOGS_ after OTLP overrides it for one; headers from the two merge, the signal's winning on a clash. A signal's own ENDPOINT is the full URL, kept in OtlpOptions.signal_endpoint. PROTOCOL is http/json or grpc, and anything else is http/protobuf. COMPRESSION is on only for gzip, and TIMEOUT is in milliseconds.

Parses a W3C baggage header value into members. A member with a missing =, an invalid token key, a bad %XX escape or a forbidden byte in its value is skipped, and values are percent-decoded. Text after the first ; of a member is kept in metadata. A repeated key keeps its last value in its original position. At most 180 members are returned, and none when the value is longer than 8192 bytes.

Parses a comma-separated list of key=value pairs, as in OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS. Whitespace around keys and values is trimmed and %XX escapes are decoded. Members without a = or with an empty key are skipped, and a later member replaces an earlier one with the same key.

Parses a W3C traceparent header value. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Returns none when the value is malformed: wrong length or separators, uppercase or non-hexadecimal digits, version ff, a version 00 value with extra bytes, or an all-zero trace id or span id. The result is marked remote, keeps only the sampled bit of the flags and has an empty state.
Returns the SDK installed for the calling green thread, or none when there is none.

Runs body with telemetry suppressed for the calling green thread and returns its result. The previous context is restored when body returns. Every exporter runs under it, so the exporter itself is not traced.

Returns the sampler named by OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER in env. The names are always_on, always_off, traceidratio, parentbased_always_on, parentbased_always_off and parentbased_traceidratio, ignoring case. A missing or unrecognised name gives parentbased_always_on. The ratio samplers read OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG, which is 1.0 when missing, not a number or outside 0.0 to 1.0.
fn server_span(scope: str, r: http.Request) -> Call

Starts a server span for the HTTP request r under scope and makes it the calling green thread's context. The parent is extracted from the request's traceparent, tracestate and baggage headers. The span is named after the method, or HTTP for a method outside the standard set, and carries the request method, url.path, url.query, server.address, client.address, user_agent.original and network.protocol.version where known. Returns an idle call when no SDK is active, and a call that does not own the span when a server call is already in progress, so a framework can name and finish the span that std/http opened.

Installs an SDK configured from the process environment and returns the Sdk that owns it. When OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is true, ignoring case, the SDK is built with no processors and is not installed, so every call stays a no-op. See config_from_env and install.

Returns the OpenTelemetry name for the severity number n. Numbers 1 to 24 map to TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR and FATAL in groups of four, with 2 to 4 appended after the first, such as INFO3. Any other number returns an empty string.
fn span[T](name: str, body: fn(Span) -> T) -> T
Runs body inside a span named name from the tracer for the scope std/otel. See in_span.
fn sql_each(db: sql.ConnectionHandle, scope: str, operation: str, collection: str, query: str, values: []sql.Value, visit: fn([]sql.Column, []sql.Value) -> bool) ! sql.Error
Runs db.each inside a database call, passing each row to visit. The span and errors are handled as in sql_query.
fn sql_execute(db: sql.ConnectionHandle, scope: str, operation: str, collection: str, query: str, values: []sql.Value) -> i64 ! sql.Error
Runs db.execute inside a database call and returns the affected row count. The span and errors are handled as in sql_query.
fn sql_query(db: sql.ConnectionHandle, scope: str, operation: str, collection: str, query: str, values: []sql.Value) -> sql.Rows ! sql.Error

Runs db.query inside a database call and returns its rows. operation and collection name what the statement does and where; see db_span. An sql.Error is returned unchanged and its variant name becomes error.type; for a Server error the code is used and also set as db.response.status_code. With no SDK active the query runs directly.
Returns a function that writes a line and a newline to standard error. Short writes and interrupted writes are repeated, and a write that fails returns its error.
fn string(key: str, value: str) -> Attribute
Returns an attribute holding the string value.
Returns an attribute holding an array of the strings in values.
Returns a tracer whose spans carry an instrumentation scope named name.
Returns the last segment of p after trailing slashes are removed. Returns "." for the empty string and "/" when p consists only of slashes.

Returns the shortest equivalent of p by lexical processing alone, without touching the file system. Repeated slashes and . segments are dropped and a .. removes the segment before it. A leading .. is kept in a relative path and dropped in an absolute one. A trailing slash is removed. An empty result is "." for a relative path and "/" for an absolute one.
Returns p without its last segment, cleaned. Returns "." when p contains no slash, and "/" for a path directly under the root.

Returns the extension of the last segment of p, including the leading dot, or the empty string when it has none. The extension starts at the last . in the final segment, so "a.tar.gz" gives ".gz" and a name that starts with a dot such as ".profile" gives the whole name. A path that ends in a slash has no extension.
Returns true when p starts with /. The empty string is not absolute.

Joins the non-empty parts with / and returns the cleaned result. Empty parts are skipped. Returns the empty string, not ".", when no part is non-empty. Later absolute parts do not replace earlier ones: join(["a", "/b"]) is "a/b".
fn matches(pattern: str, name: str) -> bool

Returns true when name matches the glob pattern in full. * matches any run of characters, including none. ? matches one character. [abc] and [a-z] match one character of the set; a leading ! or ^ negates it, and a ] right after the opening bracket is a member of the set. \ makes the next pattern character literal. *, ? and sets never match /; a / in the pattern matches only a / in the name. An unterminated [ matches nothing. The match is bytewise and does not treat a leading dot specially.
Returns the last segment of p without its extension. The segment is taken as base returns it and the suffix as ext returns it from that segment.
struct Duplex { pub input: Reader pub output: Writer }
The two pipe ends that serve one bidirectional stream. Reads the bytes the stream delivers. Writes the bytes to send on the stream.
struct FlushResult { pub completed: bool pub canceled: bool }
The outcome of a flush. Whether the reader or the writer has finished, so there is no point in writing more. Whether cancel_pending_flush ended the flush early.
struct Options { pub pause: i64 pub resume: i64 pub segment_size: i64 }

Tuning for a pipe: when a writer is held back and how large the buffer segments are. The number of committed, unconsumed bytes at which flush starts to park the writer. The number of unconsumed bytes below which the reader's advance_to wakes a parked writer. The smallest size, in bytes, of each buffer segment the writer allocates.
struct Pipe { pub reader: Reader pub writer: Writer }
The two ends of a pipe. Use one green thread for the writer and one for the reader. The end that reads. The end that writes.
struct ReadResult { pub buffer: Sequence pub completed: bool pub canceled: bool }

The outcome of a read: the bytes available, and whether the writer has finished or the read was cancelled. All bytes that were flushed and not yet consumed, including bytes that earlier reads examined but did not consume. Whether the writer has finished, so that no data follows buffer. Whether cancel_pending_read ended the read. buffer can be empty.
The owner of the reading end of a pipe. Dropping it completes the reader, so a writer never waits for an abandoned reader. The copyable view of the reading end.
A copyable view of the reading end of a pipe, for use from a green thread that does not own the reader. Releasing a handle does not complete the reader; complete_reader_on or the owning Reader does.
struct Sequence { pub start: i64 pub end: i64 ... }

A read-only view of a range of the bytes that have gone through a pipe, which can span several buffer segments. Offsets are positions in the whole stream, counted from the first byte written. A sequence shares the pipe's buffer segments and does not copy them, and it keeps them alive after the reader has consumed past them. The stream offset of the first byte of the sequence. The stream offset just past the last byte of the sequence.
A cursor that reads values from a Sequence and tracks its position.
The owner of the writing end of a pipe. Dropping it completes the writer, so a reader never waits for an abandoned writer. The copyable view of the writing end.
A copyable view of the writing end of a pipe, for use from a green thread that does not own the writer. Releasing a handle does not complete the writer; complete_writer_on or the owning Writer does.
Returns a new pipe with the given options. Bytes written to the Writer become readable from the Reader after flush.
fn advance_to(r: Reader, consumed: i64, examined: i64)
Reports how much of the last read was consumed and examined. Does the same as advance_to_on on the reader's handle.
Consumes and examines everything in result.
Makes the reader's current or next read return early. Does the same as cancel_pending_read_on on the reader's handle.
Finishes the reading end. Does the same as complete_reader_on on the reader's handle.
Waits for data and returns the bytes available. Does the same as read_on on the reader's handle.
Returns the available bytes without waiting. Does the same as try_read_on on the reader's handle.
Returns the Reader that owns the reading end behind h, which completes it when dropped.
fn advance_to_on(h: ReaderHandle, consumed: i64, examined: i64)

Reports how much of the data returned by reading was consumed and how much was examined. Both arguments are stream offsets, the same as Sequence.start and Sequence.end. Bytes before consumed are released. The next read_on parks until data beyond examined arrives, so a parser that needs more data than it has passes the end of the buffer as examined. consumed cannot go backwards or past the flushed data, and examined is at least consumed. Wakes a parked writer when fewer than resume bytes remain unconsumed.
Makes the current or next read of the pipe return early with canceled set, possibly with an empty buffer. The request lasts until a read returns.
Finishes the reading end of the pipe. Wakes a parked writer, whose flush reports completed, and a waiting read_on, which fails with NotConnected. Later calls do nothing.

Waits until the writer has flushed bytes beyond the examined position, finished, or the read is cancelled, and returns everything not yet consumed. Parks the green thread while it waits. Call advance_to_on afterwards to say how much was consumed and examined, otherwise the next call returns the same bytes at once. Fails with NotConnected after the reader has completed, and with the writer's error from fail_writer_on once no flushed bytes remain.
Returns the bytes not yet consumed if there are bytes beyond the examined position or the writer has finished, and none otherwise. Does not park. Returns none after the reader has completed.
fn byte_at(q: Sequence, position: i64) -> u8
Returns the byte at stream offset position, or 0 if no segment of q holds it. The offset is not checked against the bounds of q.
Returns the first contiguous slice of q, or an empty slice if q is empty.
fn index_of(q: Sequence, b: u8) -> i64
Returns the stream offset of the first byte of q equal to b, or -1 if there is none.
Returns whether q has no bytes.
Returns the number of bytes in q.
Returns a SequenceReader positioned at the start of q.
fn slice(q: Sequence, from: i64, to: i64) -> Sequence
Returns the part of q from stream offset from to to. The offsets are clamped to the bounds of q, and an empty sequence results if to is before from. Shares the bytes with q.
Returns the bytes of q as contiguous slices, in order. The slices are views of the pipe's buffer and are not copies.
Returns a copy of the bytes of q as one slice.
Returns the stream offset of the next unread byte. This is an offset in the same coordinates as Sequence.start, not a count of the bytes read.
Returns whether the unread bytes begin with expected, without advancing.
Returns the next byte and advances past it, or none at the end.
Returns the next byte without advancing, or none at the end.
Reads size bytes as a big-endian unsigned integer and advances past them, or returns none and does not move if fewer than size remain. size is at most 8.
Returns the next n bytes and advances past them, or none and does not move if fewer than n remain.
Reads size bytes as a little-endian unsigned integer and advances past them, or returns none and does not move if fewer than size remain. size is at most 8.
Returns the next line without its terminator and advances past it. A line ends at \n, and a \r just before it is removed too. Returns none and does not move if the unread bytes contain no \n.
Returns the bytes before the next delimiter and advances past the delimiter. Returns none and does not move if there is no delimiter in the unread bytes.
Returns the number of bytes not yet read.
Advances over n bytes and returns true, or returns false and does not move if fewer than n remain.
Returns the bytes not yet read as a Sequence.
Records that n bytes of the memory from get_memory were filled. Does the same as advance_on on the writer's handle.
Makes the writer's current or next flush return early. Does the same as cancel_pending_flush_on on the writer's handle.
Finishes the writing end. Does the same as complete_writer_on on the writer's handle.
Finishes the writing end with the error e. Does the same as fail_writer_on on the writer's handle.
Makes the written bytes readable and applies backpressure. Does the same as flush_on on the writer's handle.
Returns writable memory at the end of the pipe's buffer. Does the same as get_memory_on on the writer's handle.
Copies data into the pipe's buffer without flushing it. Does the same as write_on on the writer's handle.
Writes data and flushes the pipe. Does the same as write_and_flush_on on the writer's handle.
Returns the Writer that owns the writing end behind h, which completes it when dropped.
Records that n bytes of the memory from get_memory_on were filled. Does nothing once the writer has finished. The bytes are not visible to the reader until flush_on.
Makes the current or next flush of the pipe return early with canceled set. The request lasts until a flush returns.
Finishes the writing end of the pipe. Makes the bytes written so far readable and wakes the reader. The reader consumes what remains and then sees completed. Later calls do nothing.

Finishes the writing end of the pipe with the error e. Bytes written but not yet flushed are discarded. The reader consumes the bytes already flushed, and then its read fails with e. Does nothing if the writer has already finished.

Makes every byte written so far readable, wakes a waiting reader, and parks the green thread while the reader is too far behind. The writer parks while the reader has pause or more unconsumed bytes, until the reader consumes down to resume, completes, starts waiting for data or the flush is cancelled. The result reports whether the reader or the writer has completed, and whether cancel_pending_flush_on ended the flush.

Returns a slice of at least hint bytes, or at least one when hint is less than 1, to write into. Reuses the free space of the last segment when it is large enough and otherwise allocates a segment of hint bytes or segment_size, whichever is larger. The slice may be longer than hint. Call advance_on with the number of bytes filled; the bytes are visible to the reader only after flush_on. Does not park.
Writes data with write_on and then flushes with flush_on, returning the flush result.
Copies data into the pipe's buffer without flushing it. Does not park, however much has been written. Call flush_on to make the bytes readable and to apply backpressure.
fn duplex(s: io.Stream, options: Options) -> Duplex
Returns a Duplex that reads from and writes to s. Combines from_stream and to_stream on the same stream, so s is closed once the output is completed.
fn from_stream(s: io.Stream, options: Options) -> Reader

Returns a Reader that delivers the bytes read from s. Starts a green thread that reads s into the pipe and flushes after every read. At end of input the pipe's writer completes, and a read error fails the reader's read with that error. The green thread stops once a flush reports that the reader has completed. It never closes s.
fn to_stream(s: io.Stream, options: Options) -> Writer

Returns a Writer whose flushed bytes are written to s. Starts a green thread that writes the flushed bytes to s. It closes s when the writer completes or fails, or when a write to s fails, and then completes the reading end so the writer's flush reports completed.
The owner of a started child process. Dropping a child that has not been waited for kills it with Kill, reaps it and closes its streams. The shared view of the child.
struct ChildHandle { pub pid: i64 pub stdin: io.Stream? pub stdout: io.Stream? pub stderr: io.Stream? ... }

A copyable view of a started child process. The view holds the process id and the parent's ends of the pipes. It does not kill or reap the child when released; wait_on reaps it and Child does both when dropped. The process id of the child. A stream that writes to the child's standard input, or none unless it was Piped. Closing it closes the pipe, which the child sees as end of input. A stream that reads the child's standard output, or none unless it was Piped. Reads return 0 at end of output. A stream that reads the child's standard error, or none unless it was Piped. Reads return 0 at end of output.
struct Command { pub program: str pub args: []str pub env: [str: str]? pub dir: str pub stdin: Stdio pub stdout: Stdio pub stderr: Stdio pub group: bool }

A program to run, with its arguments, environment, working directory and standard stream setup. Made with command and adjusted by setting fields. Starting it with start, start_handle or run does not modify the command. The program to run. A name without / is searched for in PATH as find does. The arguments after the program name. The program name itself is passed as argv[0]. The complete environment of the child, or none to give it the current environment from os.environment. The working directory of the child. An empty string keeps the parent's. How the child's standard input is connected. How the child's standard output is connected. How the child's standard error is connected. Whether the child starts in a new process group. kill then signals the whole group.
How a child process ended. The process ended by itself with this exit status. This signal ended the process.
struct Output { pub status: Exit pub stdout: []u8 pub stderr: []u8 }
The result of run: the exit and everything the child wrote. How the child ended. Everything the child wrote to standard output. Everything the child wrote to standard error.

Where one of a child's standard streams is connected. The child uses the parent's descriptor. The child is connected to a pipe, and the parent's end is available as a stream on the child. The child is connected to /dev/null: reads return end of input and writes are discarded.
fn kill(c: Child, signal: signals.Signal) ! io.Error
Sends signal to the child owned by c. Does the same as kill_on on its handle.
Waits for the child owned by c to end and returns how it ended. Does the same as wait_on on its handle.
Returns the Child that owns the process behind h, which kills and reaps it when dropped.
Sends signal to the child behind c. Does nothing once the child has been waited for. Signals the whole process group for a command started with group. Does not wait for the child to end.

Waits for the child behind c to end without reaping it. Parks the green thread until the process ends. kill_on still signals the child's process group afterwards, and wait_on then reaps the child and returns at once. Returns at once when the child has been waited for. Fails with NotConnected when a concurrent wait_on reaps the child first.

Waits for the child behind c to end, reaps it and returns how it ended. Parks the green thread until the process ends. The result is remembered, so later calls return it at once. Fails with the system error if the child cannot be reaped, and can fail with NotConnected when a concurrent call reaps it first.
fn run(c: Command, input: []u8) -> Output ! io.Error

Runs c to completion with all three standard streams piped, and returns its output. Overrides the stdin, stdout and stderr modes of c. Writes input to the child's standard input in the background and then closes it, collects standard output and standard error completely in memory, and waits for the child to end. Parks the green thread while it waits. A non-zero exit is not an error: it is reported in Output.status. Fails if the child cannot be started or waited for, and with the error of a read of standard output or standard error that fails before the end of the output, in which case the child is killed and reaped. Errors from writing input, such as a child that exits without reading it, are ignored.
Starts the command and returns the Child that owns the process. Fails as start_handle does.

Starts the command and returns a view of the process. Resolves the program with find, creates the requested pipes and forks. Returns after the child has executed the program, parking the green thread while it waits for that. Fails with NotFound if the program is not found, with the system error if a pipe or the fork fails or the child's report cannot be read, and with the error of a failing chdir or execve in the child, such as Denied, NotDir or NotFound, in which case the child has been reaped. The caller must wait for the child with wait_on or hand the view to adopt.
Returns whether e is a normal exit with status 0.
Returns a Command for program with args and the defaults for the other fields. args does not include the program name.

Returns the path of the executable that name refers to, or none. A name containing / is checked as given. Any other name is looked for in each directory of PATH, taken from os.env so os.set_env applies, or /usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin when it is unset; an empty entry stands for the current directory. A match must be executable and not a directory. On Windows a name containing \ or / is checked as given, PATH entries are separated by ;, and a name without an extension also matches with each extension in PATHEXT. Blocks the OS thread while it checks the candidates.
