The error returned when .properties text is malformed. A \u escape on line is malformed, or holds a surrogate that is not part of a valid pair. line counts from 1 and is the line on which the entry starts. message is malformed unicode escape or unpaired surrogate.
struct Properties { pub keys: []str pub values: [str: str] }

The entries of a Java .properties file: a map of keys to values plus the order in which the keys were first set. The keys in the order they were first set. A key appears once. The value of each key in keys.

Formats p as .properties text, one key=value line per entry in keys order, each ending in \n. Backslash, tab, newline, carriage return and form feed are written as \\, \t, \n, \r and \f, and =, :, # and ! are backslash-escaped. Every space in a key and a leading space in a value is written as \ . Control characters and non-ASCII characters are written as \uXXXX, using a surrogate pair above U+FFFF. The output parses back to the same entries.
fn get(p: Properties, key: str) -> str?
Returns the value of key, or none when it is not set.
fn set(mut p: Properties, key: str, value: str)
Sets key to value. A new key is appended to keys; an existing key keeps its position and takes the new value.

Parses .properties text into a Properties. Lines end at 
, 
 or . A line whose first non-blank character is # or ! is a comment, and blank lines are skipped; blank means space, tab or form feed. The key ends at the first unescaped =, : or blank, and a single = or : with surrounding blanks separates it from the value, which runs to the end of the logical line and is not trimmed at the end. A line ending in an odd number of backslashes continues on the next line, whose leading blanks are dropped; a comment marker on a continuation line is part of the value. In keys and values 	, 
,  and   are control characters, \uXXXX is a UTF-16 code unit with a high and low surrogate escape combining into one character, and \ before any other character yields that character. A trailing lone backslash at the end of the input is dropped. A key set twice keeps its first position and last value. Fails with Syntax, which carries the line, for a malformed \u escape.
A cursor over an encoded message that yields its fields in order. Made by decoder or as_message; next advances it.
A growable buffer that fields are appended to in the protobuf wire format. Made by encoder or encoder_with. The buffer grows as needed. encoded returns the bytes written so far.
struct Field { pub number: i64 pub wire: Wire pub value: u64 pub data: []u8 }

One field read from an encoded message by Decoder.next: its number, wire type and raw value. The as_ functions interpret it as a protobuf type, and the unpack_ functions read repeated fields. The field number, from 1 to 536870911. The wire type the field was encoded with. The raw value for Varint, Fixed64 and Fixed32 fields, as unsigned bits with no sign extension, and the payload length in bytes for a Bytes field. The payload of a Bytes field, as a slice of the decoded input; empty for the other wire types.
enum Wire { Varint Fixed64 Bytes Fixed32 }

A protobuf wire type, which says how the value of a field is laid out. Groups (wire types 3 and 4) are not supported. Wire type 0: a base-128 varint of one to ten bytes. Used by int32, int64, uint32, uint64, sint32, sint64, bool and enums. Wire type 1: eight little-endian bytes. Used by fixed64, sfixed64 and double. Wire type 2: a varint length followed by that many bytes. Used by string, bytes, embedded messages and packed repeated fields. Wire type 5: four little-endian bytes. Used by fixed32, sfixed32 and float.
Returns whether the decoder has consumed all of its input.

Reads the next field of the message, or returns none at the end of the input. Fails with Malformed when a field is truncated, the field number is 0 or above 536870911, a length runs past the end of the input or the wire type is 6 or 7, and with Unsupported for the group wire types 3 and 4. When it fails the decoder does not advance. Unknown fields are returned like known ones, so a caller skips one by ignoring it.

Starts an embedded message in field field and returns a mark to pass to end_message. The tag is written now and the message's fields follow, written with the other write_ functions. The length prefix is inserted by end_message, which moves the message's bytes. Messages can nest.
Returns the bytes written so far. The slice views the encoder's own buffer, so a later write or reset can change it. Copy it to keep it past the next write.
Ends the embedded message that begin_message started, which returned mark. It inserts the varint length of everything written since the mark.
Appends v as four little-endian bytes, with no field tag.
Appends v as eight little-endian bytes, with no field tag.
Appends the bytes of data as they are, with no tag or length.
Appends the bytes of s as they are, with no tag or length.
fn put_tag(e: *Encoder, field: i64, w: Wire)
Appends the tag that starts a field, the number field and the wire type w packed as field << 3 | wire, as a varint. field is not validated; a valid field number is 1 to 536870911.
Appends v as a varint of one to ten bytes, seven bits per byte, least significant group first. This writes no field tag.
Discards everything written so the encoder can be used again, keeping its buffer.
Returns the number of bytes written so far.
fn write_bool(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: bool)
Writes field field as a bool varint, 1 for true and 0 for false.
Writes field field as bytes: its tag, the byte length and the bytes of data.
fn write_double(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: f64)
Writes field field as a double, eight little-endian bytes of the IEEE 754 bits.
fn write_fixed32(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: u32)
Writes field field as fixed32, four little-endian bytes.
fn write_fixed64(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: u64)
Writes field field as fixed64, eight little-endian bytes.
fn write_float(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: f32)
Writes field field as a float, four little-endian bytes of the IEEE 754 bits.
fn write_int32(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: i32)
Writes field field as an int32 varint. A negative value is sign-extended to 64 bits and takes ten bytes, as the specification requires. The same call writes an enum value.
fn write_int64(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: i64)
Writes field field as an int64 varint. A negative value takes ten bytes, as the specification requires.
Writes field field as a packed repeated double field: one Bytes field holding eight bytes per value. Writes nothing when values is empty.
Writes field field as a packed repeated fixed32 or sfixed32 field: one Bytes field holding four bytes per value. Writes nothing when values is empty. For sfixed32, convert each value to u32 first.
Writes field field as a packed repeated fixed64 or sfixed64 field: one Bytes field holding eight bytes per value. Writes nothing when values is empty. For sfixed64, convert each value to u64 first.
Writes field field as a packed repeated sint64 or sint32 field, each value ZigZag encoded. Writes nothing when values is empty.

Writes field field as a packed repeated uint64, uint32, bool or enum field: one Bytes field holding the varints back to back. Writes nothing when values is empty, as the specification omits an empty packed field.
fn write_sfixed32(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: i32)
Writes field field as sfixed32, four little-endian bytes of the two's complement.
fn write_sfixed64(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: i64)
Writes field field as sfixed64, eight little-endian bytes of the two's complement.
fn write_sint64(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: i64)
Writes field field as a sint64 varint, ZigZag encoded. Use it for sint32 too.
fn write_string(e: *Encoder, field: i64, s: str)
Writes field field as a string: its tag, the byte length and the bytes of s. s is not checked for UTF-8.
fn write_uint64(e: *Encoder, field: i64, v: u64)
Writes field field as a uint32 or uint64 varint. A uint32 field takes the same encoding, so v must fit that range for such a field.
Returns the value of a bool field: false for 0 and true for any other varint. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Varint.
Returns the payload of a bytes field as a slice of the decoded input. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Bytes.
Returns the value of a double field. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Fixed64.
Returns the value of a fixed32 field; reinterpret it as i32 for sfixed32. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Fixed32.
Returns the value of a fixed64 field; reinterpret it as i64 for sfixed64. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Fixed64.
Returns the value of a float field. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Fixed32.
Returns the value of an int32 field or an enum field, the low 32 bits of the varint. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Varint.
Returns the value of an int64 field, the varint reinterpreted as two's complement. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Varint.
Returns a decoder over the payload of an embedded message field. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Bytes.
Returns the value of a sint32 or sint64 field, undoing the ZigZag encoding. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Varint.
Returns the payload of a string field. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Bytes. The bytes are not checked for UTF-8.
Returns the value of a uint32 or uint64 field. Fails with Malformed unless the field has wire type Varint. A uint32 field is not range checked.

Returns the values of a repeated double field. Accepts a single Fixed64 field, which gives one value, or a packed Bytes field, which gives every eight-byte value in it. Fails with Malformed for another wire type or a packed length that is not a multiple of eight.

Returns the values of a repeated fixed32 or sfixed32 field, as unsigned bits. Accepts a single Fixed32 field, which gives one value, or a packed Bytes field, which gives every four-byte value in it. Fails with Malformed for another wire type or a packed length that is not a multiple of four.

Returns the values of a repeated fixed64 or sfixed64 field, as unsigned bits. Accepts a single Fixed64 field, which gives one value, or a packed Bytes field, which gives every eight-byte value in it. Fails with Malformed for another wire type or a packed length that is not a multiple of eight.

Returns the values of a repeated varint field. Accepts both encodings of a repeated field: a single Varint field gives one value, and a packed Bytes field gives every varint in it. Call it once per occurrence and concatenate the results. Fails with Malformed for another wire type or a truncated varint.
Returns a decoder over data, positioned at the first field. The decoder keeps data; it does not copy it.
Returns an empty encoder with room for 256 bytes.
Returns an empty encoder with room for capacity bytes, and at least 16.
fn read_varint(data: []u8, mut at: i64) -> u64 ! io.Error

Reads the varint that starts at data[at] and advances at past it. Fails with Malformed when the input ends inside the varint or the value does not fit in 64 bits. Varints longer than necessary are accepted, up to ten bytes. When it fails, at may already have advanced.
Returns the signed number whose ZigZag encoding is v.
Returns the number of bytes the varint encoding of v takes, from 1 to 10.
Returns the ZigZag encoding of v, which maps small magnitudes of either sign to small unsigned numbers: 0, -1, 1 and -2 become 0, 1, 2 and 3. This is the encoding of sint32 and sint64.

struct Config { pub tls: tls.Config pub idle_timeout: i64 pub handshake_timeout: i64 pub keep_alive: i64 pub max_data: i64 pub max_stream_data: i64 pub max_streams: i64 pub max_uni_streams: i64 pub retry: bool }

The settings of a QUIC endpoint and of the connections it creates. The TLS configuration. alpn is required. A server also needs certificates and key. The idle timeout in milliseconds, after which a connection that has seen no traffic closes. 0 disables it. How long in milliseconds a handshake may take before the connection is abandoned. A value of 0 or less uses 10000. The milliseconds between PING frames sent while a connection is idle. 0 sends none. The connection-level flow control limit, in bytes, advertised for data the peer may send. The flow control limit, in bytes, advertised for each stream. The number of bidirectional streams the peer may open. The number of unidirectional streams the peer may open. Whether a server validates client addresses with a Retry packet before it starts a connection.
A QUIC connection that its owner uses through handle and that closes when dropped. The copyable view of the connection.

struct ConnectionHandle { pub protocol: str pub remote: net.Addr pub local: net.Addr pub server: bool pub group: i64 pub suite: tls.Suite pub peer_certificates: []x509.Certificate pub close_code: i64 pub close_reason: str pub closed_by_peer: bool pub application_close: bool ... }

A copyable view of an established QUIC connection. Every copy refers to the same connection. The ALPN protocol that was negotiated. The address of the peer. The local address of the socket. Whether this end is the server. The named group code of the key exchange. The negotiated cipher suite. The certificate chain of the peer, leaf first, and empty when the peer sent none. The error code of the CONNECTION_CLOSE that ended the connection, valid once it has closed. The reason phrase of the CONNECTION_CLOSE that ended the connection, valid once it has closed. Whether the peer sent the CONNECTION_CLOSE, valid once the connection has closed. Whether the CONNECTION_CLOSE was of the application kind rather than the transport kind, valid once the connection has closed.
The owner of a listening QUIC endpoint that closes it when dropped. The copyable view of the listener.
struct ListenerHandle { pub addr: net.Addr pub config: Config ... }

A copyable view of a listening QUIC endpoint. Every copy refers to the same endpoint and its closed state. The address the endpoint is bound to, with the actual port when port 0 was requested. The settings the listener was started with, which every accepted connection uses.
struct Stats { pub smoothed_rtt: i64 pub min_rtt: i64 pub congestion_window: i64 pub bytes_in_flight: i64 pub packets_sent: i64 pub packets_received: i64 pub packets_lost: i64 pub key_updates: i64 }

A snapshot of the transport counters of a connection. The smoothed round trip time in nanoseconds. The smallest round trip time observed, in nanoseconds. The congestion window in bytes. The bytes sent that are neither acknowledged nor declared lost. The number of packets sent. The number of packets received and accepted. The number of packets declared lost. The number of times this end has replaced its sending keys, whether it started the key update or followed the peer.

A copyable view of one stream of a QUIC connection. Every copy refers to the same stream. Streams are not closed when dropped: finish ends the sending side and reset and stop abandon the sending and receiving sides. The stream ID, whose two low bits say who opened the stream (0 client, 1 server) and whether it is unidirectional (2).
Accepts the next bidirectional stream the peer opened on the connection c. Does the same as accept_stream_on on its handle.
Accepts the next unidirectional stream the peer opened on the connection c. Does the same as accept_uni_stream_on on its handle.
fn close_connection(c: Connection, code: i64, reason: str)
Closes the connection c with the application error code and reason. Does the same as close_on on its handle.
Stops c from closing the connection when dropped, and returns its view. The caller must close the connection with close_on.
Opens a new bidirectional stream on the connection c. Does the same as open_stream_on on its handle.
Opens a new unidirectional stream on the connection c. Does the same as open_uni_stream_on on its handle.
Returns a snapshot of the transport counters of the connection c. Does the same as stats_on on its handle.
Replaces the packet protection keys of the connection c. Does the same as update_keys_on on its handle.

Accepts the next bidirectional stream the peer opened on the connection behind h. Streams are returned in ID order, including ones the peer opened implicitly by using a higher ID, so a stream can be returned before any of its data has arrived. Parks the green thread until the peer opens one. Fails with the error that ended the connection, including while parked.
Accepts the next unidirectional stream the peer opened on the connection behind h, which this end can only read. Behaves as accept_stream_on does for unidirectional streams.
Returns the Connection that owns the connection behind h, which closes it when dropped.
fn close_on(h: *ConnectionHandle, code: i64, reason: str)

Closes the connection behind h with the application error code and reason. Sends a CONNECTION_CLOSE, records code and reason on the handle and parks the green thread until the frame has been sent. While a stream still holds data the peer has not acknowledged, the close is held back until the streams settle, for at most 5 seconds and never past the idle timeout, so a peer cannot keep the call parked longer. The connection then stays in the closing state for three times the probe timeout, answering datagrams from the peer with the same frame, and stats_on fails with NotConnected from the moment of the call. Before the handshake completes the frame is a transport error with code 0x0c and no reason. A code outside 0 to 2^62 - 1 is clamped into that range and a reason longer than 1024 bytes is truncated. Does nothing when the connection has already ended or is closing.

Opens a new bidirectional stream on the connection behind h. Stream IDs count up in steps of 4 from 0 for a client and from 1 for a server. Parks the green thread while the peer's limit on bidirectional streams is reached, which the peer raises with MAX_STREAMS as it finishes streams, and sends STREAMS_BLOCKED once per limit value. Fails with the error that ended the connection, as stats_on does, including while parked.

Opens a new unidirectional stream on the connection behind h, which this end can only write. Stream IDs count up in steps of 4 from 2 for a client and from 3 for a server. Parks and fails as open_stream_on does, with the limit on unidirectional streams.

Returns a snapshot of the transport counters of the connection behind h. Parks the green thread until the connection answers. Once the connection is closing, draining or ended it fails with the error that explains the end: NotConnected after this end closed it, Aborted after the peer closed it, Malformed after this end closed it for a protocol error, TimedOut after the idle or handshake timeout, Reset after a stateless reset and Unsupported after a Version Negotiation packet.

Starts a key update on the connection behind h (RFC 9001 section 6). Derives the next sending keys, flips the key phase bit of the packets sent from now on, and returns without waiting for the peer; the peer answers by updating its own sending keys, which this end follows when the first packet of the new phase arrives. A connection also updates by itself after 2^23 packets sent with one key. Fails Invalid before the handshake is confirmed and while the first packet sent with the current keys after the previous update is unacknowledged, which includes a second call without traffic in between, and with the error that ended the connection, as stats_on does.
Accepts the next connection on l. Does the same as accept_handle on its handle and wraps the result in a Connection.
Closes the listener l. Does the same as close_listener_on on its handle.

Accepts the next connection on the listener behind h and returns its view. Parks the green thread until a connection arrives. Fails with NotConnected once the listener is closed, including while the call is waiting.

Closes the listener behind h. Closes every connection of the listener with application error code 0 and an empty reason, including the ones that are queued for accept, then closes the socket, which ends the endpoint's reader, and wakes every green thread waiting in accept or accept_handle, which fail with NotConnected. Asks every connection to close before it waits for any, then parks the green thread until each has sent its CONNECTION_CLOSE, so the wait is that of the slowest connection, at most 5 seconds as for close_on, and not the sum. New connections are refused from the first call on, and later calls do nothing.

Ends the sending side of the stream s after the bytes already written. Sends FIN with the last data. Calling it again does nothing. Fails BrokenPipe after reset or STOP_SENDING, Invalid for a stream this end only reads, and with the error that ended the connection.
fn read(s: Stream, buf: []u8) -> i64 ! io.Error

Reads up to buf.len bytes from the stream s into buf and returns the count. Parks the green thread until at least one byte is available. Returns 0 at the end of a finished stream, for an empty buf and for a stream whose state has been released after it was read to the end. Fails Reset when the peer reset the stream, Aborted after this end called stop, Invalid for a stream this end only writes, and with the error that ended the connection, including while parked.

Abandons the sending side of the stream s with the application error code. Sends RESET_STREAM carrying the highest offset sent and drops the unacknowledged bytes. Parked and later writes fail BrokenPipe. A code outside 0 to 2^62 - 1 is clamped into that range. Does nothing on a finished stream, a stream this end only reads or an ended connection.

Abandons the receiving side of the stream s with the application error code. Sends STOP_SENDING, discards the unread bytes and every byte that arrives later, and fails parked and later reads Aborted. The peer's writer sees BrokenPipe once it receives the frame. A code outside 0 to 2^62 - 1 is clamped into that range. Does nothing on a stream that is already finished or reset, a stream this end only writes or an ended connection.
Returns an io.Stream over the stream s. Its read and write call read and write, and its close calls finish and ignores its error.
fn write(s: Stream, data: []u8) -> i64 ! io.Error

Writes data to the stream s and returns data.len. Copies the bytes into the stream's send buffer, which holds at most 1 MiB of bytes the peer has not acknowledged, and parks the green thread while it is full, so a write of any length completes once the peer has acknowledged enough. Returns before the bytes are delivered. Fails BrokenPipe after finish or reset, after the peer sent STOP_SENDING and for a stream whose state has been released, Invalid for a stream this end only reads, and with the error that ended the connection, including while parked.
fn connect(a: net.Addr, config: Config) -> Connection ! io.Error
Opens a QUIC connection to the address a and returns it. Does the same as connect_handle and wraps the result in a Connection.
fn connect_handle(a: net.Addr, config: Config) -> *ConnectionHandle ! io.Error

Opens a QUIC connection to the address a, completes the handshake and returns the view of the connection. Binds a UDP socket of the family of a on a free port that belongs to the connection and is closed when it ends. config.tls.server_name defaults to the text of a.ip when empty. Parks the green thread until the handshake finishes. Fails Invalid when config.tls.alpn is empty and with the error net.bind_udp returns when no socket can be bound. A handshake that fails fails with the error the TLS handshake returned, Refused when the server closed the connection during the handshake and Malformed when this end closed it for a protocol violation, such as invalid transport parameters.
fn dial(host: str, port: i64, config: Config) -> Connection ! io.Error
Opens a QUIC connection to the host host on port and returns it. Does the same as dial_handle and wraps the result in a Connection.
fn dial_handle(host: str, port: i64, config: Config) -> *ConnectionHandle ! io.Error

Resolves host, opens a QUIC connection to its first address on port, completes the handshake and returns the view of the connection. config.tls.server_name defaults to host when empty. Otherwise behaves as connect_handle, and also fails with NotFound when host cannot be resolved.
fn listen(host: str, port: i64, config: Config) -> Listener ! io.Error

Binds a UDP socket to host and port and starts a QUIC server endpoint on it. Port 0 chooses a free port, which handle.addr.port reports. Fails Invalid when config.tls.alpn is empty or config.tls has no certificates or no key, and with the error net.bind_udp returns when the socket cannot be bound. Dropping the listener closes the socket.
struct AckRange { pub smallest: i64 pub largest: i64 }
A contiguous run of acknowledged packet numbers, both ends inclusive. The lowest packet number of the run. The highest packet number of the run.
struct AckResult { pub acked: []Sent pub lost: []Sent pub rtt_updated: bool }

The outcome of processing an ACK frame. The in-flight packets the frame acknowledged for the first time, in packet number order. The packets the frame caused to be declared lost, in packet number order. Whether the frame produced a round-trip time sample.

struct Recovery { pub latest_rtt: i64 pub smoothed_rtt: i64 pub rttvar: i64 pub min_rtt: i64 pub first_rtt_sample: i64 pub max_ack_delay: i64 pub pto_count: i64 pub max_datagram_size: i64 pub congestion_window: i64 pub bytes_in_flight: i64 pub ssthresh: i64 pub recovery_start_time: i64 pub handshake_confirmed: bool pub peer_completed_address_validation: bool pub has_handshake_keys: bool pub amplification_blocked: bool pub limited: bool ... }

The loss detection and congestion control state of one connection path (RFC 9002). The module reads no clock and performs no I/O: every time is a nanosecond reading supplied by the caller, and every timer is a value for the caller to wait for. Fields marked as set by the caller are read at the next event or rearm_timer call. A new value comes from recovery. The most recent round-trip time sample in nanoseconds. The exponentially weighted moving average of the round-trip time in nanoseconds, initially 333 ms. The mean deviation of the round-trip time in nanoseconds, initially half of 333 ms. The lowest round-trip time sample in nanoseconds, ignoring acknowledgment delay, or 0 before the first sample. The time the first round-trip time sample was taken, or -1 before it. The peer's max_ack_delay transport parameter in nanoseconds, set by the caller. It starts at 25 ms. The number of probe timeouts since an acknowledgment reset the backoff. The maximum datagram payload in bytes, set from recovery. It sizes the minimum window and the congestion avoidance step. The number of bytes the sender may have in flight. The sum of the sizes of the in-flight packets that are neither acknowledged nor declared lost. The slow start threshold in bytes, or the largest i64 before the first congestion event. The time the current recovery period started, or -1 when none is active. A packet sent at or before this time does not grow the window when acknowledged. Whether the handshake is confirmed (RFC 9001 section 4.1.2), set by the caller. A confirmed handshake caps acknowledgment delays by max_ack_delay and arms the Application space. Whether the peer has finished validating this endpoint's address, set by the caller to true on a server. A client sets it implicitly when a Handshake packet is acknowledged, and the confirmed handshake implies it. Whether this endpoint holds Handshake keys, set by the caller. It selects the space of a client's anti-deadlock probe. Whether a server may send nothing more until it receives datagrams from the client, set by the caller. A blocked server arms no probe timer. Whether the sender is limited by the application or by flow control instead of the window, set by the caller. Acknowledgments do not grow the window while it is true.
struct Sent { pub number: i64 pub time: i64 pub size: i64 pub ack_eliciting: bool pub in_flight: bool }

A packet the endpoint sent, as reported to on_sent and handed back in AckResult and Timeout. Times are nanoseconds on a monotonic clock chosen by the caller and are never negative. Sizes include the QUIC header and the AEAD tag but not UDP or IP overhead. The packet number, strictly greater than every number already reported in its space. The time the packet was sent. The size of the packet in bytes. Whether the packet holds a frame that obliges the peer to acknowledge it. Whether the packet counts toward bytes in flight: it holds an ack-eliciting or PADDING frame. A packet that is not in flight is not tracked and must not be ack-eliciting.

A packet number space: the Initial, Handshake and Application Data (0-RTT and 1-RTT) packets are numbered, acknowledged and declared lost separately. Packets protected with the Initial keys. Packets protected with the Handshake keys. Packets protected with the 0-RTT or 1-RTT keys.
struct Timeout { pub lost: []Sent pub probe: Space? pub probes: i64 }

The outcome of a loss detection timeout. The packets declared lost by the time threshold, in packet number order. Empty for a probe timeout. The space that needs ack-eliciting probe packets, or none when the timeout declared packets lost or no timer was armed. The number of ack-eliciting datagrams to send as probes: 2 after a probe timeout and 1 for the client's anti-deadlock packet.

Returns whether sending bytes more bytes keeps the bytes in flight within the congestion window. Probe packets sent after a timeout and the packet that follows entering recovery bypass the window; the caller decides when to ask.
Returns three times pto_duration in nanoseconds, the length of the closing and draining periods.

Returns the time at which the caller must call on_timeout, or -1 when no timer is armed. The value is the time threshold loss time of the earliest space when one is waiting. Otherwise it is the probe timeout of the earliest space with an ack-eliciting packet in flight, which backs off by 2 for each pto_count. Initial and Handshake periods omit max_ack_delay, the Application space is never armed before handshake_confirmed, and a server with amplification_blocked has no timer. A client that has not completed address validation arms the timer even with nothing in flight, starting from the time of the last event. The value only changes when an event or rearm_timer recomputes it. A value in the past means the timeout is due.
fn discard_space(r: *Recovery, space: Space, now: i64)

Forgets every packet of space at time now, as when its keys are discarded. The packets leave bytes_in_flight, the space's loss time and last ack-eliciting time are cleared, pto_count returns to 0 and the timer is recomputed. Call it for the Initial space when Handshake packets are first sent or received, and for the Handshake space when the handshake is confirmed.
Returns the highest packet number the peer has acknowledged in space, or -1 when it has acknowledged none.
Returns the time at which an unacknowledged packet in space becomes eligible for time threshold loss, or -1 when none is waiting.
fn on_ack(r: *Recovery, space: Space, ranges: []AckRange, ack_delay_ns: i64, now: i64) -> AckResult ! io.Error

Processes an ACK frame received in space at time now and returns what it newly acknowledged and caused to be lost. ranges are the acknowledged packet numbers in the descending order of the frame, and ack_delay_ns is the decoded acknowledgment delay in nanoseconds. Fails Malformed without changing any state when ranges is empty, when a range is reversed or negative, when ranges overlap or are not in descending order, when the frame acknowledges a number never sent, or when a range covers a number marked by skip. The caller answers with a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION connection error. Only the first 256 ranges are processed. Each range is located by binary search over the tracked packets, so the work is bounded by the number of ranges and the packets they newly acknowledge, never by the size of a range or by how many packets are outstanding. A number that was sent without being in flight, was acknowledged before or was declared lost is accepted and ignored. The largest acknowledged number counts as a round-trip time sample when the frame newly acknowledges that packet, which must have been in flight, and at least one newly acknowledged packet is ack-eliciting. The sample is never negative and is capped at 2^40 ns. min_rtt takes the raw sample. The acknowledgment delay is ignored in the Initial space, capped by max_ack_delay once handshake_confirmed is set, never exceeds the sample and is not subtracted when that would put the sample below min_rtt. It then declares lost the earlier packets that are three or more packet numbers or more than 9/8 of the round-trip time older than the largest acknowledged, applies the NewReno window rules to the losses and acknowledgments, and resets pto_count unless this is a client that has not completed address validation. An acknowledgment in the Handshake space sets peer_completed_address_validation. A frame that acknowledges no new packet and does not raise the largest acknowledged number changes nothing; one that raises it still runs loss detection, so an acknowledgment of a packet that was not in flight can declare earlier packets lost. Persistent congestion is established when two ack-eliciting packets sent after the first round-trip time sample are declared lost together, no packet sent between them was acknowledged, and the span exceeds three probe timeout periods including max_ack_delay. It sets the window to the minimum, ends the recovery period and makes the next sample the new min_rtt.
fn on_sent(r: *Recovery, space: Space, p: Sent)

Records that the packet p was sent in space. A packet that is not in flight only raises the highest number sent, so an acknowledgment of it is accepted but reports nothing. An in-flight packet is tracked until it is acknowledged or declared lost, adds its size to bytes_in_flight, and, when ack-eliciting, becomes the last ack-eliciting packet of its space. The timer is recomputed at p.time. Numbers in one space must strictly increase and times must not decrease.

Handles the expiry of the loss detection timer at time now and returns what the caller must do. Call it when now reaches deadline. When a space has a time threshold loss time, the packets that are now overdue are declared lost and returned in lost, the window rules apply, and no probe is requested. Otherwise it is a probe timeout: pto_count increases, which doubles the next period, and probe names the space whose ack-eliciting data the caller sends again, in probes datagrams. A probe timeout does not declare packets lost. When nothing is in flight at a client that has not completed address validation, probe is the Handshake space if has_handshake_keys is set and the Initial space otherwise, with one probe; the caller sends an ack-eliciting Handshake packet, or an Initial packet padded to 1200 bytes. Probe packets bypass can_send and are reported through on_sent. Returns a Timeout with no loss and no probe when no timer is armed.

Returns the probe timeout period in nanoseconds without backoff: the smoothed round-trip time, four times its variation (at least 1 ms) and max_ack_delay. A connection that sends CONNECTION_CLOSE waits three times this period in the closing and draining states, which is closing_duration.

Recomputes the loss detection timer at time now. Call it after changing handshake_confirmed, peer_completed_address_validation, has_handshake_keys or amplification_blocked, and when a server receives a datagram while amplification_blocked was set. Then compare deadline with now: a timer already in the past is due, so the caller runs on_timeout.
fn skip(r: *Recovery, space: Space, number: i64)

Marks number as a packet number the sender deliberately leaves unused in space, the defence against optimistic acknowledgments (RFC 9000 section 21.4). Call it for numbers above every number already sent, then continue numbering above it. on_ack fails Malformed for a frame that covers a skipped number. The most recent 32 skipped numbers per space are remembered. Packet threshold loss assumes consecutive numbers, so a skipped number makes a loss one packet later than otherwise. A number at or below the highest number sent is ignored.
Returns the number of in-flight packets in space that are neither acknowledged nor declared lost.

Returns the state of a new path whose datagrams carry at most max_datagram_size bytes of payload, which is at least 1200 for QUIC. The round-trip time starts at 333 ms, the window at min(10 * size, max(14720, 2 * size)) bytes in slow start, and the minimum window at 2 * size. The packet threshold is 3, the time threshold 9/8 of the round-trip time, the timer granularity 1 ms, the loss reduction factor 1/2 and the persistent congestion threshold 3. A client starts without a validated address, so peer_completed_address_validation is false; a server sets it.
struct AckFrame { pub largest: i64 pub delay: i64 pub ranges: []AckRange pub ecn: bool pub ect0: i64 pub ect1: i64 pub ce: i64 }

The contents of an ACK frame (RFC 9000 section 19.3). The largest packet number acknowledged. The acknowledgment delay as encoded, in units of 2^ack_delay_exponent microseconds. The acknowledged ranges from the highest to the lowest. The first range ends at largest, and each later range lies below the previous one with at least one unacknowledged packet between them. Whether the frame carries ECN counts. The count of packets received with the ECT(0) codepoint, when ecn is set. The count of packets received with the ECT(1) codepoint, when ecn is set. The count of packets received with the ECN-CE codepoint, when ecn is set.
struct AckRange { pub smallest: i64 pub largest: i64 }
A range of consecutive packet numbers an ACK frame acknowledges. The lowest packet number in the range. The highest packet number in the range.
struct CloseFrame { pub application: bool pub code: i64 pub frame_type: i64 pub reason: str }

The contents of a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame (RFC 9000 section 19.19). Whether the frame closes with an application error code, which has frame type 0x1d and no frame_type, instead of a transport error code. The error code. The type of the frame that caused a transport error, and 0 for an application error. The human-readable reason, which can be empty.
A read position over a byte slice, made by cursor. Every read advances the position and fails with io.Error.Malformed when fewer bytes remain than the read needs.

enum Frame { Padding(i64) Ping Ack(AckFrame) ResetStream(i64, i64, i64) StopSending(i64, i64) Crypto(i64, []u8) NewToken([]u8) Stream(StreamFrame) MaxData(i64) MaxStreamData(i64, i64) MaxStreams(bool, i64) DataBlocked(i64) StreamDataBlocked(i64, i64) StreamsBlocked(bool, i64) NewConnectionId(i64, i64, []u8, []u8) RetireConnectionId(i64) PathChallenge([]u8) PathResponse([]u8) ConnectionClose(CloseFrame) HandshakeDone }

A QUIC frame (RFC 9000 section 19). A run of PADDING frames, each one byte. The parser collapses consecutive ones into a single value. A PING frame. An ACK frame. A RESET_STREAM frame that abruptly ends a stream's sending side. A STOP_SENDING frame that asks the peer to stop sending on a stream. A CRYPTO frame carrying handshake data at offset. A NEW_TOKEN frame carrying an address validation token for later connections. A STREAM frame. A MAX_DATA frame raising the connection-wide data limit. A MAX_STREAM_DATA frame raising the data limit of one stream. A MAX_STREAMS frame raising the limit on bidirectional streams when bidi is true and on unidirectional streams otherwise. A DATA_BLOCKED frame reporting that the connection-wide limit blocks sending. A STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame reporting that the limit of one stream blocks sending. A STREAMS_BLOCKED frame reporting that the stream limit blocks opening bidirectional streams when bidi is true and unidirectional streams otherwise. A NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame. id is 1 to 20 bytes and reset_token is 16 bytes. A RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame naming a connection ID by sequence number. A PATH_CHALLENGE frame carrying 8 bytes. A PATH_RESPONSE frame echoing 8 bytes. A CONNECTION_CLOSE frame. A HANDSHAKE_DONE frame.
struct Header { pub kind: PacketKind pub version: i64 pub dcid: []u8 pub scid: []u8 pub token: []u8 pub pn_offset: i64 pub size: i64 pub versions: []i64 pub tag: []u8 }

The fields of a packet header that are readable while header protection is still applied. The kind of packet. The version of a long header packet, and 0 for a short header packet. The destination connection ID. A short header packet has the length given to parse_header. The source connection ID of a long header packet, and empty for a short header packet. The token of an Initial packet, or the retry token of a Retry packet, and empty for other packets. The offset of the packet number field from the start of the packet, as used by open. It is 0 for packets without a packet number: Retry, Version Negotiation and unknown versions. The length in bytes of the packet within the datagram, so that coalesced packets can be split. A packet that has no length field extends to the end of the datagram. The versions a Version Negotiation packet lists, and empty for other packets. The 16-byte Retry Integrity Tag of a Retry packet, and empty for other packets.
struct Keys { pub aead: aead.Aead pub key: []u8 pub iv: []u8 pub hp: []u8 pub secret: []u8 pub suite: tls.Suite ... }

The packet protection keys of one direction at one encryption level (RFC 9001 section 5). Made by keys, next_keys or initial_keys. The AEAD that protects packet payloads, keyed with the quic key value. The AEAD key, derived with the label quic key. The 12-byte IV that a packet number is XORed into to form the nonce. The header protection key. The traffic secret the keys derive from. The cipher suite the keys belong to.
struct Opened { pub number: i64 pub payload: []u8 pub key_phase: bool pub first_byte: i64 pub reserved_bits_set: bool }

The result of removing protection from a packet. The full packet number, decoded against the largest number received so far. The decrypted payload, which parse_frames reads. The key phase bit of a short header packet, and false for a long header packet. The first byte of the header with header protection removed. Whether any reserved bit of the unprotected first byte is set. A connection treats it as a PROTOCOL_VIOLATION after the packet decrypted.
enum PacketKind { Initial ZeroRtt Handshake Retry VersionNegotiation Short Unknown }

The kind of a QUIC packet, from its header. A long header packet of type Initial. A long header packet of type 0-RTT. A long header packet of type Handshake. A Retry packet. A Version Negotiation packet, which has version 0. A short header packet, which carries 1-RTT data. A long header packet of a version other than 1 whose type bits have no known meaning.

struct Parameters { pub original_destination_connection_id: []u8? pub max_idle_timeout: i64 pub stateless_reset_token: []u8? pub max_udp_payload_size: i64 pub initial_max_data: i64 pub initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local: i64 pub initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote: i64 pub initial_max_stream_data_uni: i64 pub initial_max_streams_bidi: i64 pub initial_max_streams_uni: i64 pub ack_delay_exponent: i64 pub max_ack_delay: i64 pub disable_active_migration: bool pub preferred_address: []u8? pub active_connection_id_limit: i64 pub initial_source_connection_id: []u8? pub retry_source_connection_id: []u8? }

The transport parameters of an endpoint (RFC 9000 section 18.2), with the protocol defaults for parameters that are not sent. The destination connection ID of the first Initial packet the client sent. Only a server sends it. The idle timeout in milliseconds, where 0 means no timeout. The default is 0. The 16-byte stateless reset token for the connection ID the server chose in the handshake. Only a server sends it. The largest UDP payload the endpoint accepts, at least 1200. The default is 65527. The connection-wide limit on data the peer may send. The default is 0. The initial data limit of a bidirectional stream the sender of the parameters opened. The default is 0. The initial data limit of a bidirectional stream the receiver of the parameters opened. The default is 0. The initial data limit of a unidirectional stream. The default is 0. The initial limit on bidirectional streams the peer may open, at most 2^60. The default is 0. The initial limit on unidirectional streams the peer may open, at most 2^60. The default is 0. The exponent of the ACK delay unit, which is 2^exponent microseconds, at most 20. The default is 3. The longest delay in milliseconds before the endpoint acknowledges a packet, below 2^14. The default is 25. Whether the endpoint does not support connection migration. The default is false. The raw value of the preferred address parameter, which only a server sends: an IPv4 address and port, an IPv6 address and port, a connection ID and a stateless reset token. The most connection IDs the endpoint can store, at least 2. The default is 2. The source connection ID the endpoint put in its first Initial packet. The source connection ID of the Retry packet the server sent. Only a server that sent a Retry sends it.
struct StreamFrame { pub id: i64 pub offset: i64 pub data: []u8 pub fin: bool }

The contents of a STREAM frame (RFC 9000 section 19.8). The stream ID. The offset of data within the stream. The stream data. Whether the frame ends the stream, so offset + data.len is the final size.
fn ack_delay_ns(ack: AckFrame, exponent: i64) -> i64

Returns the acknowledgment delay of ack in nanoseconds, given the peer's ack_delay_exponent. The delay is ack.delay * 2^exponent microseconds. The result saturates at the largest i64 instead of overflowing, so a hostile delay such as 2^62 - 1 is safe to use. An exponent outside 0 to 20 is clamped into that range, and a negative delay gives 0.
Reads one byte and returns it as a value from 0 to 255. Fails with Malformed at the end of the data.
Returns the number of bytes not yet read.
Returns the offset of the next byte to read.
Reads every remaining byte and returns them as a slice that shares the cursor's data.
Reads the next n bytes and returns them as a slice that shares the cursor's data. Fails with Malformed when n is negative or more than left(c).
Reads a big-endian 16-bit unsigned integer. Fails with Malformed when fewer than 2 bytes remain.
Reads a big-endian 32-bit unsigned integer. Fails with Malformed when fewer than 4 bytes remain.

Reads a variable-length integer (RFC 9000 section 16) and returns its value, from 0 to 2^62 - 1. Fails with Malformed when the data ends inside the integer. Encodings longer than necessary are accepted.
Returns whether f makes the peer send an acknowledgment: every frame except Ack, Padding and ConnectionClose.
Returns the number of bytes put_frame writes for f. A packet writer uses it to fit frames into the space left in a packet.
Derives the keys of the next key phase from k (RFC 9001 section 6). The secret is advanced with the label quic ku, which gives a new key and IV. The header protection key is kept.
fn open(k: Keys, packet: []u8, h: Header, largest: i64) -> Opened ! io.Error

Removes header protection and decrypts the packet packet, which is exactly h.size bytes of the datagram. h comes from parse_header. The packet number is decoded against largest, the largest packet number received in that space, or -1 when none has arrived. The input is not modified, so a packet that fails can be opened again with other keys. Fails with Malformed when the packet is not h.size bytes or is too short to sample, Invalid when authentication fails, the packet number decodes above 2^62-1 or h is a kind without a packet number. The reserved bits and key phase of the first byte are reported in the result.
fn peek_key_phase(k: Keys, packet: []u8, h: Header) -> bool ! io.Error

Returns the key phase bit of the short header packet packet, found by removing header protection. Header protection keys do not change with the key phase, so a receiver reads the bit with the current keys to learn whether the packet needs the next keys. Returns false for a long header packet. Fails with Malformed when the packet is too short to sample and Invalid for a kind without a packet number.
fn seal(k: Keys, header: []u8, pn: i64, payload: []u8) -> []u8

Returns the protected packet for payload. header is the unprotected header up to and including the packet number field, which the caller has written with the chosen length; for a long header the Length field covers the packet number, the payload and the 16-byte tag. pn is the full packet number, which forms the nonce. The header is the associated data. Header protection is applied over the packet number and the low bits of the first byte, sampling the ciphertext from 4 bytes past the start of the packet number field. The payload must be at least 4 - packet number length bytes so the sample exists; a shorter one panics, and a sender pads it with PADDING frames.

Returns the extension body for p, the value of TLS extension quic_transport_parameters (RFC 9000 section 18). Parameters equal to their default are omitted, and so are connection IDs and tokens that are none. Parameters appear in order of their identifiers. Panics when an integer is negative or above 2^62 - 1.
fn stream_frame_size(s: StreamFrame, last: bool) -> i64
Returns the number of bytes put_stream_frame writes for s. The offset is written only when it is not 0, and the length only when last is false.
The transport error code AEAD_LIMIT_REACHED, 0x0f, for a packet protection key that reached its usage limit.
The transport error code APPLICATION_ERROR, 0x0c, for an error the application caused.
The transport error code CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR, 0x09, for more connection IDs than the limit allows.
The transport error code CONNECTION_REFUSED, 0x02, which a server uses to refuse a connection.
The transport error code CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED, 0x0d, for more buffered handshake data than the endpoint keeps.
The transport error code FINAL_SIZE_ERROR, 0x06, for data that contradicts a stream's final size.
The transport error code FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR, 0x03, for data beyond a flow control limit.
The transport error code FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR, 0x07, for a malformed frame.
The transport error code INVALID_TOKEN, 0x0b, for a token a server rejects.
The transport error code KEY_UPDATE_ERROR, 0x0e, for a key update that violates the rules of RFC 9001 section 6.
The largest value a variable-length integer holds, 2^62 - 1.
The transport error code NO_ERROR, 0x00, which closes a connection without an error.
The transport error code NO_VIABLE_PATH, 0x10, for a path that cannot carry packets of the minimum size.
The transport error code PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, 0x0a, for a violation no other code describes.
The transport error code STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR, 0x04, for a stream ID beyond the limit.
The transport error code STREAM_STATE_ERROR, 0x05, for a frame a stream's state does not allow.
The transport error code TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR, 0x08, for invalid transport parameters.
The transport error code CRYPTO_ERROR for the TLS alert alert, which is 0x100 + alert.
Returns a cursor at the start of data.
fn decode_packet_number(largest: i64, truncated: i64, pn_bits: i64) -> i64

Returns the full packet number a truncated one stands for (RFC 9000 appendix A.3). largest is the largest packet number received so far in the packet number space, or -1 when none has arrived. truncated is the value of the packet number field and pn_bits its width: 8, 16, 24 or 32.

Parses the body of a quic_transport_parameters extension. Parameters with unknown identifiers, including the reserved 31 * N + 27 ones, are ignored. Fails with Malformed for a truncated parameter, a duplicate identifier, an integer whose length does not match its encoding, max_udp_payload_size below 1200, ack_delay_exponent above 20, max_ack_delay of 2^14 or more, active_connection_id_limit below 2, either initial_max_streams above 2^60, a stateless_reset_token that is not 16 bytes, a connection ID above 20 bytes, a disable_active_migration with a value or a preferred_address that is not laid out as RFC 9000 section 18.2 gives. A connection maps Malformed to TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR. Byte slices in the result share raw.
fn encode_packet_number(full: i64, largest_acked: i64) -> i64

Returns the number of bytes of a packet number field for full, given the largest packet number the peer has acknowledged. Implements RFC 9000 appendix A.2 and returns 1 to 4. largest_acked is -1 when nothing has been acknowledged. The length covers twice the number of packets in flight, so the receiver can decode the number unambiguously.

Returns the keys that protect Initial packets sent by the server when server is true and by the client otherwise (RFC 9001 section 5.2). dcid is the destination connection ID of the first Initial packet the client sent. The keys use the version 1 salt and AES-128-GCM.
fn keys(suite: tls.Suite, secret: []u8) -> Keys ! io.Error

Derives the packet protection keys of suite from the traffic secret secret (RFC 9001 section 5.1). The key, IV and header protection key come from HKDF-Expand-Label with the labels quic key, quic iv and quic hp. Fails with Invalid when secret has the wrong length for the suite's hash.

Parses the frames of a decrypted packet payload. Consecutive PADDING bytes become one Padding. Fails with Malformed for an empty payload, a truncated frame, an unknown frame type, a frame type encoded in more bytes than necessary, a STREAM or CRYPTO frame whose offset plus length exceeds 2^62 - 1, a MAX_STREAMS or STREAMS_BLOCKED limit above 2^60, a NEW_TOKEN with an empty token, a NEW_CONNECTION_ID whose ID is not 1 to 20 bytes or whose retire_prior_to exceeds sequence, and ACK ranges that reach below packet number 0. A connection maps Malformed to FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR. Byte slices in the frames share payload.
fn parse_header(datagram: []u8, at: i64, short_dcid_len: i64) -> Header ! io.Error

Parses the packet header that starts at offset at of datagram, with header protection still applied. short_dcid_len is the length of the connection IDs this endpoint issues, which a short header does not carry. The connection IDs and token are copies. For version 1, long header connection IDs above 20 bytes, a clear fixed bit, a length field running past the datagram and a Retry packet shorter than its tag are Malformed, as is a Version Negotiation packet whose version list is empty or not a multiple of 4 bytes. Version Negotiation packets and long header packets of other versions are parsed by their invariant fields only: the kind is VersionNegotiation or Unknown and the packet extends to the end of the datagram.

Appends the frame f. A STREAM frame is written with an explicit length, so other frames can follow it; use put_stream_frame to omit the length of the last one. Padding appends count zero bytes. An Ack with no ranges acknowledges only largest. The id and reset_token of NewConnectionId and the data of PathChallenge and PathResponse are written as given and must have the lengths their variants document. Panics when an integer is negative or above 2^62 - 1.
fn put_packet_number(mut out: []u8, pn: i64, length: i64)
Appends the low length bytes of the packet number pn, for a length from 1 to 4.
fn put_stream_frame(mut out: []u8, s: StreamFrame, last: bool)

Appends the STREAM frame s. The offset is written only when it is not 0. When last is false the frame carries an explicit length; when last is true the length is omitted and the frame must be the final one of the packet, since its data runs to the end of the payload.
Appends v as a variable-length integer in its shortest form. Panics when v is negative or above max_varint.
fn put_varint_sized(mut out: []u8, v: i64, size: i64)

Appends v as a variable-length integer of exactly size bytes, which is 1, 2, 4 or 8. A packet writer uses it to reserve a Length field of known size before the payload length is known. Panics when v does not fit in size bytes or size is not one of the four lengths.
fn retry_packet(version: i64, dcid: []u8, scid: []u8, original_dcid: []u8, token: []u8) -> []u8

Returns a Retry packet (RFC 9000 section 17.2.5) that carries token, with its integrity tag. dcid is the source connection ID of the Initial packet being answered and scid is the connection ID the client must use from now on. original_dcid is the destination connection ID of that Initial packet; it is covered by the tag and not sent. The first byte is 0xff.

Returns the 16-byte Retry Integrity Tag of a Retry packet (RFC 9001 section 5.8). original_dcid is the destination connection ID of the Initial packet the Retry answers and retry_without_tag is the Retry packet up to but not including the tag.

Returns whether the last 16 bytes of the Retry packet packet are the integrity tag for original_dcid. original_dcid is the destination connection ID of the first Initial packet this endpoint sent. A packet shorter than 16 bytes is not valid.
Returns the number of bytes put_varint writes for v: 1, 2, 4 or 8. v must be from 0 to max_varint; a larger or negative value gives 8.

Returns a Version Negotiation packet (RFC 9000 section 17.2.1) listing versions. dcid is the source connection ID of the packet being answered and scid its destination connection ID. The first byte has the long header bit set and its other seven bits random.
The error type of the rand constructors. The seed is not the length the generator requires.

A pseudo-random number generator. Made by rng and seeded (xoshiro256**), pcg32 and pcg64 (PCG), or chacha and chacha_rng (ChaCha20). Every function that draws numbers takes it as mut, so the state advances in place. A copy of an Rng continues the same sequence independently of the original. Only the ChaCha generators are suitable for secrets; the others are statistical generators whose output can be predicted from a few values.
fn below(mut r: Rng, n: i64) -> i64
Returns a uniformly distributed integer in 0..n, that is 0 up to and including n - 1. Panics when n is not positive.
fn beta(mut r: Rng, a: f64, b: f64) -> f64
Returns a beta distributed f64 in [0, 1] with shape parameters a and b. Computed as x / (x + y) for two gamma draws. Panics when a or b is not positive.
fn between(mut r: Rng, lo: i64, hi: i64) -> i64
Returns a uniformly distributed integer from lo to hi, both inclusive. Panics when hi is less than lo.
fn binomial(mut r: Rng, n: i64, p: f64) -> i64

Returns the number of successes in n independent trials that each succeed with probability p. The result is in 0..=n. Uses sequential inversion when n times the smaller of p and 1 - p is below 10.0, and the BTRS transformed rejection method (Hormann) otherwise. Panics when n is negative or p is outside [0, 1].
fn chance(mut r: Rng, p: f64) -> bool
Returns true with probability p. A p of 0.0 or less is never true and a p of 1.0 or more is always true.
fn exponential(mut r: Rng, rate: f64) -> f64
Returns an exponentially distributed f64 with the given rate, so the mean is 1 / rate. Uses inversion. Panics when rate is not positive.
Returns a uniformly distributed f64 in [0, 1). The value has 53 bits of precision: it is next shifted right by 11 and divided by 2^53.
fn gamma(mut r: Rng, shape: f64, scale: f64) -> f64

Returns a gamma distributed f64 with the given shape and scale. Uses the Marsaglia and Tsang method; a shape below 1.0 is boosted by one and corrected with a power of a uniform draw. The mean is shape * scale. Panics when shape or scale is not positive.
fn geometric(mut r: Rng, p: f64) -> i64

Returns the number of trials up to and including the first success when each trial succeeds with probability p. The result is at least 1, and is always 1 when p is 1.0. Panics when p is not in (0, 1].
Returns the next 64 random bits from r. All other draws are derived from this function, except that a pcg32 generator builds each value from two 32-bit outputs.
Returns the next 32 random bits from r. A pcg32 generator returns one native output; the other generators return the high 32 bits of next.
fn normal(mut r: Rng, mean: f64, sd: f64) -> f64

Returns a normally distributed f64 with the given mean and standard deviation sd. Uses the Marsaglia polar method, which produces values in pairs; the second value is kept in the generator for the next call.
fn permutation(mut r: Rng, n: i64) -> []i64
Returns the integers 0 up to n - 1 in a random order. Every permutation is equally likely. Returns an empty slice for n of 0. Panics when n is negative.
fn pick[T](mut r: Rng, xs: []T) -> T?
Returns a uniformly chosen element of xs, or none when xs is empty. The slice is not modified.
fn pick_cumulative(mut r: Rng, cumulative_weights: []f64) -> i64?

Returns the index drawn with probability proportional to its weight, given the running sums from cumulative, or none when the slice is empty or its total is not positive. Finds the index by binary search, so each draw takes O(log n) time. An index whose weight is 0 is never returned.
fn poisson(mut r: Rng, lambda: f64) -> i64

Returns a Poisson distributed count with mean lambda. Returns 0 for a lambda of 0.0. Uses Knuth's multiplication method below 10.0 and the PTRS transformed rejection method (Hormann) from there. Panics when lambda is negative.
fn sample(mut r: Rng, n: i64, k: i64) -> []i64
Returns k distinct integers from 0..n in a random order. Uses Floyd's algorithm, so it does not allocate an n-sized slice. Panics unless 0 <= k <= n.
fn shuffle[T](mut r: Rng, mut xs: []T)
Shuffles xs in place with the Fisher-Yates algorithm, so that every permutation is equally likely. An empty or one-element slice is left unchanged.
fn weighted_pick(mut r: Rng, weights: []f64) -> i64?

Returns an index drawn with probability proportional to its entry in weights, or none when weights is empty or sums to zero or less. Builds the running sums on every call; use cumulative and pick_cumulative for repeated draws.
fn zipf(mut r: Rng, n: i64, s: f64) -> i64

Returns a Zipf distributed rank in 1..=n where rank k has probability proportional to k raised to the power -s. Uses rejection-inversion sampling (Hormann and Derflinger), so it takes constant time for any n. Returns 1 when n is 1. Panics when n is less than 1 or s is not positive.

Returns a ChaCha20 generator (RFC 8439 block function, 20 rounds) keyed by the 32-byte seed. The output is the keystream of the key with an all-zero nonce and a 64-bit block counter starting at 0, consumed as little-endian 64-bit words. Fails with BadSeed when seed is not exactly 32 bytes. The same seed always produces the same sequence.
Returns a ChaCha20 generator keyed with 32 bytes from crypto.random. The sequence differs on every call. This is the generator to use when the output must be unpredictable.

Returns the running sums of weights. The result has the same length as weights. Pass it to pick_cumulative to draw many times from the same weights without recomputing it. An empty input gives an empty result.
fn pcg32(seed: u64, stream: u64) -> Rng

Returns a PCG-XSH-RR 32-bit generator with a 64-bit state, started from seed on the sequence selected by stream. Generators with different stream values produce independent sequences from the same seed. next32 returns one native 32-bit output and next joins two of them.
fn pcg64(seed: u64, stream: u64) -> Rng

Returns a PCG-XSL-RR 128-bit generator (pcg64) with a 128-bit state, started from seed on the sequence selected by stream. Generators with different stream values produce independent sequences from the same seed. The seed is added to the low 64 bits of the 128-bit state and the stream selects the odd 128-bit increment stream << 1 | 1. next returns one native 64-bit output.

Returns a xoshiro256** generator seeded with 32 bytes from crypto.random. The sequence differs on every call. The generator itself is not cryptographically secure; use chacha_rng for that. When the entropy is an all-zero state, which xoshiro cannot leave, the state comes from seeded instead.
Returns a xoshiro256** generator whose 256-bit state is expanded from seed with SplitMix64. The same seed always produces the same sequence, on every platform. Every u64 is a valid seed, including 0.

A token bucket that refills continuously and holds at most burst tokens. Accounting is in exact nanosecond units, so fractional tokens accrue without drift. A new bucket starts full. A Bucket is a handle: copies share one state, and every operation is safe to call from several green threads.

The error returned by the waiting operations of Bucket and Keyed, and by admit_wait on a Window. The cancel token was cancelled before or while waiting. The request asks for more tokens than the bucket's burst, so it can never be satisfied.

A set of per-key Buckets that share one rate and burst, bounded in size. At most capacity keys are tracked. Looking up a new key at capacity evicts the least recently used one, and keys idle for the idle duration are dropped on the next lookup or sweep. An evicted key starts again with a full bucket. A Keyed is a handle: copies share one state, and every operation is safe to call from several green threads.

A sliding-window limiter that admits at most limit events in any interval of per. It records the time of each admitted event and forgets one once per has passed, so unlike Bucket it allows no bursts across window edges. A Window is a handle: copies share one state, and every operation is safe to call from several green threads.
Takes one token if available and returns true, or returns false without blocking.
fn allow_n(b: Bucket, n: i64) -> bool

Takes n tokens if they are available now and returns true, or takes nothing and returns false. Never blocks. Returns false when n is negative or larger than the burst, or when fewer than n tokens have accrued. n of 0 returns true unless the bucket is in debt from reserve.
Returns the number of whole tokens available now. Returns 0 while the bucket is in debt.
Returns the bucket's capacity in tokens.
fn delay(b: Bucket, n: i64) -> duration.Duration?
Returns how long until n tokens are available, without taking any. Returns a zero duration when they are available now and none when n is negative or larger than the burst.
Gives back n tokens, for a reservation that went unused. The count is capped at the burst and the balance at a full bucket. A count of zero or less does nothing.
fn reserve(b: Bucket, n: i64) -> duration.Duration?

Takes n tokens unconditionally and returns how long the caller must wait before using them. The returned delay is zero when the tokens were available. Otherwise the bucket goes into debt and later requests queue behind this one. Returns none and takes nothing when n is negative or larger than the burst, or when the debt would grow beyond the bucket's internal limit. Never blocks; pass an unwanted reservation back with refund.

Changes the bucket's capacity to burst tokens. A balance above the new capacity is cut down to it; a larger capacity does not add tokens. Panics if burst is not positive or if burst times the refill interval overflows the bucket's internal limit.
Changes the refill rate to rate_per_second tokens each second. Panics under the same conditions as set_rate_per.
fn set_rate_per(b: Bucket, tokens: i64, per: duration.Duration)

Changes the refill rate to tokens tokens every per. Tokens already accrued are kept, valued in whole tokens when the interval changes. Panics if tokens or per is not positive or if the burst times per overflows the bucket's internal limit.
Reserves one token and waits until it is available. Fails with Cancelled if t is cancelled before or during the wait.
fn wait_n(b: Bucket, n: i64, t: *cancel.Token) ! Error

Reserves n tokens and waits until they are available. Blocks the calling green thread for the reserved delay. Fails with Cancelled if t is already cancelled or is cancelled during the wait, in which case the reservation is refunded. Fails with TooLarge if n is negative, exceeds the burst or the debt limit.
fn allow_key[K: Hash](k: Keyed[K], key: K) -> bool
Takes one token from the bucket for key if available and returns true, or returns false without blocking.
fn allow_key_n[K: Hash](k: Keyed[K], key: K, n: i64) -> bool
Takes n tokens from the bucket for key if available and returns true, or returns false without blocking. See allow_n for the edge cases.
fn bucket_for[K: Hash](k: Keyed[K], key: K) -> Bucket

Returns the bucket for key, creating it full if the key is not tracked. Marks the key as most recently used and evicts idle keys, and the least recently used key if a new key would exceed the capacity. The returned bucket stays usable after eviction but is no longer tracked.
fn forget_key[K: Hash](k: Keyed[K], key: K)
Stops tracking key, so its next use starts with a full bucket. Does nothing if the key is not tracked.
fn reserve_key[K: Hash](k: Keyed[K], key: K, n: i64) -> duration.Duration?
Reserves n tokens from the bucket for key and returns the delay before they may be used. Returns none under the conditions listed on reserve.

Evicts every key that has been idle for the idle duration. Eviction otherwise happens only on lookup, so call this to release memory while the limiter is unused. Does nothing when idle eviction is disabled.
Returns the number of keys currently tracked, including idle keys not yet evicted.
fn wait_key[K: Hash](k: Keyed[K], key: K, t: *cancel.Token) ! Error
Reserves one token from the bucket for key and waits until it is available. Blocks the calling green thread. Fails with Cancelled if t is cancelled before or during the wait.
Records an event and returns true if fewer than limit events fall in the last per, or returns false without recording it. Never blocks.
Waits until an event is admitted and records it. Blocks the calling green thread, pausing for retry_in between attempts. Fails with Cancelled if t is cancelled before an attempt or during a pause.
Returns the number of admitted events still inside the window.
Returns how long until admit would succeed. Returns a zero duration when the window has room now.
fn bucket(rate_per_second: i64, burst: i64, c: clock.Clock) -> Bucket
Returns a bucket that refills rate_per_second tokens each second and holds at most burst, reading time from c. The bucket starts full. Panics under the same conditions as bucket_per.
fn bucket_per(tokens: i64, per: duration.Duration, burst: i64, c: clock.Clock) -> Bucket

Returns a bucket that refills tokens tokens every per and holds at most burst, reading time from c. The bucket starts full. Panics if tokens, per (in nanoseconds) or burst is not positive, or if burst times per overflows the bucket's internal limit.
fn keyed[K: Hash](rate_per_second: i64, burst: i64, capacity: i64, idle: duration.Duration, c: clock.Clock) -> Keyed[K]

Returns a keyed limiter whose buckets refill rate_per_second tokens each second and hold burst, tracking at most capacity keys. A key unused for idle is evicted; an idle of zero or less disables idle eviction. Time comes from c. Panics if capacity is less than 1 or if rate_per_second or burst is not positive or does not fit.
fn window(limit: i64, per: duration.Duration, c: clock.Clock) -> Window
Returns a window that admits limit events per per, reading time from c. Panics if limit or per is not positive.

An owned connection to a Redis server, from connect, connect_tls or connect_stream. Dropping a Client closes the connection, unless detach released it first. The shared state of the connection, for the _on functions.

A copyable reference to the state of one server connection. Copies refer to the same connection. Commands on it are serialised by an internal lock, so green threads may share it. detach returns one from a Client, adopt turns it back into a Client, and the _on functions take it directly. The RESP version in use: 3 after a successful HELLO 3, otherwise 2.
enum Error { Connect Closed Timeout Protocol TooLarge Unsupported Subscribed Aborted Type Auth(str) Server(str) }

The error type of the redis module, returned by connecting, commands and decoding. The server could not be reached or the TLS handshake failed. The client is closed or the connection ended. A connect, read or write exceeded its time limit. The peer sent bytes that are not valid RESP, or a reply whose shape the call cannot accept. A reply exceeded a bound in Limits. The server does not support HELLO 3, so RESP3 cannot be negotiated. The connection is running a subscription and accepts no commands. A transaction did not run: EXEC returned nil because a watched key changed. A reply had a type the call cannot convert, such as an array where an integer was expected. The server rejected the credentials. message is the server's text. The server answered a command with an error reply. message is the server's text.
struct Field { pub name: str pub value: str }
A hash field name and its value. The field name. The field value.
struct Limits { pub bulk: i64 pub depth: i64 pub elements: i64 }

Bounds that stop a corrupt or hostile peer from forcing large allocations while decoding. Defaults are Limits {}. The largest bulk string, verbatim string or blob error payload in bytes. A larger one fails with TooLarge. Defaults to 64 MiB. The deepest nesting of arrays, maps, sets and pushes. A deeper aggregate fails with TooLarge. Defaults to 32. The largest number of elements an aggregate may declare. A larger one fails with TooLarge. Defaults to 1048576.
struct Message { pub pattern: str pub channel: str pub payload: str }
A message delivered on a Subscription. The pattern that matched channel for a psubscribe subscription. Empty for a subscribe subscription. The channel the message was published to. The message body.
struct Options { pub host: str pub port: i64 pub username: str pub password: str pub database: i64 pub protocol: i64 pub timeout: i64 pub connect_timeout: i64 pub buffer: i64 pub limits: Limits }

Connection settings for connect, connect_tls and connect_stream. Every field has a default, so Options {} connects to a local server over RESP2 without authentication. The server host name or IP literal. Defaults to "127.0.0.1". connect_tls also uses it as the TLS server name when the config has none. The server TCP port. Defaults to 6379. The ACL user name sent with AUTH or HELLO. Empty by default: AUTH then carries the password alone and HELLO authenticates default. Ignored when password is empty. The password sent when connecting. Empty, the default, sends no authentication. The database index chosen with SELECT after connecting. 0, the default, sends no SELECT. The RESP version to negotiate. 3 sends HELLO 3; any other value stays on RESP2. Defaults to 2. The read and write time limit in milliseconds for every operation on the connection. 0, the default, waits indefinitely. An operation that exceeds it fails with Timeout and closes the client. The time limit in milliseconds for establishing the TCP connection, which fails with Timeout when exceeded. 0, the default, leaves the limit to std/net. Not used by connect_stream. The capacity of the messages channel of each Subscription. When it is full the connection stops reading until the consumer catches up. Defaults to 256. The bounds applied when decoding every reply. Defaults to Limits {}.
struct Pair { pub key: Reply pub value: Reply }
A key and value reply of a Map. The key reply. The value reply.
enum Reply { Nil Status(str) Failure(str) Integer(i64) Bulk([]u8) Array([]Reply) Map([]Pair) Set([]Reply) Boolean(bool) Double(f64) BigNumber(str) Verbatim(str, str) Push([]Reply) }

A decoded RESP reply. RESP2 produces Nil, Status, Failure, Integer, Bulk and Array. RESP3 adds the remaining variants. A null: a nil bulk string or nil array, or a RESP3 null. A simple string such as OK, QUEUED or PONG, without the leading +. An error reply, from a simple error or a RESP3 blob error. text is the message as sent, such as ERR unknown command. A signed 64-bit integer. A binary-safe string as raw bytes. An ordered list of replies. A RESP3 map: key and value replies in the order sent. A RESP3 set, in the order sent. A RESP3 boolean. A RESP3 floating point number. A RESP3 big number as its decimal digits with an optional sign, left unconverted. A RESP3 verbatim string. format is the three byte format tag such as txt or mkd and text is the content. A RESP3 out-of-band push frame. The client skips these outside a subscription.
struct Scored { pub member: str pub score: f64 }
A sorted set member and its score. The member. The score the set orders the member by.
struct SetOptions { pub ex: i64 pub px: i64 pub nx: bool pub xx: bool pub keep_ttl: bool }

Modifiers for set_with. A zero or false field leaves its modifier off. Combinations the server rejects, such as nx with xx, fail with Server. The expiry in seconds, sent as EX. 0, the default, sends none. The expiry in milliseconds, sent as PX. 0, the default, sends none. Stores the value only when the key does not exist, sent as NX. Stores the value only when the key already exists, sent as XX. Keeps the time to live already on the key instead of clearing it, sent as KEEPTTL.

A running subscription to channels or patterns, from subscribe or psubscribe. While it runs the connection is dedicated to it: commands on the client fail with Subscribed, and no read time limit applies. A green thread reads the connection and sends each message to messages. messages is closed when the subscription ends, which happens after unsubscribe is confirmed or when the connection fails or is closed. An unsubscribe leaves the client usable for commands; a failure closes it. Receives the messages in the order the server sent them. It is closed when the subscription ends.
Closes the connection. Closing twice is harmless. Later commands fail with Closed, and the messages channel of a running subscription is closed.
fn command(c: Client, args: []str) -> Reply ! Error

Sends one command and returns its reply. args[0] is the command name and the rest are its arguments, sent as binary-safe bulk strings. Every reply type is returned as is, including an error reply as Failure, which is not raised. RESP3 Push frames that arrive before the reply are skipped. Concurrent calls on one connection are serialised. Fails with Closed after the client is closed and Subscribed while a subscription runs. A transport failure fails with Timeout, Closed, TooLarge or Protocol and closes the client.
fn del(c: Client, keys: []str) -> i64 ! Error
Deletes keys and returns how many existed. An empty keys fails with Server.

Releases the client's ownership of its connection and returns the ClientHandle. Dropping c afterwards does not close the connection; close it with close_client_on or take it back with adopt. Use it to share the connection between green threads.
Drops the commands queued since multi and ends the transaction. Fails with Server when no transaction is open.

Runs the commands queued since multi and returns the result of each in order. Fails with Aborted when the server returns nil because a watched key changed, Server on an error reply such as EXECABORT or EXEC without MULTI, and Type on any other reply.
fn exists(c: Client, keys: []str) -> i64 ! Error
Returns how many of keys exist. An empty keys fails with Server.
fn expire(c: Client, key: str, seconds: i64) -> bool ! Error
