Returns s with every letter in its Unicode uppercase form. Full mappings are applied, so one character can become several: ß becomes SS. Mappings do not depend on locale or context. An ASCII string is handled as text.upper does.
Returns the byte index of the first invalid UTF-8 sequence in s, or -1 when s is valid.
Returns s with each invalid byte replaced by U+FFFD. Returns s itself when it is already valid.
Returns whether s is valid UTF-8.

Why a UTF-16 conversion failed. A surrogate code unit has no partner. at is its index in the code unit slice, not a byte offset. The byte input has an odd number of bytes, so its last byte is not a whole code unit.
struct Escape { pub code: u32 pub length: i64 pub lone: bool }

A \uXXXX escape decoded by decode_escape. The code point. A surrogate pair of two escapes gives the supplementary code point, and a surrogate with no partner keeps its own value. The number of bytes the escape used after its \u: 4 for one escape and 10 for a pair. Whether code is a surrogate with no partner.
struct Unit { pub code: u32 pub size: i64 }

A code point decoded from UTF-16 together with the number of code units it took. The decoded code point, or 0xFFFD for a lone surrogate or an out-of-range position. The number of code units consumed: 1 or 2, or 0 when the position is out of range.
Decodes UTF-16 code units into a string. Fails with LoneSurrogate at the index of the first surrogate that has no partner.
fn decode_bytes(data: []u8, order: unicode.Order) -> str ! Error

Decodes UTF-16 bytes into a string. A leading byte order mark is removed, and it selects its own byte order over order: FF FE for little-endian and FE FF for big-endian. Without one, order applies. Fails with OddLength when the bytes after the mark are an odd number and with LoneSurrogate when a surrogate has no partner.
Decodes UTF-16 bytes into a string, replacing invalid input with U+FFFD. The byte order mark is handled as in decode_bytes. Each lone surrogate and a trailing odd byte become one U+FFFD.
fn decode_escape(s: str, at: i64) -> Escape ! text.ParseError

Decodes the \uXXXX escape whose four hexadecimal digits start at index at of s, just after its \u. A high surrogate followed by a \uXXXX low surrogate is joined into one code point. The result reports a lone surrogate and leaves the policy to the caller. Fails with BadDigit at the index of the first byte of the first escape that is not a hexadecimal digit, or at s.len when it runs past the end.
Decodes UTF-16 code units into a string, replacing each lone surrogate with U+FFFD.

Decodes the code point that starts at index at of units. A surrogate pair gives a supplementary code point with size 2. A surrogate with no partner gives 0xFFFD with size 1, and an index outside units gives 0xFFFD with size 0.
Returns the UTF-16 code units of s. Each byte of s that is not valid UTF-8 becomes 0xFFFD.
fn encode_bytes(s: str, order: unicode.Order, bom: bool) -> []u8
Returns s encoded as UTF-16 bytes in the given byte order, preceded by a byte order mark when bom is true. Each byte of s that is not valid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD.
Appends the UTF-16 encoding of the code point c to out. A supplementary code point becomes a surrogate pair. A surrogate or a value above 0x10FFFF is written as 0xFFFD.
Reads UTF-16 code units from data in the given byte order. A byte order mark is not interpreted. Fails with OddLength when data.len is odd.
Returns whether u is a high (leading) surrogate, in 0xD800 to 0xDBFF.
Returns whether u is a low (trailing) surrogate, in 0xDC00 to 0xDFFF.
Returns whether u is a surrogate code unit, in 0xD800 to 0xDFFF.
fn join(high: u16, low: u16) -> u32
Returns the code point that the surrogate pair high and low encodes. high must be a high surrogate and low a low surrogate; other values give a meaningless result.
Returns the bytes of units in the given byte order, two bytes per unit and without a byte order mark.
Reads UTF-16 code units from data in the given byte order, ignoring a trailing odd byte. A byte order mark is not interpreted.

Why a UTF-32 conversion failed. A value is not a Unicode scalar value: it is a surrogate or above 0x10FFFF. at is its index in the code point slice, not a byte offset. The byte input is not a multiple of 4 bytes long.
Decodes code points into a string. Fails with InvalidCodePoint at the index of the first surrogate or value above 0x10FFFF.
fn decode_bytes(data: []u8, order: unicode.Order) -> str ! Error

Decodes UTF-32 bytes into a string. A leading byte order mark is removed, and it selects its own byte order over order. Without one, order applies. Fails with BadLength when the bytes after the mark are not a multiple of 4 and with InvalidCodePoint for a surrogate or a value above 0x10FFFF.
Decodes UTF-32 bytes into a string, replacing invalid input with U+FFFD. The byte order mark is handled as in decode_bytes. Each invalid value and a trailing partial code point become one U+FFFD.
Decodes code points into a string, replacing each invalid value with U+FFFD.
Returns the code points of s as a slice of u32. Each byte of s that is not valid UTF-8 becomes 0xFFFD.
fn encode_bytes(s: str, order: unicode.Order, bom: bool) -> []u8
Returns s encoded as UTF-32 bytes in the given byte order, preceded by a byte order mark when bom is true. Each byte of s that is not valid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD.
Reads code points from data in the given byte order. A byte order mark is not interpreted and values are not validated. Fails with BadLength when data.len is not a multiple of 4.
Returns the bytes of cs in the given byte order, four bytes per code point and without a byte order mark.
struct Field { pub name: str pub value: str }
A name and value pair of a query string or of an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. The name, before encoding. The value, before encoding.
Returns fields as an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body: name=value pairs joined by &. Names and values are encoded with escape_form. Returns an empty string for no fields.

Returns s percent-encoded, keeping only the unreserved bytes A-Z, a-z, 0-9, -, ., _ and ~. Every other byte becomes % and two uppercase hexadecimal digits, so a space is %20. Use it for one path segment, one query name or one query value.
Returns s encoded as one name or value of an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body. As escape, except that a space becomes +.
Returns s with the bytes that are not allowed in a request target percent-encoded, as decided by target_byte. Existing % escapes and reserved delimiters are left as they are.
fn escape_where(s: str, keep: fn(u8) -> bool) -> str
Returns s with every byte for which keep returns false replaced by % and two uppercase hexadecimal digits. Returns s itself when every byte is kept.

Parses a query string, or an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body, into a map of names to values. Names and values are decoded with unescape_form_lossy. Empty pairs are skipped, a name without = maps to an empty string, and a repeated name keeps its last value.
Returns path with its . and .. segments resolved, as in RFC 3986 section 5.2.4. A .. above the root is dropped. A path that ends in a dot segment ends in /.
fn resolve(base: str, reference: str) -> str

Resolves the URI reference reference against base and returns the target URI, following RFC 3986 section 5.2. The fragment of base is dropped and the fragment of reference is kept. A reference with a scheme is returned as it is, and one starting with // takes the scheme of base. An empty reference gives base, one starting with ? replaces the query, one starting with / replaces the path, and any other is joined to the directory of the base path. Dot segments are resolved in the path of the result. base may be only a path and query, such as /a/b?c.
Returns the index of the : that ends the scheme of s, or -1 when s does not start with a scheme. A scheme is a letter followed by letters, digits, +, - or ..

Returns whether c may appear unescaped in the path and query of a request target. Controls, space, DEL and non-ASCII bytes are not allowed, nor are ", <, >, \, ^, `, {, | and }. Reserved delimiters such as /, ?, &, = and % are allowed.
Returns s with each %XX sequence replaced by its byte, or none when a % is not followed by two hexadecimal digits. A + is left as it is.
Returns s with each %XX sequence replaced by its byte and each + by a space. A % that is not followed by two hexadecimal digits is kept as written. Use it for query names and values and form bodies.
Returns s with each %XX sequence replaced by its byte. A % that is not followed by two hexadecimal digits and a + are kept as written. Use it for path segments.
Returns whether c is an unreserved byte of RFC 3986: A-Z, a-z, 0-9, -, ., _ or ~.
Returns s without its fragment: everything from the first #.
Why a UUID string was rejected. The string is not 36 bytes long. A byte is not a hexadecimal digit, or a hyphen is missing where the format requires one. at is its index.
A 128-bit universally unique identifier. bytes holds the 16 bytes in network order. The 16 bytes of the identifier, most significant first.
fn equal(a: Uuid, b: Uuid) -> bool
Returns whether a and b hold the same 16 bytes.
Returns u as 36 lowercase characters in the 8-4-4-4-12 hyphenated form.
Returns the creation time of a version 7 UUID as Unix milliseconds, or none for any other version.
Returns the version number held in the high four bits of byte 6. The variant bits are not checked.
Returns the nil UUID, whose 128 bits are all zero.

Parses the 36-character hyphenated form, accepting upper- and lowercase digits. Fails with Length when s is not 36 bytes, and with BadDigit at the index of the first byte that is not a hexadecimal digit or not a hyphen at index 8, 13, 18 or 23. The version and variant are not checked.
Returns a random version 4 UUID with the RFC 9562 variant bits. The 122 free bits come from std/crypto's random source.

Returns a version 7 UUID that sorts by creation time. The first 48 bits are the Unix time in milliseconds read from the real-time clock, the version and variant bits follow RFC 9562, and the remaining bits are random. UUIDs made within one millisecond are not ordered among themselves.
A router: routes, the middleware applied to them and a path prefix. Made by app. group makes a child app that registers its routes on the same router.
struct Context { pub request: http.Request pub params: [str: str] pub user: str pub claims: json.Value pub values: [str: str] pub response_headers: []header.Header pub session: *Session? }

The state of one request, passed to middleware and handlers. The request as received. The path parameters of the matched route, keyed by name without the leading :. A trailing * segment is stored under "*". Values are percent-decoded. The authenticated principal, or an empty string until an authentication middleware sets it. The verified token claims set by bearer, jwt and oidc, or Null when none were set. Per-request storage that middleware and handlers use to pass strings to each other. Headers added to the response after the handler returns, in the order they were set. They are appended, so a header the handler also set appears twice. The session loaded by the sessions middleware, or none when the request has not been through it.
struct Info { pub title: str pub version: str pub description: str }
The info object of the OpenAPI document. The title of the API. The version of the API, not of the OpenAPI specification. A description of the API. Omitted from the document when empty.
struct Middleware { pub run: fn(*Context, fn() -> http.Response) -> http.Response pub security: Security? }

A step that wraps a handler. Middleware registered on an app applies to the routes registered after it, in registration order, with the first registered running outermost. Runs the step with the request context and next, which calls the rest of the chain and returns its response. A step that returns without calling next short-circuits the chain. The scheme the step enforces, listed in the OpenAPI document for every route it wraps, or none for a step that does not authenticate.
struct OidcClient { pub issuer: str pub client_id: str pub client_secret: str pub redirect_uri: str pub scopes: str }

The registration of this application with an OpenID Connect provider, used by oidc_login. The provider's issuer URL, from which the discovery document is fetched. The identifier the provider issued to the application. It is also the audience the ID token must carry. The client secret. Left empty for a public client, in which case none is sent. The callback URL registered with the provider. The space-separated scopes to request. Defaults to openid profile email.
struct Operation { pub summary: str pub description: str pub tags: []str pub request: serde.Schema? pub response: serde.Schema? pub status: i64 }

Describes a route for the OpenAPI document. Returned by route and its method helpers so a caller can fill it in. A one-line summary of the operation. Omitted from the document when empty. A longer description of the operation. Omitted from the document when empty. Tags that group the operation in the document. The schema of the JSON request body, or none when the operation takes no body. The schema of the JSON response body, or none when the operation does not describe one. The status code of the success response in the document. Defaults to 200.
enum Problem { BadRequest(str) Unauthorized(str) Forbidden(str) NotFound Conflict(str) Unprocessable(str) TooMany Internal(str) Status(i64, str) }

An error that a handler returns to the client as an RFC 9457 problem response. Each variant maps to a status code, and problem_response renders it. Handlers declared ! Problem can fail with any variant. The request is malformed. Status 400; detail explains what is wrong. Credentials are missing or invalid. Status 401; detail explains why. The caller is not allowed to do this. Status 403; detail explains why. The resource does not exist. Status 404. The request conflicts with the current state of the resource. Status 409; detail explains the conflict. The request is well-formed but its content is not acceptable. Status 422; detail explains why. The caller has sent too many requests. Status 429. The server failed. Status 500; detail is sent to the client, so it must not hold secrets. A problem with any status code, for statuses the other variants do not cover. The title is the standard text of code.
struct Security { pub name: str pub scheme: json.Value }
Describes how a middleware authenticates, for the generated OpenAPI document. The key of the scheme in components.securitySchemes, such as bearer. The OpenAPI security scheme object as JSON.

The key-value state of one visitor, kept in an encrypted cookie by sessions. The stored values. Writing to the map directly does not mark the session as changed, so use session_set and session_clear to change it.
struct SessionOptions { pub key: []u8 pub cookie: str pub max_age: i64 pub secure: bool pub same_site: http.SameSite pub path: str }

Configures the sessions middleware. The AES-256-GCM key that seals the cookie. It must be exactly 32 bytes. The name of the cookie. Defaults to session. The lifetime in seconds, counted from the last write. Defaults to one day. Whether the cookie is marked Secure. Defaults to true. The SameSite attribute of the cookie. Defaults to Lax; Unset omits it. The Path attribute of the cookie. Defaults to /.
struct StaticOptions { pub index: str pub listing: bool pub dotfiles: bool pub cache_control: str pub precompressed: bool }

Configures static_with. The file served for a directory. Defaults to index.html; an empty string disables it. Whether a directory without an index file gets an HTML listing. Defaults to false, which answers 404. Whether files and directories whose name starts with . are served. Defaults to false, which answers 404. The cache-control value sent with files. An empty string, the default, sends none. Whether to serve a .br or .gz file next to the requested file when the client accepts that coding, preferring br. Defaults to false. The response keeps the content type of the original file and carries content-encoding.
fn del(a: *App, path: str, handler: fn(*Context) -> http.Response) -> *Operation
Registers a DELETE route. See route.
fn endpoint[Req, Res](a: *App, method: str, path: str, status: i64, handle: fn(*Context, Req) -> Res ! Problem) -> *Operation

Registers a route whose handler takes a JSON body decoded as Req and returns a Res as JSON. The response has status on success. A body that does not decode, or a Problem that handle fails with, becomes the problem response. The schemas of Req and Res and status are recorded in the returned Operation for the OpenAPI document.
fn get(a: *App, path: str, handler: fn(*Context) -> http.Response) -> *Operation
Registers a GET route. See route.

Returns a child app whose routes carry prefix appended to the parent's prefix and the parent's middleware followed by middleware. The child registers its routes on the parent's router, in the order of registration across both.

Returns the app as a request handler for http.serve. A request whose path matches a route of another method runs the middleware of the first such route and then gets a 405 problem with an allow header, so middleware such as cors can answer first. A request that matches no route gets a 404 problem. Each request is recorded as a server span named after the matched route pattern.
fn oidc_login(a: *App, login: str, callback: str, client: OidcClient, signed_in: fn(*Context, jose.Claims) -> http.Response)

Registers the two routes of an authorization-code sign-in with PKCE on a. login redirects with 302 to the provider's authorization endpoint with a fresh state, nonce and code challenge, which it keeps in the session, and answers 502 when the provider cannot be reached. callback checks state, exchanges the code, verifies the ID token and its nonce, clears the stored values, and returns the response of signed_in called with the verified claims. A bad state or missing code gets a 400 problem, and a failed exchange or nonce mismatch a 401 problem. The sessions middleware must wrap both routes, and a request that reaches either route without it gets a 500 problem.
fn openapi(a: *App, path: str, info: Info)
Registers a GET route at path that serves the document of openapi_document as JSON. The document is built on each request, so it reflects the routes registered at that time.

Returns an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the routes of the app. A :name segment becomes {name} with a path parameter. Operations list their summary, description, tags, request body and response from their Operation, a default response of the Problem schema, and the security schemes of their middleware. Struct and enum schemas are shared in components.schemas.
fn patch(a: *App, path: str, handler: fn(*Context) -> http.Response) -> *Operation
Registers a PATCH route. See route.
fn post(a: *App, path: str, handler: fn(*Context) -> http.Response) -> *Operation
Registers a POST route. See route.
fn put(a: *App, path: str, handler: fn(*Context) -> http.Response) -> *Operation
Registers a PUT route. See route.
fn query_endpoint[Res](a: *App, method: str, path: str, handle: fn(*Context) -> Res ! Problem) -> *Operation
Registers a route whose handler returns a Res as JSON with status 200. A Problem that handle fails with becomes the problem response. The schema of Res is recorded in the returned Operation.
fn route(a: *App, method: str, path: str, handler: fn(*Context) -> http.Response) -> *Operation

Registers a handler for method and path and returns the route's Operation. The app's prefix is prepended to path. A segment starting with : captures one path segment into Context.params, and a final * segment captures the rest of the path under "*". Routes are tried in registration order, and the first whose path and method match handles the request. A GET route also answers HEAD.
fn static(a: *App, prefix: str, dir: str)
Serves the files under dir below prefix with the default options. See static_with.
fn static_with(a: *App, prefix: str, dir: str, o: StaticOptions)

Serves the files under dir for GET requests below prefix. The request path must not contain .., a backslash or an encoded slash, or the response is a 400 problem. A path that resolves outside dir, including through a symbolic link, or to anything but a regular file or directory, gets a 404 problem. A directory requested without a trailing slash is redirected with 301. Files are served by files.serve_file_with, so HEAD, conditional and range requests are supported.
Adds a middleware to the app. It applies only to routes registered after this call, so call it before registering the routes it should wrap.

Decodes the request body as JSON into T. Fails with BadRequest for a syntax error or nesting that is too deep, and with Unprocessable for a value of the wrong type, a missing field, an unknown variant or a number out of range. The detail names the position or field.
Returns the cookies of the request as a map of names to values. See http.request_cookies.
Returns the CSRF token of the session, creating and storing a random 64-character hex token if there is none. Send it to the client for the x-csrf-token header that csrf checks.

Returns a Server-Sent Events response fed by producer. producer runs in its own task with an emitter, and the stream ends when it returns. sse.send on the emitter returns false once the client has disconnected.

Returns a Server-Sent Events response that sends every event received on ch. The stream ends when ch is closed or the client disconnects. A keepalive comment is sent when no event has arrived for the default keepalive interval.
Returns the value of the first request header called name, or none when it is absent. The name is matched without regard to case.
Returns the path parameter name, or an empty string when the route has no such parameter.
fn param_int(c: *Context, name: str) -> i64 ! Problem
Returns the path parameter name as an integer. Fails with BadRequest when it is empty or not an integer.
Returns the query parameter name, or none when the request has no such parameter. The query string is parsed on each call.
Removes every value from the session and deletes the cookie.
Returns the session value for key, or none when it is not set. Without the sessions middleware the session is empty and lasts only for the request.
fn session_set(c: *Context, key: str, value: str)
Sets the session value for key, so that the cookie is rewritten. Without the sessions middleware the value is lost when the request ends.
Adds a set-cookie header for cookie to the response. It does not replace an earlier cookie of the same name. See http.format_set_cookie for how the cookie is written.
fn set_header(c: *Context, name: str, value: str)
Adds a header to the response. The header is added after the handler returns and does not replace a header of the same name.
Sets the summary and tags of an operation.

Returns the application/problem+json response for a problem. The body holds type set to about:blank, title, status and detail. The title is the standard text of the status. A 401 response also carries www-authenticate: Bearer.

Returns a middleware that keeps a Session for each visitor in an encrypted cookie. Fails with Invalid when o.key is not 32 bytes. The cookie holds the values and an expiry, sealed with AES-256-GCM and bound to the cookie name. A cookie that is missing, altered or expired gives an empty session. A cookie is sent only when the request changed the session, which restarts its lifetime, or cleared it, which deletes the cookie. A session that is cleared stays cleared even if values are set afterwards. The scheme is listed in the OpenAPI document as an apiKey in a cookie.
fn api_key(header_name: str, check: fn(str) -> str?) -> Middleware

Returns a middleware that authenticates requests by the API key in the header_name header. check maps a key to the principal it belongs to, or none to reject it. A principal is stored in Context.user. A missing, empty or rejected key gets a 401 problem. The scheme is listed in the OpenAPI document as an apiKey in a header.
Returns an empty app with no routes, no middleware and no prefix.
fn basic(realm: str, check: fn(str, str) -> str?) -> Middleware

Returns a middleware that authenticates requests with HTTP Basic credentials. check receives the user name and password and returns the principal, which is stored in Context.user, or none to reject them. The user name ends at the first colon of the decoded credentials. Missing, malformed or rejected credentials get a 401 problem with a www-authenticate: Basic challenge for realm.

Returns a middleware that authenticates requests with a bearer token from the authorization header. check returns the token's claims, or none to reject it. Accepted claims are stored in Context.claims, and a string sub claim is stored in Context.user. A missing or rejected token gets a 401 problem. The scheme is listed in the OpenAPI document as HTTP bearer with the JWT format.
fn compress(minimum: i64, level: i64) -> Middleware

Returns a middleware that compresses response bodies. The coding is the first of zstd, br and gzip that the accept-encoding header accepts with a non-zero quality. A response is compressed only when its body has at least minimum bytes, is not streamed, has no content-encoding, and has a content-type that is text/* other than an event stream, or contains json, xml, javascript or svg. level is passed to the compressor. The response gets content-encoding and vary: Accept-Encoding, replacing any vary it had, and loses its content-length.

Returns a middleware that allows cross-origin requests from origin with the request headers allow_headers. It sets access-control-allow-origin and vary: Origin on every response. A request with method OPTIONS is answered with 204, the allowed methods and allow_headers joined by commas, without calling the rest of the chain. The middleware runs for a request whose path matches a route of another method, so a preflight for a route registered with get or post reaches it.

Returns a middleware that rejects unsafe requests without the session's CSRF token. Requests other than GET, HEAD and OPTIONS must carry an x-csrf-token header equal to the session's token, compared in constant time. Otherwise the response is a 403 problem. It must run after sessions.
fn html(status: i64, body: str) -> http.Response
Returns a response with status and body as text/html; charset=utf-8.
fn json_response[T](status: i64, v: T) -> http.Response
Returns a response with status whose body is v serialised as JSON and whose content-type is application/json.

Returns a bearer middleware that accepts JWTs verified against keys under options. The signature, exp, nbf, and the issuer and audience when options names them, are checked. The full payload becomes Context.claims. Any verification failure gets a 401 problem.
Returns a middleware that prints METHOD path status to standard output after each request.
fn oidc(issuer: str, audience: str) -> Middleware

Returns a bearer middleware that accepts JWTs issued by the OpenID Connect provider at issuer for audience. The signing keys come from the jwks_uri of the provider's discovery document. They are cached for an hour and refetched when a token names an unknown kid, at most once a minute. Only asymmetric signature algorithms are accepted. A token that fails verification, or a provider that cannot be reached, gets a 401 problem. The scheme is listed in the OpenAPI document as openIdConnect.
fn redirect(location: str, status: i64) -> http.Response
Returns an empty response with status, such as 302 or 303, and a location header of location.
Returns a middleware that requires the session value key to be set. The value is stored in Context.user. Otherwise the response is a 401 problem.
fn text(status: i64, body: str) -> http.Response
Returns a response with status and body as text/plain; charset=utf-8.
struct Authentication { pub credential_id: []u8 pub new_sign_count: i64 pub user_verified: bool pub multi_device: bool pub backed_up: bool }

A verified authentication. The id of the credential that signed, from rawId. The signature counter from the response, to store in place of the old one. Whether the UV flag was set. Whether the credential is eligible for backup or sync across devices (the BE flag). Whether the credential is currently backed up (the BS flag).
struct AuthenticationOptions { pub rp_id: str pub challenge: []u8 pub timeout: i64 pub allow_credentials: [][]u8 pub user_verification: UserVerification }

The inputs of an authentication (assertion) request. authentication_options turns it into the JSON for navigator.credentials.get. The default challenge is evaluated each time a value is built. The relying party identifier. The random challenge the authenticator signs, which verify_authentication must be given again as Expected.challenge. Defaults to 64 random bytes. How long the client waits for the user, in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000. The credential ids the user may authenticate with. Empty, the default, lets the client offer any discoverable credential for rp_id. The user verification requirement. Defaults to Preferred.

enum Error { MalformedCredential(str) IdMismatch WrongCredentialType(str) MalformedClientData WrongClientDataType(str) ChallengeMismatch OriginMismatch(str) MalformedAttestationObject UnsupportedAttestation(str) UnexpectedAttestationStatement MalformedAuthenticatorData RpIdHashMismatch UserNotPresent UserNotVerified MissingCredentialData InconsistentBackupFlags MalformedPublicKey UnsupportedAlgorithm(i64) BadSignature SignCountRegression(i64, i64) }

The reasons a registration or authentication response is rejected. A member of the credential JSON is missing, has the wrong type or is not valid Base64url. field names it. The credential id is not the Base64url of rawId. The credential type is not public-key. found is the type received. clientDataJSON is not a JSON object with string type, challenge and origin members, or its challenge is not Base64url. The client data type is not webauthn.create for a registration or webauthn.get for an authentication. found is the type received. The client data challenge differs from Expected.challenge. The client data origin differs from Expected.origin. found is the origin received. The attestation object is not a CBOR map with a text fmt and a byte string authData. The attestation format is not none. format is the format received. The attestation statement is not an empty map, as the none format requires. The authenticator data is shorter than 37 bytes, has invalid attested credential data or extensions, or has trailing bytes. The authenticator data does not start with the SHA-256 of Expected.rp_id. The user present (UP) flag is not set. Expected.require_user_verification is set and the user verified (UV) flag is not. A registration response has no attested credential data or an empty credential id. The backup state (BS) flag is set while backup eligibility (BE) is not. The credential public key is not a valid COSE_Key for a supported algorithm. The credential public key uses a COSE algorithm other than -7, -8 and -257. alg is the identifier received. The assertion signature does not verify under the stored public key. The signature counter did not increase, which can indicate a cloned authenticator. received is the counter in the response and stored the one the caller holds.
struct Expected { pub challenge: []u8 pub rp_id: str pub origin: str pub require_user_verification: bool }

What the relying party expects of a response. The challenge that was sent in the options, as raw bytes. Compared in constant time. The relying party identifier. The authenticator data must carry its SHA-256. The exact origin the client reports, such as https://example.com. Whether the UV flag must be set. Defaults to false; the UP flag is always required.

A credential public key decoded from a COSE_Key (RFC 9052). The supported algorithms are ES256 (COSE -7), EdDSA with Ed25519 (-8) and RS256 (-257). A P-256 ECDSA key as the 65-byte uncompressed SEC 1 point: 0x04 followed by the 32-byte x and y coordinates. An Ed25519 key as its 32-byte public key (RFC 8032). An RSA key for RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256 (RFC 8017), with the modulus and exponent stripped of leading zero bytes.
struct Registration { pub credential_id: []u8 pub public_key: []u8 pub sign_count: i64 pub aaguid: []u8 pub user_verified: bool pub multi_device: bool pub backed_up: bool }

A verified registration, ready to store. The credential id, the key to look the credential up by. The credential public key as the CBOR encoded COSE_Key bytes, which verify_authentication and parse_public_key take. The initial signature counter, 0 for authenticators that do not count. The 16-byte authenticator attestation GUID identifying the authenticator model. Whether the UV flag was set. Whether the credential is eligible for backup or sync across devices (the BE flag). Whether the credential is currently backed up (the BS flag).

struct RegistrationOptions { pub rp_id: str pub rp_name: str pub user_name: str pub user_id: []u8 pub user_display_name: str pub challenge: []u8 pub timeout: i64 pub exclude_credentials: [][]u8 pub selection: Selection? pub algorithms: []i64 }

The inputs of a registration (credential creation) request. registration_options turns it into the JSON for navigator.credentials.create. The defaults for user_id and challenge are evaluated each time a value is built, so every request gets fresh random values. The relying party identifier, normally the registrable domain of the site. The human-readable name of the relying party. The account name of the user, such as an email address. The user handle, an opaque identifier of the account that should not reveal personal information. Defaults to 64 random bytes. The display name of the user. When empty, the default, user_name is used. The random challenge the authenticator signs, which verify_registration must be given again as Expected.challenge. Defaults to 64 random bytes. How long the client waits for the user, in milliseconds. Defaults to 60000. The credential ids the user already has, so the authenticator does not register the same one twice. Empty by default. The authenticator selection criteria, or none to omit authenticatorSelection and leave the choice to the client. The COSE algorithm identifiers to accept, in order of preference. Defaults to supported_algorithms(): -8 (EdDSA), -7 (ES256) and -257 (RS256), the algorithms parse_public_key supports.

Whether the authenticator should create a discoverable credential, the residentKey requirement of WebAuthn. A discoverable credential is not wanted; residentKey is sent as discouraged. A discoverable credential is preferred; residentKey is sent as preferred. A discoverable credential is required; residentKey is sent as required and requireResidentKey as true.
struct Selection { pub resident_key: ResidentKey? pub user_verification: UserVerification }

The authenticatorSelection criteria of a registration request. The discoverable credential requirement, or none to leave residentKey out of the request. requireResidentKey is true only for Required. The user verification requirement. Defaults to Preferred.

How strongly the authenticator should verify the user, such as with a PIN or biometric, the userVerification requirement of WebAuthn. User verification should not be performed. User verification is performed when the authenticator supports it, but its absence is accepted. User verification must be performed. Pair it with Expected.require_user_verification so the server enforces it.
Returns the JSON object for PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions described by o. Binary values (challenge and credential ids) are Base64url without padding.
fn verify_signature(key: PublicKey, data: []u8, signature: []u8) -> bool

Returns whether signature is a valid signature of data under key. ES256 verifies a DER encoded ECDSA signature over the SHA-256 of data, RS256 a PKCS#1 v1.5 signature over the SHA-256 of data and EdDSA a signature over data itself. Returns false, not an error, for a signature that does not verify.

Returns the JSON object for PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions described by o. Binary values (user.id, challenge and credential ids) are Base64url without padding, as the JSON form of the WebAuthn API expects. attestation is always none, matching verify_registration, which accepts only that format. authenticatorSelection is present only when o.selection is set.

Decodes a CBOR encoded COSE_Key into a PublicKey. The alg label (3) selects the type and must agree with the other labels: ES256 needs key type 2 (EC2), curve 1 (P-256) and 32-byte x and y; EdDSA needs key type 1 (OKP), curve 6 (Ed25519) and a 32-byte x; RS256 needs key type 3 (RSA) and a non-empty modulus n and exponent e. Fails with MalformedPublicKey when the CBOR is invalid, is not a map or a label is missing, has the wrong type or the wrong value, and with UnsupportedAlgorithm carrying the alg for any other algorithm.
Returns the COSE algorithm identifiers parse_public_key supports, in order of preference: EdDSA (-8), ES256 (-7) and RS256 (-257).
fn verify_authentication(credential_json: json.Value, expected: Expected, public_key: []u8, sign_count: i64) -> Authentication ! Error

Verifies the JSON of a navigator.credentials.get response against the stored credential and returns the result. credential_json is the JSON form of a PublicKeyCredential whose response has clientDataJSON, authenticatorData and signature, Base64url encoded. public_key and sign_count are the values saved from Registration or the last Authentication; the caller finds them from the credential id before calling. The checks are those of verify_registration with the client data type webauthn.get, then the signature counter, then the signature over the authenticator data followed by the SHA-256 of the client data. The counter is checked only when either value is nonzero, and must then be strictly greater than sign_count, otherwise SignCountRegression is returned. Fails with BadSignature when the signature does not verify and otherwise with the Error variant of the first check that fails.
fn verify_registration(credential_json: json.Value, expected: Expected) -> Registration ! Error

Verifies the JSON of a navigator.credentials.create response and returns the credential to store. credential_json is the JSON form of a PublicKeyCredential (id, rawId, type and a response with clientDataJSON and attestationObject, Base64url encoded). The checks follow WebAuthn registration verification: the credential id and type, the client data type webauthn.create, challenge and origin, the rpIdHash, the UP flag (and UV when required), the attested credential data and its COSE public key, and the backup flags. Only the none attestation format with an empty statement is accepted; no attestation signature or certificate chain is verified. Fails with the Error variant of the first check that fails.
struct Attribute { pub name: Name pub value: str }

An attribute of a start tag. Namespace declarations (xmlns and xmlns:prefix) are returned as attributes too, in the namespace http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/. The attribute name. The value with references resolved and whitespace normalised as the specification requires. Attribute-list declarations in the internal subset supply defaults and normalise tokenised types.
struct Element { pub name: Name pub attributes: []Attribute pub children: []Node }

An element of a parsed document. Made by parse. Every string is an owned copy, independent of the input. The element's name with its namespace resolved. The attributes in document order, including namespace declarations. The child nodes in document order.
enum Error { Malformed(i64, i64, str) Limit(i64, i64, str) Unsupported(str) }

The error returned when reading XML fails. The input is not well-formed or breaks a namespace constraint, at line and column, counted from 1; message says why. The document exceeds a limit of the reader, at line and column: elements nested deeper than 1024, entities nested deeper than 40, or entity expansion beyond 1048576 bytes plus eight times the input size. The document uses a feature the reader does not support; message names it. Today that is an encoding other than UTF-8, UTF-16, ISO-8859-1 or US-ASCII.
struct Name { pub prefix: str pub local: str pub namespace: str }

An element or attribute name with its namespace resolved (Namespaces in XML 1.0). The prefix as written, or the empty string when the name has none. The part of the name after the prefix, or the whole name when it has none. The namespace URI the prefix resolves to, or the empty string when the name is in no namespace. An unprefixed attribute is in no namespace; an unprefixed element is in the default namespace, if one is declared.
enum Node { Element(*Element) Text(str) CData(str) Comment(str) Instruction(str, str) }

A node in the content of an Element. A child element. Character data. Adjacent text, including text split by entity references, is one Text node. A CDATA section's content, kept apart from Text nodes. A comment, without its delimiters. A processing instruction with its target and data.
struct Position { pub line: i64 pub column: i64 }
A location in the document. The line, counting from 1. \r\n and \r count as one line break. The column, counting from 1 in characters, not bytes.

A pull parser over one XML document, made by reader. It follows XML 1.0 (fifth edition) with Namespaces in XML 1.0, enforces well-formedness and the namespace constraints, and parses the internal DTD subset. General entities declared there expand, including markup, with recursion detection; external entities are never fetched and parameter entities are not expanded. Names are resolved and interned per reader. next returns tokens and position says where the last one began.
enum Token { StartElement(Name, []Attribute, bool) EndElement(Name) Text(str) CData(str) Comment(str) Instruction(str, str) Doctype(str) End }

One unit of an XML document, returned by next. A Text token carries character data, and every other markup construct has a token of its own. The strings view the reader's input unless a reference or normalisation forced a copy, so copy a value to keep it after the input changes. A start tag, with its name, its attributes and whether it is an empty-element tag (<a/>). An empty element has no EndElement token after it. An end tag. It carries the name of the element it closes, with the namespace of its start tag. Character data with character and entity references replaced. Text can arrive as several consecutive Text tokens, because an entity that expands to markup splits it. Whitespace between elements is returned as text. Text outside the root element is an error unless it is whitespace, which is skipped. A CDATA section, without its delimiters. A comment, without <!-- and -->. A processing instruction with its target and its data, which is empty when there is none. The XML declaration is not returned as an instruction. The document type declaration, trimmed, from the root name to the end of the internal subset, without <!DOCTYPE and the closing >. The end of the document, returned once the root element is closed and the input ends, and by every call after that.

A writer that builds an XML document in memory, made by writer. Call start_element, write_attribute, write_text and the other write_ functions in document order and finish to take the text. Text and attribute values are escaped. An element with no content is written as <a/>. With indentation on, an element that contains only elements, comments and instructions has each child on its own line, indented two spaces per level, and an element with text or CDATA is written without added whitespace.
Returns the value of the first attribute of e whose local name is local, or none when there is none. The namespace is ignored, and namespace declarations are not attributes here.
Returns the first child element of e whose local name is local, or none when there is none. The namespace is ignored.
Returns every child element of e whose local name is local, in document order. The name * matches every child element. The namespace is ignored.

Returns the element at path below e, or none when a step finds nothing. path is steps separated by /, for example a/b. Each step selects the first child element with that local name, and * selects the first child element of any name. Empty steps are skipped, so an empty path returns e itself.

Returns e and its descendants as XML text. indent selects indented output as writer does. Names are written as qualified gives them, and attributes, text, CDATA, comments and instructions are written as the write_ functions do. The namespace declarations kept in e.attributes are written as attributes. No declaration is written.

Returns the text of e: the Text and CData content of e and of all its descendant elements, in document order. Comments and processing instructions are left out. An element whose only child is a text or CDATA node returns it without copying.
Returns the name as written: prefix:local, or local when there is no prefix.

Returns the next token of the document. The XML declaration is read and checked first and is not returned. Comments, processing instructions and the document type declaration are returned in document order, including those before and after the root element. Returns End after the root element and everything following it. Fails with Malformed for anything that is not well-formed, including an unclosed element, a missing root element, content after the root element, mismatched tags, duplicate attributes and undeclared prefixes; with Limit when a limit is exceeded; and with Unsupported for an unsupported encoding.
Returns the line and column where the token that next returned last began. Before the first token it is line 1, column 1.
Closes the innermost open element, as </name>, or as /> when it has no content. Does nothing when no element is open.
Closes every element that is still open and returns the document text. The returned string views the writer's buffer, so do not write to the writer afterwards.

Opens the element name, ending the previous start tag if it is still open. name is written as given, so a prefix goes in it. It is not checked. Follow it with write_attribute and write_namespace calls, then the content, then end_element.
fn write_attribute(w: *Writer, name: str, value: str)

Writes the attribute name with value in the start tag that start_element just opened. The value is escaped for an attribute: &, <, ", carriage return, newline and tab become references. Does nothing once the start tag has ended, that is after any content or a nested element is written.
Writes s as a CDATA section. A ]]> inside s is split across two sections, so the output stays well-formed. Text inside an element turns off indentation for that element.
Writes a comment. A -- inside s, and a - at its end, get a space inserted so the output stays well-formed.
Writes the declaration <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>. Call it before the root element.
fn write_instruction(w: *Writer, target: str, data: str)
Writes the processing instruction target with data. When data is empty nothing follows the target. A ?> inside data gets a space inserted between the characters. target is not checked.
fn write_namespace(w: *Writer, prefix: str, uri: str)
Writes a namespace declaration in the open start tag: xmlns for an empty prefix and xmlns:prefix otherwise, with the value uri. Does nothing once the start tag has ended.
Writes the text s as character data, escaping &, <, > and carriage return. Text inside an element turns off indentation for that element.

Decodes the XML document data into a T through std/serde. The root element is the value. A struct, map or enum is read from the attributes and child elements of an element, matched to fields by local name, ignoring the namespace; attributes in the xmlns and xsi namespaces are skipped. A slice field is read from all child elements with the field's name, or from a whitespace separated attribute value; a root slice is read from the children of the root element. An element with xsi:nil of true or 1 reads as none, and a missing optional field is none. Scalars are read from the text of the element or attribute, trimmed. A boolean is true, false, 1 or 0; a float may be INF, -INF or NaN; a []u8 is base64. An enum variant is the element's text for a variant without fields and the first child element for one with fields, named by that element. Fails with serde.Error.Syntax, carrying the line, for malformed XML, with Mismatch and Range when a value does not fit its type, and with Missing and UnknownVariant as serde.read describes. In errors other than Syntax, at is 0.

Parses the XML document data into a tree and returns its root element. Reads with reader, so the same encodings, entity handling and limits apply, and fails with the reader's Error. Comments and processing instructions outside the root element and the document type declaration are dropped.

Returns a reader over the document data. The input may be UTF-8, UTF-16 with a byte order mark, ISO-8859-1 or US-ASCII, as the byte order mark or the encoding of the XML declaration says; it is converted to UTF-8, and \r\n and lone \r become \n, before reading. An input in another encoding, a UTF-16 label without a byte order mark, or invalid UTF-16 makes the first call to next fail.
fn serialize_value[T](root: str, v: T) -> str

Returns v as an XML document with the root element root, written without indentation or declaration. Every struct field, map entry and slice element becomes a child element named by the field, the key or item; scalars are written as element text, booleans as true and false, floats as NaN, INF or -INF when not finite, and []u8 as base64. A slice that is a field becomes repeated elements with the field's name, and a top-level slice becomes item elements inside the root. A none optional writes nothing. An enum variant without fields is its name as text, and a variant with fields is an element named by the variant that holds the fields. Nothing is written as an attribute. A value that writes no element gives <root/>.
Returns an empty writer. When indent is true, element-only content is indented with two spaces per level and a newline starts each line after the first.
enum Error { Syntax(i64, i64, str) TooManyNodes(i64, i64) }

The error returned when reading YAML fails. The text is not valid YAML 1.2, at line and column, counted from 1; message says why. It covers every problem the scanner, parser and composer find, for example a bad indentation, an undefined alias or tag handle, a duplicate mapping key, an invalid escape, a scalar that does not match its tag or an integer that does not fit an i64. Expanding aliases would create more nodes than Options.max_nodes allows, at the line and column of the alias or node that crossed the limit, counted from 1. Each use of an alias counts as the size of the node it refers to.
struct Event { pub kind: EventKind pub anchor: str pub tag: str pub value: str pub style: Style pub explicit: bool pub line: i64 pub column: i64 }

One event of the YAML parse stream, as returned by events. Events are in document order. Every sequence and mapping has a start and an end event, and the nodes between them are its entries; a mapping alternates keys and values. What the event is. The anchor name without the &, or the empty string when the node has none. For an Alias event it is the name being referred to. The node's tag, resolved against the %TAG directives of the document, or the empty string when it has none. !!str is tag:yaml.org,2002:str, a local tag !x is !x, a verbatim tag !<uri> is uri and the non-specific tag ! is !. The decoded text of a Scalar, with quotes, escapes and block scalar folding already applied. It is empty for every other kind. How a Scalar was written, or whether a collection is Block or Flow. Plain for the other kinds. Whether a DocumentStart came from a --- marker or a DocumentEnd from a ... marker. false for every other kind. The line of the event in the source, counting from 1. The column of the event in the source, counting from 1.
enum EventKind { StreamStart StreamEnd DocumentStart DocumentEnd SequenceStart SequenceEnd MappingStart MappingEnd Scalar Alias }

The kind of an Event. The start of the stream. It is the first event. The end of the stream. It is the last event. The start of a document. Event.explicit says whether a --- marker was written. The end of a document. Event.explicit says whether a ... marker was written. The start of a sequence. Event.style is Block or Flow. The end of a sequence. The start of a mapping. Event.style is Block or Flow. The end of a mapping. A scalar, whose decoded text is in Event.value. A node with no content, such as a key with no value, is a Plain scalar with an empty value. An alias to an anchored node. Event.anchor is the anchor name.
struct Node { pub value: Value pub tag: str pub anchor: str pub style: Style pub line: i64 pub column: i64 }

A node of a composed YAML document. The node's content. The tag as written, resolved as Event.tag is, or the empty string when there is none. The anchor name, or the empty string when the node has none. encode uses it as the preferred name when the node is shared. How the node was written. A node built in code is Plain. The line in the source, counting from 1, or 0 for a node that was built in code. The column in the source, counting from 1, or 0 for a node that was built in code.
struct Options { pub max_nodes: i64 pub max_depth: i64 }

Limits for parsing YAML, to bound the work done on untrusted input. The most nodes a document may expand to, counting an alias as the whole node it refers to; defaults to 1000000. Exceeding it fails with TooManyNodes. The deepest nesting of sequences and mappings accepted; defaults to 512. Exceeding it fails with Syntax.
struct Pair { pub key: *Node pub value: *Node }
A key and value pair of a Map. The key. Mapping keys may be any node, not only scalars. The value.
enum Style { Plain SingleQuoted DoubleQuoted Literal Folded Block Flow }

How a node was written in the source, as recorded in Node.style and Event.style. A scalar is Plain, SingleQuoted, DoubleQuoted, Literal or Folded, and a sequence or mapping is Block or Flow. encode does not use it. A plain scalar, written without quotes. A scalar in single quotes. A scalar in double quotes. A block scalar introduced by |. A block scalar introduced by >. A sequence or mapping written in block style, with indentation. A sequence or mapping written in flow style, with [] or {}.
enum Value { Null Bool(bool) Int(i64) Float(f64) Str(str) Binary([]u8) Seq([]*Node) Map([]Pair) }

A YAML value after the composer has resolved its tag, using the YAML 1.2 core schema. A null: ~, null, Null, NULL or an empty plain scalar, or a scalar tagged !!null. A boolean: true, True, TRUE, false, False or FALSE, or a scalar tagged !!bool. An integer: decimal with an optional sign, 0x hexadecimal or 0o octal. It must fit an i64. A floating point number: decimal with a fraction or exponent, .inf with an optional sign, or .nan, each also as .Inf, .INF, .NaN or .NAN. A scalar tagged !!float that is an integer is read as a float. A string: any other plain scalar, any quoted or block scalar, and any scalar tagged !!str or !. Bytes, from a scalar tagged !!binary, decoded from base64 with whitespace ignored. A sequence of nodes. A mapping, as pairs in the order they were written.
Returns the element of the sequence n at index, or none when n is not a sequence or index is out of range, including a negative index.
Returns the boolean n holds, or none when n is not a Bool.

Returns the node n as YAML text in block style, ending in a newline. A sequence is written as - item lines and a mapping as key: value lines, indented by two spaces per level; an empty sequence is [] and an empty mapping {}. The Style of a node is ignored. A node reachable more than once through the same *Node is written once with an anchor and then as *alias: the anchor is the node's anchor when that is a valid name no other node uses and a1, a2 and so on otherwise. A string is plain when it would read back as the same string, which rules out text that resolves to a null, boolean or number, the YAML 1.1 words such as yes and off, and text that starts or ends with a space or has indicators in a position that matters. Otherwise it is single quoted, or double quoted with escapes when it holds control or other non-printable characters. A string with a line break is a literal | block when that can carry it exactly. A float is written with a . or an exponent, as .nan, .inf or -.inf when not finite. A Binary is written as !!binary and base64. A tag is written unless it is one that the value already implies, such as tag:yaml.org,2002:str. A key that is a collection, contains a line break or is longer than 1000 bytes is written with the ? form. The output is meant to read back to the same value through parse.
Returns the number n holds as a float, or none when n is neither a Float nor an Int. An Int is converted.

Converts the node n into a T through std/serde. A struct is read from a mapping by key: unknown keys are skipped, a missing key takes the field's default or none for an optional, and any other missing key fails with Missing. Mapping keys that are scalars are matched as their text, so 1, true and null match the names "1", "true" and "null". Integers are read from Int, floats from Float or Int, text from Str and a []u8 from a Binary node, which a !!binary scalar gives. An enum variant is a string, or a mapping with one key that names the variant. Fails with serde.Error.Mismatch when a node has another type, with Range for a negative integer read as unsigned, and with UnknownVariant and Missing as serde.read describes. In errors, at is the source line of the node.
Returns the value of the first pair of the mapping n whose key is the string key, or none when n is not a mapping or has no such key.
Returns the integer n holds, or none when n is not an Int.
Returns the string n holds, or none when n is not a Str. Scalars of other types are not converted.
Returns a new node holding v, with no tag, no anchor, Plain style and no source position.
Parses the YAML text source into a T, with default Options. See deserialize_with.
fn deserialize_with[T](source: str, options: Options) -> T ! serde.Error

Parses the YAML text source that holds one document into a T, as options says. Equivalent to parse_with followed by from_node. A Syntax or TooManyNodes error becomes serde.Error.Syntax whose line is the line of the problem and whose message includes the line and column. Other failures are those of from_node.

Returns the nodes documents as a YAML stream, each document starting with a --- line. Each document is written as encode writes it, and anchors are named per document. No documents give the empty string.
Returns the events of the YAML text source, with default Options. See events_with.
fn events_with(source: str, options: Options) -> []Event ! Error

Returns the stream of events for the YAML text source, using options. The events run from StreamStart to StreamEnd and follow the YAML 1.2 grammar, resolving tag handles and %TAG directives but not scalar types: a scalar is always text, whatever it looks like. Aliases are not expanded, and anchors are not checked, so an undefined alias is found only by parse. Fails with Syntax for text that is not valid YAML, and when sequences and mappings nest deeper than options.max_depth. It never fails with TooManyNodes.
Parses the single-document YAML text source into its root node. See parse_with.
Parses the YAML text source that holds any number of documents, returning each document's root node. See parse_all_with.
fn parse_all_with(source: str, options: Options) -> []*Node ! Error

Parses the YAML 1.2 text source into one root node per document, using options. An empty stream gives no documents and an empty document is a Null node. Anchors belong to the document they appear in; an alias cannot refer to an anchor of an earlier document. Otherwise it follows parse_with, and fails with the same errors except for the one about more than one document.
fn parse_with(source: str, options: Options) -> *Node ! Error

Parses the YAML 1.2 text source that holds one document, using options. Scalars are resolved with the core schema, so an unquoted 1, true, 1.5 or ~ is not a string. Quoted and block scalars are always strings, and the tags !!str, !!null, !!bool, !!int, !!float and !!binary convert a scalar or fail. An alias gives the same Node as its anchor, not a copy. Merge keys (<<) are not special. An empty stream is a Null node. Fails with Syntax for invalid YAML, for a duplicate scalar key in one mapping, for a tag that does not suit its node, for an alias to an undefined anchor, and when the stream has more than one document; and with TooManyNodes when options.max_nodes is exceeded.
Returns v as YAML text. Equivalent to to_node followed by encode; fails like to_node.

Converts v into a node tree through std/serde. A struct and a map become a mapping with string keys, a slice a sequence, an enum variant without fields a string and a variant with fields a mapping with one key, the variant's name. A []u8 becomes a Binary node and an optional that is none a Null node. The nodes have no tags or anchors, Plain style and no position. Fails with serde.Error.Range when a u64 is above 9223372036854775807.

> irm https://low.simoncurtis.dev/install.ps1 | iex The scripts install the latest release to ~/.local/bin on Linux, and on Windows to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\low, which the script adds to PATH. Set LOW_INSTALL to choose another directory. low compiles and links programs itself, including the patches of low dev, which needs a Linux host. Build from source A program built for Windows runs the whole language and the standard library modules that only compute. Modules that call the operating system, such as files, processes and sockets, panic.
